title: Only one nation offered Rassie Erasmus support after six-match ban
article_text:
Japan head coach Eddie Jones has emerged as the only rival international boss to offer Rassie Erasmus any real sympathy following his controversial six-match suspension.

The Springboks coach was punished by World Rugby after questioning the officiating during South Africa's 21-19 defeat to France.

Erasmus highlighted a series of alleged illegal tackles before suggesting the failure to penalise them could amount to manipulation of the game.

While several leading coaches have defended match officials or refused to comment, Jones took a different approach.

Writing in his Daily Mail column, the former England boss revealed he had contacted Erasmus personally.

Jones said he believed the South African had legitimate concerns about decisions made during the defeat in Paris.

He even sent Erasmus a private text message expressing his support for those concerns.

However, Jones made clear that his sympathy had limits.

As Sky Sports reported, he believed the Springboks coach had gone too far by raising the possibility of match-fixing.

Jones also questioned whether World Rugby treats every nation equally, suggesting some countries receive preferential treatment.

The comments add another twist to the controversy surrounding Erasmus, whose suspension has already forced him to make alternative plans to watch South Africa face Ireland.

The response from other international coaches has been noticeably different.

England boss Steve Borthwick defended match officials, insisting they deserve respect and expressing complete confidence in their integrity.

France coach Fabien Galthié also stressed the responsibility coaches have to protect referees.

Ireland's Andy Farrell refused to discuss the controversy ahead of Saturday's clash with South Africa.

Scotland boss Gregor Townsend similarly avoided offering an opinion, joking about whether Erasmus was a Japanese player.

All Blacks coach Dave Rennie expressed sympathy for officials dealing with increasingly complicated tackle laws, although he did not directly address Erasmus's suspension.

That leaves Jones as the only rival head coach to have publicly offered meaningful sympathy for Erasmus's complaints.

Erasmus will be absent from the Aviva Stadium when South Africa face Ireland in the Nations Championship.

The suspension also prevents him from attending the finals weekend later this month.

However, the Springboks boss has already announced plans to host a live watchalong from his hotel.

Jones has even suggested he might tune in.

title: ATP Rankings: Alexander Zverev misses opportunity, Carlos Alcaraz closes gap to Jannik Sinner
article_text:
Carlos Alcaraz has finished the 2026 season on a high by winning the final trophy on offer, the ATP Finals, and with it he finds himself right on the heels of Jannik Sinner in the rankings.

The seven-time Grand Slam winner defeated world No 1 Alexander Zverev in the final to win the season-ending event for the first time in his career and with it came a handy 1,500 ranking points as he won the tournament undefeated.

As a result, Alcaraz is now just 350 points behind second-placed Sinner – who missed the tournament due to injury – while Zverev has a comfortable 2,400-point advantage over the Italian.

The Spaniard finished the year with three consecutive titles as he also won the Vienna Open and Paris Masters and, when asked if he feels like the No 1, he replied: “Well, no, not at all.

“What I’m going to say is I think everybody feels he’s the No 1. Me, Sascha, Jannik,[Ben] Shelton, I think everybody thinks they are the No 1 in the world.

“And I think that confidence, it’s really important. Having that confidence in yourself, it’s really important. When you hit the practice court, when you hit the match, it’s really important to have that confidence yourself.

“You know, the No 1 is Sascha. He really deserves it. Nobody’s going to take that position and the No 1 away from him. We have to think about it. We have to say that. Right now, the ranking says it’s Sascha, and we have to give credit to him.”

Despite his emphatic title run in Turin, Alcaraz won’t be able to return to No 1 after next year’s Australian Open – even if he successfully defends his trophy – as he has 2,000 points to defend while Zverev will drop only 800 points.

Zverev would have secured the post-Australian Open No 1 spot had he won the ATP Finals.

However, the German is all but assured of remaining top as Sinner would need to enter and win an ATP 500 event before the season-opening Grand Slam and then go on to win the Melbourne Park tournament.

At this stage, it is not even a given that the Italian will play at the Australian Open due to his knee injury.

Outside of the top three, Shelton is a comfortable fourth as he has a 1,350-point lead over Daniil Medvedev while Arthur Fils finishes at a career-high No 6 as he moved up one spot with his one win at the ATP Finals.

Flavio Cobolli, Frances Tiafoe, Taylor Fritz and Rafael Jodar complete the top 10.

Tennis great Novak Djokovic ends the season at a disappointing 12th – his lowest year-end finish since 2006 – with the China Open his only trophy while he finished runner-up to Alcaraz at the Australian Open.

title: Lakshya Sen On Podium For Third Time With Hong Kong Open 2026 Bronze
article_text:
Lakshya Sen won bronze at the Hong Kong Open 2026 after losing the semifinal to Denmark’s Anders Antonsen, who became men’s singles champion.

Indian ace Lakshya Sen finished on the podium for the third time in the last month. Lakshya ended his Hong Kong Open 2026 campaign with a bronze medal in the men’s singles. Sen’s third-place finish came after losing to Denmark’s Anders Antonsen in the Super 500 semifinals. Anders went on to win the Hong Kong championship after Thailand’s second seed, Kunlavut Vitidsarn, withdrew due to injury concerns. Lakshya, ranked World No. 11 in the latest BWF World Rankings, has already secured his place at the BWF World Tour Finals before the semifinals. The Finals will be held in Hangzhou, China, from 9 to 13 December.

The World No.3 Danish player has also qualified for the World Tour Finals. He is ranked 4th for the Hangzhou Finals. He defeated Sen with 21-13 and 21-13 in both sets, winning the men’s singles semifinals. Sen’s campaign ended with a bronze medal in the Hong Kong Open. The final did not happen at the Super 500 as Kunlavut pulled out due to injury, and Antonsen was declared the winner.

Sen moved to sixth place in the Race to Finals standings after winning back-to-back BWF titles. The 25-year-old won the Hylo Open 2026 men’s singles title in Germany, and two weeks later he won the Kumamoto Masters 2026 in Japan.

In the women’s singles, two-time Asian Champion, China’s Wang Zhiyi defended her title and defeated Thailand’s Pornpawee Chochuwong. Chochuwong beat India’s Rakshitha Ramraj in the quarterfinals. The 19-year-old won against World No.4 in her previous match, making it a memorable outing for her.

Indian shuttlers now turn to the Syed Modi India International in Lucknow from 24 to 29 November.

title: Lakshya Sen and PV Sindhu Qualify for BWF World Tour Finals 2026, India Set for Two-Pronged Challenge in Hangzhou
article_text:
India will have two representatives at the 2026 BWF World Tour Finals, with Lakshya Sen and PV Sindhu securing qualification for the prestigious season-ending tournament scheduled to take place in Hangzhou, China, from December 9 to 13.

Sen will compete in men’s singles, while Sindhu has booked her place in women’s singles. Their qualification marks an important moment for Indian badminton, with both players returning to the year-end championship for the first time since 2021.

The two berths also reflect contrasting but equally encouraging stories. Sen secured his place through a strong finish to the season, winning consecutive Super 500 titles in Germany and Japan. Sindhu, meanwhile, has rebuilt her form following an injury-disrupted period, returning to the world’s top six and producing some of her most consistent badminton in recent seasons.

With eight players competing in each singles discipline, the World Tour Finals bring together the season’s most successful performers for one final test.

For Lakshya Sen, qualification represents a significant turnaround after an inconsistent middle phase of the season.

The Indian began 2026 with an impressive run at the All England Open, reaching the final after defeating established opponents, including Shi Yuqi and Victor Lai. He eventually finished runner-up to Taiwan’s Lin Chun-yi.

However, a series of early exits at major tournaments and a shoulder injury disrupted his campaign. His withdrawal from the French Open in October further complicated his qualification prospects.

Sen responded with an outstanding finish, winning the Hylo Open in Germany before claiming the Kumamoto Masters Japan title. At the Hylo Open, he defeated Indonesia’s Jonatan Christie 21–17, 21–10 in the final, becoming the first Indian to win the tournament twice. In Japan, he continued his momentum by defeating Koki Watanabe in the title match.

The back-to-back titles transformed his position in the HSBC Race to Finals standings.

Sen entered the Hong Kong Open as the sixth-ranked player in the Race to Finals, holding 74,180 points. His qualification was subsequently confirmed after compatriot Kidambi Srikanth defeated Japan’s Koki Watanabe, one of the players challenging for the final qualification positions.

Sen continued his Hong Kong campaign, reaching the semifinals before losing to Denmark’s Anders Antonsen.

The 25-year-old will now return to the World Tour Finals after making his debut in 2021, when he reached the semifinals. His recent performances suggest that he will arrive in Hangzhou with considerable confidence.

The men's singles field is particularly competitive, featuring defending champion Christo Popov, Indonesia’s Alwi Farhan, Canada’s Victor Lai, Antonsen, Chou Tien-chen and Thailand’s Kunlavut Vitidsarn. Reigning World Champion Alex Lanier also qualifies through the automatic exemption.

Sindhu’s qualification is another major positive for Indian badminton.

The two-time Olympic medallist has worked her way back into the elite group after an injury-affected period that interrupted her progress. Her 2026 season has been built around consistency, with 10 quarterfinal appearances, two titles and a return to World No. 6.

Her most significant victories came at the Japan Open Super 750 and Hylo Open Super 500. At the Japan Open, Sindhu defeated Japan’s Akane Yamaguchi 21–17, 21–17 in the final to claim an important title.

She also demonstrated her ability to challenge the very best by taking world No. 1 An Se-young to three games in the French Open final, eventually losing 21–16, 11–21, 12–21.

Sindhu’s return to the World Tour Finals carries additional significance. She remains the only Indian player to have won the women’s singles title, having lifted the trophy in 2018 in Guangzhou.

Ranked fifth in the Race to Finals, she will enter the Hangzhou competition with the experience of having competed against the world's leading players for more than a decade.

The women's singles field will be led by South Korea’s An Se-young, who has enjoyed a remarkable 2026 season. The defending champion and reigning World Champion has dominated the circuit, making her the leading contender for another title.

China’s Wang Zhiyi and Chen Yufei, Japan’s Akane Yamaguchi and Tomoka Miyazaki, and Thailand’s Ratchanok Intanon and Pornpawee Chochuwong will add further depth to the competition.

While India’s singles representation is encouraging, the country will have no entries in the three doubles disciplines.

The biggest disappointment is the absence of Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty. The former world No. 1 pair won two Super 750 titles during 2026, at the Singapore Open and China Masters, but finished outside the qualification positions after competing in a reduced tournament schedule.

Their workload management and commitments to national team events affected their Race to Finals ranking.

India’s women’s doubles pair Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand, despite winning a bronze medal at the 2026 World Championships, also missed qualification.

The 2026 World Tour Finals will feature eight qualifiers in each discipline, divided into two groups of four. The group stage will be followed by semifinals and finals, with the championship concluding on December 13.

The tournament carries total prize money of USD 3.5 million, underlining its status as one of the most prestigious events on the badminton calendar.

For India, the challenge will rest on Sen’s late-season momentum and Sindhu’s experience at the highest level. Both have already demonstrated that they can compete with the world’s best.

The next step is to convert that form into a strong finish in Hangzhou. With two singles players back among the season’s elite, Indian badminton will have another opportunity to end 2026 on a high.

title: Gauff, Townsend Clinch USA BJK Cup Victory over Hungary
article_text:
Coco Gauff created a happy homecoming weekend in Delray Beach.

Delray Beach native Coco Gauff and Taylor Townsend clinched Billie Jean King Cup Qualifying victory for the U.S. on Sunday, defeating Hungarian doubles pair Anna Bondar and Dalma Galfi 6-4, 6-3 at the Delray Beach Tennis Center.

Ashlyn Krueger, ranked No. 41 in the world, capped the tie with a 6-2, 6-1, dead singles win over Adrienn Nagy, giving captain Lindsay Davenport a clean sweep in the tie.

“I think there was always this scenario that we would probably be up 2-0. Once that was the scenario, I was, like, of course, I’m going to play and try to just finish it 3-0,” Gauff said. “Yeah, I think we were both prepared to play with each other. We didn’t know what the end of Day 1 results would

have looked like. Maybe if it was 1-All, maybe I would have not played, because I would have had to play singles

30 minutes later. But, you know, it’s always that risk.

“I feel like Taylor and Lindsay were confident in my ability to play in doubles and potentially have to play singles after, but I’m really happy that they trusted me to step in and make the change. But, yeah, I’m really happy that I got to play with Taylor today.”

The U.S. joins seven nations advancing out of the Playoffs to the 2027 Qualifiers. The Qualifiers will be played in April, with the specific dates and ties to be announced.

title: Badminton: Pearly-Thinaah savour booster ahead of tough test at World Tour Finals
article_text:
PETALING JAYA: National women’s doubles aces Pearly Tan-M. Thinaah could not have picked a better time to rediscover their form and rhythm.

The world No. 4 pair reclaimed the Hong Kong Open crown yesterday, defeating Japan’s Sumire Nakade-Miyu Takahashi 22-20, 21-16 in 40 minutes at the Kai Tak Arena.

Winning the crown without dropping a game puts them in good stead ahead of next month’s season-ending World Tour Finals.

“It’s definitely a confidence boost for the World Tour Finals,” said Thinaah.

It was sweet revenge for the 2024 champions, who lost to the Japanese pair in the Taipei Open final in August.

The victory brought them their third title of the year and second in five weeks, following triumphs at the Indonesia Masters in January and Denmark Open last month.

Their unbeaten run in Hong Kong marked a welcome turnaround after a disappointing first-round exit at last week’s Japan Masters.

“This week, we really wanted to put last week behind us, come in fresh and be more focused.”

A heart-to-heart talk helped them regroup, with Pearly taking satisfaction in how they handled difficult situations and managed their emotions throughout the week.

That composure showed in the final when they saved a game point at 19-20 despite Pearly breaking her racquet.

They then pulled away from 14-14 in the second game to seal the title.

“There were still ups and downs in the first few matches, but the way we managed them was really positive,” said Thinaah.

“There was also a lot of communication between us, which really helped throughout the week.”

A sterner examination awaits at the Finals in Hangzhou from Dec 9-13, with China’s Liu Shengshu-Tan Ning, world champions Baek Ha-na-Lee So-hee of South Korea and Japan’s Yuki Fukushima-Mayu Matsumoto among the qualified contenders.

Fukushima-Matsumoto ended the Malaysians’ breakthrough semi-final run last year.

Pearly-Thinaah had previously exited at the group stage in 2021, 2022 and 2024, while missing qualification in 2023.

“We want to go back and focus on the next two weeks. There are still many things we need to work on.”

“These will be two crucial weeks for both of us – learning, supporting each other and handling our emotions. We’re really excited for the World Tour Finals,” added Thinaah.

title: ATP Finals: Carlos Alcaraz beats world number one Alexander Zverev to claim title
article_text:
Carlos Alcaraz outplayed world number one Alexander Zverev to end his wait for a first ATP Finals title and complete a remarkable post-injury return to the sport.

A season which began with Alcaraz becoming the youngest man to complete the career Grand Slam, before he was ruled out for more than four months with a wrist issue, ended with the Spaniard holding aloft another of the sport's biggest trophies.

Alcaraz, still wearing heavy strapping around his upper-left leg following his injury scare earlier in the week, collapsed to the ground in celebration after sealing a 6-2 7-6 (9-7) win in a dramatic second-set tie-break.

It was a statement victory over Zverev, who took advantage of Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner's injury absences to rise to the top of the rankings and claim his first two major titles.

It was a 14th successive win and a third-straight title triumph for seven-time major winner Alcaraz, who demonstrated beyond any doubt that he is back to his devastating best.

"Lifting this trophy is something I have been chasing for a really long time, it means the world to me," the 23-year-old said.

"I have been through really difficult moments with myself, with my team. For me it's been an amazing week.

"I couldn't finish the week in a better way."

It is just 84 days since Alcaraz made his return at the US Open in August after a lengthy spell on the sidelines.

Since that tournament, the current world number three has won 21 of his 22 matches and swept titles at four of the five tournaments he has entered.

With his latest victory, Alcaraz has become the youngest man to win all four Grand Slams and the season-ending Finals - and only the fourth in history.

Zverev, who ends 2026 with an ATP Tour-leading 69 match victories, had not dropped serve in four straight-set matches to reach the final.

But for much of the two-hour title decider, his greatest weapon was dismantled by a brilliant Alcaraz.

Alcaraz handled the occasion far better as he emerged from a tense start with a 4-1 double-break lead on his way to the first set.

The contrasting emotions of the two players were evident when Alcaraz wore a big grin after pulling off a between-the-legs lob that Zverev smashed into the net. At the other end of the court, the German threw away his racquet in disgust.

While Alcaraz danced to music during a change of ends, Zverev's frustrations only grew as, after winning back one of the two breaks of serve, he received a second time violation on his way to losing serve for a third successive game.

The top seed left the court after unravelling in the first set, having produced just three winners to 19 unforced errors in an inconsistent start.

Alcaraz's march to the title appeared inevitable as he took control of the second set with a fourth break of serve, but Zverev restored parity in the eighth game and kept his hopes alive by forcing a tie-break.

Overturning a 3-0 deficit in the tie-break, Zverev then won six straight points to arrive at three set points.

However, he failed to take all of them, including one on his own serve, before Alcaraz drove in a backhand winner on his second match point.

After picking himself off the floor, the Spaniard celebrated with his team in the stands after finally landing the title he had been chasing for four years.

In the doubles, French debutants Theo Arribage and Albano Olivetti lifted the trophy after a comeback victory against Marcelo Arevalo and Mate Pavic.

The sixth seeds recovered from losing the first set to win 3-6 7-6 (7-2) 10-6, ending the year with the most wins (59) and titles (seven) in men's doubles.

title: Carlos Alcaraz and Alexander Zverev’s ATP Finals prize money & ranking points revealed
article_text:
Carlos Alcaraz is the 2026 ATP Finals champion, defeating Alexander Zverev in Sunday’s final to triumph in Turin.

The final pitted two reigning Grand Slam champions against each other, with French Open and US Open champion Zverev, the world No 1, up against world No 3 and Australian Open winner Alcaraz.

Alcaraz was gunning for the first ATP Finals title of his career, having lost in the 2025 final, while Zverev was looking to win the title for the third time after previous triumphs in 2018 and 2021.

And, it was the Spaniard who triumphed inside the Inalpi Arena on Sunday, battling past a resilient Zverev claim a 6-2, 7-6(7) victory in the championship match.

With the tournament now over, we look at the ranking points and prize money that both men will take home from the tournament.

Want more from Tennis365? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for tennis coverage you can trust.

What ranking points did Zverev and Alcaraz win in Turin?

Significant ranking points were on off in Turin this year, with 200 points per round-robin victory and 1,500 points guaranteed for any unbeaten champion at the ATP Finals.

With both Alcaraz and Zverev unbeaten on their way to the final, 1,500 points was therefore guaranteed for the champion.

It was Alcaraz who claimed that full 1,500 points thanks to his victory, which includes a full 500 points alone for winning Sunday’s final against the German.

That means he finishes the year as the world No 3 on 7,600 points, just 350 points behind leading rival and world No 2 Jannik Sinner in the ATP Rankings.

Meanwhile, runner-up Zverev takes home 1,000 ranking points for finishing as the runner-up. He ends the season on 10,350 points in the ATP Rankings, comfortably sealing the year-end No 1 position for the first time in his career.

What prize money did Zverev and Alcaraz win in Turin?

With neither of the two losing a match up until the final, both had already banked significant prize money winnings ahead of Sunday’s showpiece match.

Both men received a participant fee of $338,000 for their event qualification, $405,000 per round-robin win, and $1,206,000 for their respective victories in Saturday’s semi-finals.

Meanwhile, for his runner-up finish, Zverev claims a not-insignificant $2,759,000 after an impressive showing at the final ATP Tour event of 2026.

title: Jannik Sinner OUT of the Australian Open? Alarming report suggests an extended lay-off
article_text:
Jannik Sinner was forced to abort the second half of the 2026 season due to a knee injury and the latest reports suggest he may also be out of action of a large part of next year.

Sinner has not struck a ball in anger since winning the Wimbledon final against Alexander Zverev in July, with the Italian ruled out with a knee problem that has proved to be more serious than initially feared.

His absence allowed Zverev to take over as world No 1, with his hopes of getting back on court now in doubt again after a report in Italian publication Gazzetta dello Sport suggesting the problems are far from over for Sinner.

The report suggests Sinner has been consulting with Finnish surgeon Lasse Lempainen and he may now be forced to undergo surgery to resolve the problem.

“There are various procedures that could be applied to Sinner,” reports Federica Cocchi.

“These range from entering the knee to check the condition of the external meniscus and possibly cleaning it, to what’s called a “Z-plasty,” which involves a small incision, as if a very tight rope were cut to release the tension.

“This procedure may also involve removing the underlying bursa, which may have accumulated fluid.

“The third option is certainly the riskiest: operating on the knee bone if it’s believed to be impinging on the bone.

“While this could be a curative measure, the downside is that the bone, in reaction, could form an even larger callus, further worsening the inflammation of the band. In short, if surgery is necessary, it’s best to make the decision quickly to avoid wasting any more precious time.

“Obviously, if Lempainen is required, returning to Australia would not be possible, but depending on the type of surgery, recovery and return to action times could vary, at least three months.”

The initial vibes coming from the Sinner camp was that his absence from the game would be brief when he confirmed he would miss the Canadian Masters in August, but the knee problem has ended up being significant.

There are strong suggestions in the report that Sinner may now try and target a return in the European clay court season in April, with his extended absence a huge blow if it is confirmed.

It would also mean he misses out on a huge pay-day, as he is guaranteed $1.5million just for appearing at the Six Kings Slam exhibition event in Saudi Arabia next month.

Sinner has yet to make any public comment on his, but he did suggest in a recent video on his YouTube channel that he was ‘a long way’ from getting back on court.

Realistically, Sinner would need to be back on court and practicing in late December to have a realistic chance of being fit for the Australian Open in mid-January, but that comeback date may look ambitious given the latest update from the respected course in Italy.

title: Nitto ATP Finals 2026 Prize Money Breakdown- How Much Will Carlos Alcaraz & Alexander Zverev Earn?
article_text:
Winning the ATP Finals trophy could earn one player $5.17 million, but even falling short of the championship does not mean walking away with a small payday. At the 2026 edition in Turin, a player who wins all three group-stage matches and reaches the semifinals is guaranteed $1.553 million, even if their title hopes end there.

With every victory carrying a separate financial reward, the season-ending tournament offers one of the most lucrative opportunities in men's tennis.

The 2026 Nitto ATP Finals, held from November 15 to 22 at the Inalpi Arena in Turin, Italy, features a record $15.75 million prize pool across singles and doubles.

The undefeated singles champion can collect $5,171,000, while the winning doubles team can split $959,300. But what makes this year's prize money particularly interesting is not just the record total; it is how much each match is worth and how the payouts compare with last season.

How Much Does the ATP Finals Singles Champion Earn?

The maximum singles payout is reserved for a player who completes an undefeated campaign. This requires three round-robin victories, a semifinal win, and a victory in the championship match.

The participation fee is adjusted according to the number of group matches a player completes. An alternate who does not enter the competition receives $156,000.

This structure means that a player who wins all three group matches earns $1.553 million before the semifinals. Even if that player loses in the last four, the amount already earned remains theirs.

The doubles competition also offers a substantial financial reward, although the figures are paid per team rather than per individual player.

An undefeated doubles champion pair can earn $959,300. The breakdown includes a $134,200 participation fee for completing all three group matches, $96,600 for each round-robin victory, $178,500 for winning the semifinal and $356,800 for taking the final.

An alternate doubles team receives $51,700.

Alcaraz and Zverev Guaranteed $2.75 Million, With $5.17 Million at Stake in Final

Both finalists have already secured a substantial payday after completing an unbeaten round-robin campaign and winning their respective semifinals.

Since each has won all four matches played so far, Alcaraz and Zverev are guaranteed at least $2,759,000 each, regardless of Sunday's result. This includes the $338,000 participation fee, $1.215 million from their three group-stage victories and the $1.206 million semifinal-winning bonus.

However, the winner will receive an additional $2.412 million for claiming the championship. That would take the total earnings to $5,171,000, making either player the highest-paid singles competitor at this year's tournament.

The runner-up will finish with $2,759,000. Both finalists are also competing for the maximum 1,500 ATP ranking points available at the event.

What Is Different About the Prize Money This Year?

The biggest change in 2026 is the tournament's record-breaking overall purse. The total prize money has increased to $15.75 million, compared with $15.5 million in 2025 (a rise of $250,000).

The maximum singles champion's payout has also increased from $5.071 million in 2025 to $5.171 million this year. That is an additional $100,000 for an undefeated champion.

The doubles payout, however, has remained unchanged from the previous edition. The undefeated winning team will again share $959,300.

There is another major incentive beyond the financial rewards: ATP ranking points. Players receive 200 points for each round-robin victory, 400 for a semifinal win and 500 for winning the final.

An undefeated singles champion can therefore collect a maximum of 1,500 ranking points. Unlike most ATP Tour tournaments, the ATP Finals does not award ranking points simply for participating.

With a record prize pool, valuable ranking points and the distinction of finishing the season as champion, the Turin tournament remains one of the most lucrative prizes in men's tennis.

title: Daniil Medvedev downplays Alexander Zverev’s improvement after ATP Finals defeat
article_text:
Alexander Zverev is one win away from completing his perfect season after he stormed into the championship match at the ATP Finals with a win against Daniil Medvedev.

Zverev recorded his 69th win of a year that has seen him win his first two Grand Slam titles at the Roland Garros and the US Open, with his 7-6(0), 6-4 win over Medvedev in Turin giving him a shot at Carlos Alcaraz in the final.

The newly crowned world No 1 has been frustrated by constant suggestions that he has only claimed the world No 1 ranking due to long-term injuries afflicting Jannik Sinner and Alcaraz.

Medvedev had a 14-8 winning record against Zverev prior to their latest meeting, so he is perfectly placed to give a verdict on whether the German has raised his level over the last year.

Zverev did not face a break point in the two sets against Medvedev, with his opponent suggesting his biggest weapon will always be his serve.

“I think his serve is better,” declared Medvedev, before he was asked if Zverev’s forehand has also gone up a level and he replied: “I will put it this way: I think his forehand was very good even before, and then sometimes he can miss. Today he also missed a couple, so I would not say it’s better.

“I said even before the match, serve is important. Actually, probably Sascha didn’t get broken yet this tournament, so not easy. Didn’t get a break point, so of course not that easy.

“On the tiebreak, I had to do a bit better if I wanted to win the set, and same on the second set when I got broken. Could have done maybe a little bit better. But deserved to lose, so we move on.”

Zverev will be desperate to record a win against Alcaraz and banish the notion that he is a step behind what some have claimed are the real ‘Big 2’ in men’s tennis, with former world No 1 Jim Courier among those admitting outside factors will always cloud some judgements on the German.

Back in June 2024, criminal proceedings against Zverev over allegations he pushed and strangled his ex-girlfriend, Brenda Patea, were discontinued by a Berlin court following a settlement.

Zverev denied the accusations, and court proceedings ended without a verdict or a finding of guilt. Under the agreement, Zverev was ordered to pay €150,000 to the German state and a further €50,000 to charitable organisations.

In an interview with L’Equipe after his Roland Garros victory in June, Zverev said the allegations against him “have been proven false” and that his “innocence has been proven”.

According to Bounces, Patea has filed a new civil lawsuit against Zverev over alleged ‘false statements’ made in that L’Equipe interview, with Courier arguing those allegations will always haunt Zverev.

Want more from Tennis365? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for tennis coverage you can trust.

“Well, the computer is the computer. It doesn’t have any feelings. It just spits out the numbers on who did what,” he said on a recent episode of the Off Court with Greg Rusedski podcast as he spoke about the debate over Zverev’s rise to the world No 1 ranking.

“He’s the most accomplished tennis player this year. He’s got the most points in the last 52 weeks and there he’s the 30th person to have that honour. So yes, he’s earned it. And anyone who doesn’t think that it is just not using their analytical or critical mind. They’re using their emotions.

“And people have strong feelings about Zverev because of all the on-court issues, off-court issues that he’s dealt with over his career that has made it a little more complicated, I think, for some people to to watch his career.

“If you just look at his performance, two major titles, he’s been ultra consistent, and he is the world number one. And I don’t think it’s disputable that the computer is what it is and the ranking is what it is.”

title: Badminton: Wang Zhiyi sets sights on An Seyoung after ending eight-month title wait with Hong Kong Open triumph
Hong Kong Open: Man/Tee Erase 27-Year Blip
article_text:
Man Wei Chong and Tee Kai Wun ended Malaysia’s 27-year wait for a men’s doubles crown at LI-NING Hong Kong Open 2026 on Sunday, delivering a composed 21-19 21-18 victory over Asian Games champions Daniel Marthin and Leo Rolly Carnando.

In doing so, the pair became the first Malaysians to capture the category since legends Cheah Soon Kit and Yap Kim Hock in 1999.

“I’m very grateful to make this history. It’s an honour to follow in the footsteps of greats,” said Man.

“Today is a good story but we already want to focus on next year. We don’t want to think we are champions and then slow down because next year is an important year for us. So we want to fight even harder.”

Against a pair renowned for explosive power, Man and Tee executed a disciplined tactical blueprint to neutralise the Indonesian threat from the outset.

“Everybody knows Daniel’s smash is crazy so we just didn’t want to make it easy for him to use this weapon,” explained Tee. “We had to push them to put them under pressure a little bit and we did that quite well. I made enough room for Man to kill.”

Man credited his partner’s court command for allowing him to dominate the forecourt.

“He controlled the match pretty well, so I got more opportunities in front of the net and more chances to attack.”

While a mid-season knee injury to Man left the duo short of the points required to qualify for next month’s HSBC BWF World Tour Finals, triumphs at last month’s French Open and now in Hong Kong ensure they close their 2026 campaign with formidable momentum.

Meanwhile, Wang Zhi Yi snapped an eight-month title drought in emphatic fashion, cruising past Pornpawee Chochuwong 21-16 21-11 in the women’s singles final.

The victory marks Wang’s first trophy since March – when she stunned the standout An Se Young to claim the All England title – and provides an ideal confidence boost before she heads home to Hangzhou for the World Tour Finals.

“I feel so proud of myself. Today I tried to stay focused and follow my game plan. I’m happy almost like when I won in March,” said Wang.

“It’s a process to always try to keep improving myself. This title means a lot to me. It gives me a lot of confidence to continue my work.”

title: Hong Kong Open — Antonsen declared men’s singles winner after walkover; Zhiyi defends women’s crown
article_text:
Anders Antonsen was declared the men’s singles champion at the Hong Kong Open 2026 after second seed Kunlavut Vitidsarn withdrew from the summit clash with an injury.

“Men’s singles second seed Kunlavut Vitidsarn has withdrawn from his LI-NING Hong Kong Open 2026 final match due to a back injury. His opponent Anders Antonsen will be awarded the title during the prize presentation ceremony,” BWF said in a statement on Sunday.

Antonsen had booked his spot in the final with a commanding 21-13, 21-13 win over India’s Lakshya Sen, while Vitidsarn had gotten the better of Indonesia’s Moh. Zaki Ubaidillah 18-21, 21-15, 21-16 in a 72-minute semifinal battle.

The title in Hong Kong was Antonsen’s second BWF 500 title of the year, having clinched the Thailand Open in May. His opponent in the final then was also Vitidsarn, but the Dane had won the clash in the third game.

In the women’s singles final, two-time Asian Champion Wang Zhiyi defended her title with a dominant win over Pornpawee Chochuwong. Zhiyi took the first game 21-16 before sealing the contest 21-11 in the second game in just 40 minutes.

In the men’ doubles, the Malaysian pair of Man Wei Chong and Tee Kai Wun, who had beaten India’s Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty, went on to beat Indonesia’s Leo Rolly-Daniel Marthin in a tense final.

Wei Chong and Kai Wun won the first game 21-19, with neither pair looking to give away easy points. In the second game, the Malaysian duo pulled away to 16-9 and survived a late surge to seal the contest 21-18.

title: Kunlavut withdraws from Hong Kong Open final with back injury
article_text:
HONG KONG — 22 November 2026, Thailand’s world No. 2 men’s singles badminton player Kunlavut Vitidsarn withdrew from the Hong Kong Open 2026 final due to a back injury, handing the championship title to Denmark’s Anders Antonsen.

The Badminton World Federation (BWF) confirmed the withdrawal on its official Facebook page ahead of Sunday’s scheduled men’s singles final.

Kunlavut, nicknamed “View”, had been due to face Antonsen, the world No. 3, in the championship match.

However, the Thai shuttler was unable to compete because of a back injury, resulting in Antonsen being awarded the title without playing the final.

Kunlavut finished as runner-up at the BWF World Tour Super 500 tournament.

Further details about the severity of his injury and his expected return to competition were not provided in the report.

title: Wei Chong-Kai Wun sign off season in style with Hong Kong Open glory [WATCH]
article_text:
KUALA LUMPUR: Man Wei Chong-Tee Kai Wun signed off the season in style by winning their second World Tour men's doubles title at the Hong Kong Open on Sunday.

The Malaysian world No. 9 pair secured a 21-19, 21-18 win over Asian Games champions Leo Rolly Carnando-Daniel Marthin of Indonesia in the Super 500 final at Kai Tak Arena.

It was the French Open champions' second victory in three meetings against world No. 18 Leo Rolly-Daniel.

Wei Chong-Kai Wun's eighth World Tour title earned them US$39,500 (RM162,500), while Leo Rolly-Daniel had to settle for US$19,000 (RM78,200).

Meanwhile, Malaysia are on course for a double triumph as world No. 4 Pearly Tan-M. Thinaah take on Japan's world No. 11 pair Sumire Nakade-Miyu Takahashi in the women's doubles final later on Sunday.

title: BWF World Tour Finals 2026: P.V. Sindhu Returns, An Se-young Chases Historic 12th Title in Hangzhou
article_text:
The women's singles competition at the 2026 HSBC BWF World Tour Finals promises a fascinating conclusion to the badminton season, bringing together eight of the world's leading players in Hangzhou from December 9 to 13.

Headlined by an extraordinary An Se-young campaign and the return of India's P.V. Sindhu to the season-ending championships, the tournament will combine established champions, emerging talent and several compelling rivalries.

Thailand's Ratchanok Intanon and Pornpawee Chochuwong secured the final two qualification places following their performances at the Hong Kong Open, completing an eight-player field that also includes Akane Yamaguchi, An Se-young, Wang Zhiyi, Chen Yufei, Sindhu and Japan's Tomoka Miyazaki.

The tournament will be staged at the Hangzhou Olympic Sports Centre Gymnasium, marking the final edition of Hangzhou's four-year hosting agreement covering 2023–2026. With a reported total prize pool of US$3.5 million, the 2026 edition is also set to be the richest World Tour Finals in the competition's history.

South Korea's An Se-young has produced one of the most dominant seasons in modern badminton. The world number one enters Hangzhou with 11 titles in 2026, a 71–1 win-loss record and a remarkable 55-match winning streak.

Her achievements include titles at the Malaysia Open, India Open, Badminton Asia Championships, Singapore Open, Indonesia Open, BWF World Championships, China Masters, Asian Games, Denmark Open, French Open and Korea Open.

She also successfully defended her World Tour Finals title in 2025. Having won the season-ending championship in both 2021 and 2025, An will be targeting another title in Hangzhou and an unprecedented 12th tournament victory of the calendar year.

Her biggest challengers are likely to be China's Wang Zhiyi and Japan's Akane Yamaguchi. An's only completed defeat against a player in the 2026 Hangzhou field came against Wang, who beat her in the All England Open final. That result makes the Chinese shuttler particularly interesting in the title conversation.

Akane Yamaguchi is projected to enter as the top seed, although the official seedings remain subject to the BWF's final Race to Finals standings.

The Japanese star has enjoyed a highly consistent season, winning four World Tour titles, including the China Open Super 1000 and Kumamoto Masters Super 500. She also reached 11 individual finals across the season, demonstrating remarkable durability.

However, her record against An Se-young presents a major challenge. An has won all eight of their meetings in 2026, extending a significant winning advantage over her Japanese rival. Yamaguchi's ability to manage her physical condition will also be important after a demanding season. She will need to rediscover the form that made her one of the most consistent players on the circuit if she hopes to challenge for the title.

Wang Zhiyi, meanwhile, has strong reasons to believe she can make another deep run. The 2024 champion and 2025 runner-up has been one of China's most reliable performers and enters with the confidence of having defeated An this season.

For Indian badminton, P.V. Sindhu's qualification is among the major stories of the women's singles competition. The 2018 World Tour Finals champion returns to the season-ending tournament after a period disrupted by injuries. Her 2026 season has marked a significant resurgence, with titles at the Japan Open Super 750 and Hylo Open Super 500.

At the Japan Open, Sindhu defeated Yamaguchi 21–17, 21–17 in the final, demonstrating that she remains capable of beating the world's best. She also reached the French Open final, taking the opening game against An before eventually losing in three games.

Now 31, Sindhu will bring valuable experience and big-match temperament to Hangzhou. Her attacking game, particularly her powerful downward smash, gives her the ability to trouble leading opponents. The challenge will be maintaining that attacking quality while limiting errors over longer rallies.

With several leading contenders expected to be among the seeds, Sindhu could become a dangerous unseeded opponent in the group stage.

Thailand's Ratchanok Intanon will make a record 11th appearance at the World Tour Finals. The 2013 world champion secured qualification after defeating Michelle Li at the Hong Kong Open. Her season included a Malaysia Masters title, and her deceptive shot-making continues to make her a difficult opponent.

Pornpawee Chochuwong also enters in impressive form. After securing qualification with a quarter-final victory over India's Rakshitha Sree Santhosh Ramraj, she reached the Hong Kong Open final. Her World Championships bronze medal and Australian Open runner-up finish underline her credentials.

Japan's Tomoka Miyazaki is the youngest player in the field. The 20-year-old has built her qualification campaign through consistent performances, including a China Masters final and several semifinal appearances. Her challenge will be converting that consistency into victories against the established elite.

China's Chen Yufei completes the projected top four. The Tokyo Olympic champion has the quality to challenge anyone, but recent injury concerns and her early Hong Kong Open exit make her fitness an important factor heading into December.

The eight players will be divided into two groups of four, with the group-stage draw scheduled for December 5. Each player will contest three round-robin matches, with the top two from each group progressing to the semifinals.

The absence of country protection in the World Tour Finals group draw means players from the same nation can meet in the opening phase. This could create particularly interesting matchups involving the Chinese and Thai qualifiers.

The champion will receive 14,000 ranking points, while the runner-up earns 12,000. The projected women's singles winner's share of the prize money is US$280,000, based on the previous year's BWF distribution percentages.

title: Herry unperturbed as BAM men's doubles pairs miss WTF
article_text:
KUALA LUMPUR: Herry Iman Pierngadi is unperturbed that none of the BA Malaysia's (BAM) men's doubles pairs qualified for the World Tour Finals (WTF) as he believes results take precedence over the lucrative event.

Independent men's doubles world No. 5 pair Goh Sze Fei-Nur Izzuddin Rumsani and women's doubles world No. 4 pair Pearly Tan-M. Thinaah, who both topped the World Tour rankings, qualified for the US$3.5 million (RM12.34 million) WTF event in Hangzhou, China, from Dec 9-13, where eight players and pairs will battle for honours.

The reshuffle exercise undertaken by national men's doubles head coach Herry since July was a key reason BAM pairs, led by world No. 4 Aaron Chia-Soh Wooi Yik, were unable to make the cut, as players were tested with different partners.

Although Aaron-Wooi Yik were in contention, their withdrawal from the Hong Kong Open this week due to injuries put paid to their chances.

However, Herry was pleased that the players had shown marked improvement since the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games, with BAM pairs claiming three titles.

"The results in tournaments are more important than qualifying for the WTF. So far, I see a lot of progress in the players' performances and results," said Herry.

Malaysians have been making their mark on the World Tour, with new pair Aaron Tai-Yap Roy King winning the Arctic Open and Kumamoto Masters, both Super 500 events, while Wei Chong-Kai Wun captured the Super 750 French Open.

The progress of Aaron Tai-Roy King has been impressive.

The duo, who have played just six tournaments, are currently ranked world No. 38 and should break into the top 35 in the new world rankings released by the Badminton World Federation (BWF) on Tuesday.

Last year, Malaysia had five representatives at the WTF. They were Aaron-Wooi Yik, Wei Chong-Kai Wun, Pearly-Thinaah and mixed doubles combinations Chen Tang Jie-Toh Ee Wei and Goh Soon Huat-Shevon Lai.

Pearly-Thinaah and Tang Jie-Ee Wei managed to survive the group stage but bowed out in the semi-finals.

Despite the absence of BAM's men's doubles pairs this time, the form of Sze Fei-Izzuddin and Pearly-Thinaah suggests they could feature in the top four in Hangzhou.

title: Alcaraz to face Zverev in ATP Finals title decider
article_text:
Carlos Alcaraz will face world number one Alexander Zverev for the ATP Finals title after completing a superb comeback victory against Ben Shelton.

The indomitable Spaniard recovered from a flat start to outlast Shelton 3-6 6-3 7-6 (7-1) and secure a return to the showpiece, 12 months after losing to Jannik Sinner.

Alcaraz again competed with strapping around his upper-left leg having injured his hamstring earlier this week, but produced his best tennis when it mattered most.

The seven-time major winner, on a 13-match winning streak, will face Zverev in Sunday's final after the German beat Daniil Medvedev 7-6 (7-0) 6-4.

Asked how he was feeling physically, with little over 24 hours to recover for that match, Alcaraz said: "Today was a really important test. I think it went great.

"I'm probably not pushing myself to the limit. I'm realising that I need to be careful with it and sometimes I don't have to push myself to the limit, I don't have to run for every ball."

Alcaraz, bidding for his first triumph at the season-ending tournament, leads the overall head-to-head against two-time champion Zverev 7-6.

But the 23-year-old has dominated their recent meetings - winning four of the past five, including a five-set epic on his way to this year's Australian Open title.

Zverev said: "Carlos, for sure, the way he's been playing since his comeback, has been one of the best players in the world. Maybe the best player in the world.

"I look forward to tomorrow. I look forward to playing a tough match."

Alcaraz is through to his seventh final of 2026, a total unmatched by any men's singles player despite his four-month absence with a wrist injury.

The 23-year-old has been in scintillating form since his return to action at the US Open, which concluded in a quarter-final epic against Shelton in September.

He has now won 20 of his past 21 matches, sweeping back-to-back titles at the Vienna Open and Paris Masters prior to this tournament - including taking revenge on Shelton to triumph at the latter.

"I think this rivalry is just getting better and better. It's going to be a great match-up in the future," the third-ranked Alcaraz said after another close match against the world number four.

"Every time we face each other, it's a great battle. It is one of those matches that makes me be a better player and gives me a lot of feedback about what I have to improve."

Victory over Alcaraz in New York marked the biggest win of the 24-year-old Shelton's career, and a repeat of that result appeared within his grasp.

While the hamstring injury Alcaraz sustained earlier this week did not prevent him winning every set in a perfect group campaign, the Australian Open winner was second-best in a subdued start.

Shelton capitalised by blasting in a return to clinch his first break point in Alcaraz's opening service game, before withstanding two break points at 4-2 as he saw out a deserved first set.

Alcaraz's frustration grew as Shelton kept his composure to inch towards victory, maintaining a high first-serve percentage and denying his opponent opportunities.

It took Alcaraz over an hour to launch his fightback - but the former world number one struck at the perfect moment as he broke for a 5-3 lead and forced a decider.

Shelton drew applause from Alcaraz after lifting over a sublime drop shot on his way to holding for a 4-3 lead in the decider - but it was the American who blinked first in the tie-break.

After Shelton missed two forehands to fall a double break and 4-1 behind, Alcaraz guided a backhand return down the line on his first match point and let out a roar in celebration.

Zverev will end a stellar 2026 as a two-time major champion, after ending his long wait for Grand Slam success at this year's French Open and US Open.

He has, however, been "annoyed" at the reaction to his rise to world number one, which has come in a year in which Alcaraz and Sinner - the dominant pair on the ATP Tour in recent years - have struggled with injuries.

Zverev's win against Shelton earlier this week was his first against an opponent ranked in the top five this season.

After defeating Medvedev, he will have the opportunity to prove his status as the current leading men's singles player.

"I think a lot of you think that I hope that good players always lose so I have an easier path, but I enjoy the challenge of playing the best in the world," Zverev said.

"I think any time it's nice to get a win against these two [Alcaraz or Sinner], because they've definitely been the best players in the world the last four years.

"For sure, they are the benchmark. I look forward to the challenge."

Zverev has not dropped serve so far at the tournament, and saved all six break points that he has faced.

The German hit 16 aces against Medvedev, with a faultless tie-break and a single break in the second set taking him to an efficient win.

title: ATP Finals 2026 Day 7 Recap
article_text:
Day 7 of the 2026 ATP Finals saw Carlos Alcaraz and Alexander Zverev book their places in Sunday’s championship match, setting up a fitting finale between the two standout players of the season.

Alcaraz had to work considerably harder than in his previous matches, recovering from a set down to defeat Ben Shelton 3-6, 6-3, 7-6(1). The American pushed him all the way, but a poor deciding tiebreak proved costly as the Spaniard extended his winning streak to 13 matches.

In the evening semi-final, Zverev continued his impressive run in Turin, defeating Daniil Medvedev 7-6(0), 6-4 without facing a break point. The German has now won all four matches in straight sets and hasn’t dropped serve once this week.

Sunday’s final should be an interesting one, with Alcaraz chasing his first ATP Finals title and Zverev looking for a third.

Carlos Alcaraz (2) def. Ben Shelton (3) 3-6, 6-3, 7-6(1)

Carlos Alcaraz kept his hopes of a maiden ATP Finals title alive on Saturday afternoon, coming from a set down to defeat Ben Shelton 3-6, 6-3, 7-6(1) in a two-hour battle.

The Spaniard, who had breezed through the round-robin stage without dropping a set, was made to work considerably harder by Shelton, who produced some of his best tennis of the week.

The American made a flying start, breaking Alcaraz in the opening game with a superb forehand return winner before moving into a 4-1 lead.

Alcaraz looked a little flat, with his movement not quite as sharp as we’ve seen in previous matches. Whether that was down to the left hamstring issue he’s been managing this week is difficult to say, but Shelton certainly took advantage.

The third seed had chances to get back into the opening set, earning two break points at 4-2, but Shelton saved both with big serves before closing it out 6-3.

However, Alcaraz gradually found his rhythm in the second set, moving better, and whenever the point became a baseline rally, you felt like he was going to win it.

The decisive moment came at 4-3, when the Spaniard produced some solid backhand hitting to create two break points. Shelton missed wide on the first, handing Alcaraz the break, and he comfortably served out the set to level the match.

The decider was the best set of the match, with both players raising their level and producing some excellent rallies. Shelton continued to serve well and showed impressive athleticism around the net, while Alcaraz increasingly found his range from the baseline.

Neither player could find a breakthrough, so it all came down to a deciding tiebreak. And that’s where Alcaraz stepped up.

The Spaniard played an almost flawless breaker, taking it 7-1 as Shelton’s level dropped at precisely the wrong moment. After two closely contested sets, the finish was surprisingly one-sided.

It unravelled from the fourth point onwards; after landing back-to-back aces, Alcaraz looped in a return that Shelton went for an off-forehand, but completely armed the ball, and it missed by a country mile.

Nadal used that run-around forehand in the backhand corner so well during his career, but I keep seeing Shelton make mistakes trying to hit it. He then hit a pretty makeable volley long to fall 1-4 behind, and that was that.

It wasn’t Alcaraz’s best performance of the week, but he found a way through when it mattered, finishing with 33 winners and 21 unforced errors compared to Shelton’s 30 winners and 30 errors.

He also won 80% of his first-serve points, which helped keep Shelton at bay during the tight final set.

For Alcaraz, the victory extends his winning streak to 13 matches and keeps his unbeaten indoor record for 2026 intact at 14-0.

He also improves to 5-1 against Shelton, having now beaten the American twice in the past fortnight, following their meeting in the Paris Masters.

Alexander Zverev (1) def. Daniil Medvedev (4) 7-6(0), 6-4

Alexander Zverev booked his place in the 2026 ATP Finals championship match on Saturday evening, defeating Daniil Medvedev 7-6(0), 6-4 with another impressive serving display.

The World No. 1, who had won all three of his round-robin matches without dropping a set or a service game, continued that remarkable run against the 2020 champion, firing down 16 aces and going through the entire match without facing a break point.

Medvedev had served exceptionally well himself throughout the week, and he continued that trend so it was no surprise that the opening set was dominated by serve, with neither player able to find a breakthrough.

However, the tie break was a one-sided affair as Zverev completely dominated it, winning all seven points to take the breaker 7-0, sealing the set with a superb running forehand passing shot.

It was a solid passage of play from Sascha, and kinda replicated their seasons, Zverev has produced his best tennis in the big moments this year, whereas Medvedev hasn’t quite been at his best.

The second set followed a similar pattern, with both players holding comfortably for much of it, although I thought Medvedev’s serve quality dropped a touch and Zverev looked increasingly likely to make something happen on return.

The German eventually found the decisive break, capitalising on a few loose errors and a double fault on break point from Medvedev before serving out the match 6-4 without any drama.

I thought it was a suicidal serve from Meddy on the breakpoint going for a 215km/h second serve outwide. It’s very low percentage play and not really that natural serve for him to hit.

title: BREAKING NEWS: Zverev beats Medvedev to set up an ATP Finals final against Alcaraz
article_text:
Alexander Zverev beat Daniil Medvedev 7-6(0), 6-4 in the second semi-final of the ATP Finals in Turin on Saturday.

World No. 1 Alexander Zverev beat Daniil Medvedev 7-6(0), 6-4 in the second semi-final of the ATP Finals in Turin on Saturday to reach his third final at the event. On Sunday, the two-time champion will face Carlos Alcaraz, who beat Ben Shelton earlier in the day.

The serve dominated a first set made of short points: neither man faced a single break point in twelve games. Zverev then swept the tie-break 7-0. The first break point of the match only came after 71 minutes, on Medvedev’s serve at 3-3 in the second set, and Zverev converted his second opportunity to lead 4-3.

He had to fight to keep his advantage. Down 0-15 and 15-30 in the next game, he held for 5-3. Serving for the match at 5-4, he opened with a double fault, missed his first serve on the first three points and hit a second double fault at 30-30, but a service winner gave him a match point. Medvedev sent a backhand long to end it.

It is Zverev’s second straight win over the man who has long been his bete noire, after the Paris Masters quarter-final last year. Medvedev still leads their head-to-head 14-9, but the pair are now level 3-3 at the ATP Finals. Zverev, champion in 2018 and 2021, becomes the 13th man to reach three finals at the event, according to the ATP. The final will be his first match against Alcaraz or Jannik Sinner since he became world No. 1. Alcaraz leads their head-to-head 7-6 and won their last meeting, in the Australian Open semi-finals in January.

More coverage on tennismajors.com from Turin soon.

Carlos Alcaraz makes ‘frustrated’ admission after beating Ben Shelton at ATP Finals
article_text:
Carlos Alcaraz has shared his thoughts after reaching the final at the 2026 ATP Finals with a comeback victory against Ben Shelton.

The seven-time Grand Slam champion defeated world No 4 Shelton 3-6, 6-3, 7-6(1) in the semi-finals at the season-ending championships in Turin on Saturday.

Alcaraz finished top of the John McEnroe Group at the ATP Finals with a 3-0 record after he did not drop a set in dominant wins over Frances Tiafoe, Daniil Medvedev and Flavio Cobolli.

The world No 3 lost his serve for the first time in the tournament in the second game against Shelton, and he was unable to break back in the opening set.

The Spanish star responded strongly in the second set, and he broke the big-serving American at 4-3 before holding serve to force a decider.

Neither player faced a break point in the third set, but Alcaraz sealed the win in style as he dominated the decisive tiebreak by winning the last seven points.

Want more from Tennis365? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for tennis coverage you can trust.

Alcaraz now holds a 5-1 record against Shelton, having beaten the American in the Paris Masters final earlier this month after losing the pair’s epic quarter-final at the 2026 US Open.

In his on-court interview with Tennis TV, Alcaraz admitted he was frustrated by how he started the match.

“Well, just really, really happy. I was a little bit frustrated at the beginning because I didn’t start the match the way I wanted to, to be honest,” said the 23-year-old.

“And against someone like Ben; big serve, big… playing from the baseline, I think he just pushes you to the limit every time. And I think I just didn’t start that well.

“And then the break early, it was tough for me to deal with. But I’m just happy that I came back in the second set playing such a great tennis. Step by step, focus on my things, and ended up playing a good tennis.

“I think the third set was even closer, I think he raised the level a little bit from the second set; myself, as well.

“Great points, great games, and just happy to play a great tennis in the tiebreak — I think it’s when it matters, to be honest.

“So, excited for tomorrow and happy with everything today.”

Alcaraz will face either Alexander Zverev or Daniil Medvedev in the final in Turin on Sunday. He is aiming to win his maiden ATP Finals title.

title: “I feel great but don’t have to push myself to the limit”: Alcaraz passes his hamstring test, but is learning not to chase every ball
article_text:
After beating Ben Shelton in the ATP Finals semi-finals in Turin on Saturday, two days after an MRI on his hamstring, Carlos Alcaraz said the match was “a great feedback” on his physical state. The Spaniard admits he is still holding back on some movements ahead of Sunday’s final.

Carlos Alcaraz feels good enough to play for the title. “Today again, a really important test for myself to see where I am physically,” the Spaniard said on Saturday in Turin, after beating Ben Shelton 3-6, 6-3, 7-6(1) to reach the ATP Finals final, two days after an MRI on his hamstring. “I think it went great. I feel great, moving hard, probably not pushing myself to the limit.”

Asked how he felt after two hours of intense battle, and about the strapping visible on his leg, he admitted he is still managing the problem. “Probably without this problem in the leg I could move differently a little bit, probably even harder, but I’m realizing that I just need to be careful with it, and sometimes I don’t have to push myself to the limit in some movements (…) and some balls. I don’t have to run every ball, which I’m just understanding right now.”

“I’m feeling better, feeling good. Today was a great feedback for me,” he added. “Right now I’m going to (…) try to recover and be ready for tomorrow.”

In Spanish, he went a step further, explaining that the injury had taught him something about the way he plays. “Physically, I felt very good. It wasn’t a moment for doubts (…). Honestly, I felt good. Maybe I didn’t go crazy the way I might have done at another time if I hadn’t had the leg issue, but I think this has also helped me understand a little how I should go for a lot of balls when I’m healthy: maybe I don’t have to go crazy, I don’t have to run for certain impossible balls to be well physically,” he said. “Now we are going to use every minute and every hour of the day to recover, to do things right and to be as good as possible tomorrow.”

On court, the hamstring did not stop him from raising his level when it mattered, winning the third-set tie-break 7-1. “Today I just went for it, to be honest. I didn’t think about physically. I just felt well, and if I lose, it was totally fair,” Alcaraz said.

He described the mindset he took into that tie-break. “I don’t try anything different. I just try to play a good tennis, and I try not to let the moment affect my game, affect myself. I just try to be calm, I try to be relaxed and try to do the things that I have to do,” he said. “If I miss, if I lose, but feel like I did the right things, I’m leaving the court happy and I’m proud. So it wasn’t about being nervous about that moment, it’s just about to accept it, to enjoy playing this moment.”

The Spaniard had cancelled his practice on Thursday after the MRI and beaten Flavio Cobolli on Friday while deliberately holding back physically. He has never revealed his diagnosis. On Sunday, he will play for the title against the winner of the evening’s semi-final between Alexander Zverev and Daniil Medvedev, a year after losing the final to Jannik Sinner.

title: Carlos Alcaraz and Ben Shelton’s ranking points & prize money after ATP Finals semi-final
article_text:
Carlos Alcaraz prevailed in a deciding set tiebreak to defeat Ben Shelton in a pulsating semi-final at the 2026 ATP Finals.

World No 3 Alcaraz fought back to earn a 3-6, 6-3, 7-6(1) victory over fourth-ranked Shelton in the last four at the Inalpi Arena in Turin.

The Spanish star produced a stunning level to seal the win as he dominated the third set tiebreak by winning the last seven points of the match.

Alcaraz, who is chasing his maiden ATP Finals title, is through to his second final at the season-ending championships, having lost to Jannik Sinner in last year’s title match.

The seven-time Grand Slam champion dismantled Frances Tiafoe, Daniil Medvedev and Flavio Cobolli in the round robin stage in Turin, and he has extended his overall winning streak to 13 matches.

The American progressed to the last four after winning two of his three matches in the group stage.

Lakshya Sen's title hat-trick bid ends as Satwik-Chirag also crash out, India draw blank at Hong Kong Ope
article_text:
suffered straight-game defeats in their respective semifinals.

Lakshya's bid for a third consecutive title was halted by Denmark's Anders Antonsen, who produced a commanding 21-13, 21-13 victory. Earlier, Satwik and Chirag, the world No. 6 pair, went down 18-21, 19-21 against Malaysia's eighth-seeded combination of Man Wei Chong and Tee Kai Wun.

The defeats meant India finished the tournament without a finalist, despite Lakshya arriving in Hong Kong on the back of consecutive titles at the Hylo Open and Kumamoto Masters Japan over the last two weeks.

Satwik and Chirag began their semifinal with a 4-1 head-to-head advantage over Man and Tee, but the Malaysians proved more effective in the crucial moments.

The Indians made an encouraging start, racing to a 3-0 lead, before their opponents fought back in an attacking contest featuring sharp returns, angled shots and powerful smashes.

The scores remained close through the opening exchanges, but Man and Tee edged ahead 11-10 at the interval.

Tee then raised his intensity as the Malaysians opened up a 16-12 lead.

Satwik and Chirag fought back from 16-19 to level at 19-19 in the second game after trailing 15-18, but the Malaysians held their nerve. They targeted Chirag to earn match point before sealing the contest with a precise push into the corner.

The defeat ended another impressive season for the Indian pair, who had won titles in Singapore and China this year.

Lakshya, meanwhile, struggled to find his rhythm against Antonsen, who controlled the rallies with accurate placement and clever angles.

The Danish shuttler established an early 3-0 lead before Lakshya fought back to make it 8-8. However, Antonsen moved ahead at the interval and gradually took control, closing out the opening game 21-13.

The second game followed a similar pattern. Antonsen moved ahead 5-2 after the change of ends and carried an 11-6 advantage into the interval.

Lakshya produced occasional moments of resistance but remained inconsistent, allowing Antonsen to extend his lead to 18-9. The Dane eventually converted his third match point to complete a comfortable victory.

Lakshya's movement and reactions appeared a fraction slower, with the accumulated workload of his recent title-winning run possibly catching up with him.

title: Hong Kong Open 2026 badminton: Lakshya Sen's 13-match winning streak ends in semi-finals
Hong Kong Open: ‘We Will Come Back Stronger’
article_text:
Goh Soon Huat and Lai Shevon Jemie came to LI-NING Hong Kong Open 2026 needing a miracle – and very nearly pulled it off.

Having suffered three first-round exits in their previous four tournaments, the Malaysian husband-and-wife duo hauled themselves off the canvas and back into the race for the HSBC BWF World Tour Finals 2026 with a gritty semifinal run. Standing between them and the final ticket to Hangzhou next month were top seeds Feng Yan Zhe and Huang Dong Ping.

On Saturday, Goh and Lai pushed the Chinese powerhouse to the brink before falling 21-17 21-18 – a result that officially wrapped up the mixed doubles qualification race and handed the last berth to Japanese pair Yuta Watanabe/Maya Taguchi.

Yet, despite the heartbreak of falling short of a season-finale appearance, there were no hung heads in the mixed zone. Instead, there was a quiet, hard-earned relief their spark had returned.

“It wasn’t a perfect match but both of us gave the best we had,” said Lai. “Coming in from quite a rollercoaster of results and performances, today was one of our steadier matches. Although we didn’t manage to get the win, we did quite well.”

They certainly made Feng and Huang sweat, clawing back in the second game to snatch a 16-15 lead before the world No.1s slammed the door shut.

“Against the Chinese pairs, even if you lead by quite a few points, it’s still not much of an advantage because they have the ability to catch right back up,” Lai admitted.

Goh echoed that sentiment, confessing that the weight of the occasion briefly got the better of his footwork. “At the start, I quite enjoyed the match. But once we reached a more crucial point, I began to put more pressure on myself and lost my pacing – my speed got too fast and broke my rhythm.”

Still, as their 2026 campaign ends, the detour to Hong Kong proved invaluable.

“The good thing is we have regained our momentum, our rhythm and most importantly, our confidence,” Goh noted.

For Lai, who openly admitted she had been battling self-doubt, the semifinal run was the exact validation she needed.

“I can see the results of my training showing up on court this time,” she said. “That has given me a good push to know I’m heading in the right direction.”

Hangzhou will have to wait, then – but with their mojo firmly back in their kit bags, Goh and Lai are already looking forward to what 2027 brings.

title: 2026 WTA Rankings Winners & Losers: Elena Rybakina +4, Iga Swiatek -7, Alex Eala +38, Emma Raducanu -79
article_text:
The 2026 WTA Tour season has wrapped up and there is a new No 1 as Elena Rybakina finished at the top of a different-looking top-20 in the WTA Rankings compared to the start of the year.

Rybakina started the 2026 campaign at No 5 in the rankings, but she took over at No 1 after the US Open in September and confirmed her position as year-end No 1 during the Asian swing, bringing an end to Aryna Sabalenka’s long reign.

And there is also a new No 2 with teenager Mirra Andreeva finishing at a career-high on the back of her French Open and WTA Finals titles this year, up from No 9 last year.

Sabalenka – who started the year at No 1 and spent 99 consecutive weeks at the top – finishes at No 3.

The Sabalenka-Iga Swiatek days of dominance ended this year as the latter was No 2 on January 1, but she slipped to No 9 with neither winning a Grand Slam in 2026 although the Belarusian finished runner-up to Rybakina at the Australian Open and US Open.

Coco Gauff and Jessica Pegula are still firmly part of the top 10, but the likes of Madison Keys (-12), Amanda Anisimova and Jasmine Paolini (-27) have dropped off.

Elina Svitolina (+8), Linda Noskova (+6), Karolina Muchova (+11) and Marta Kostyuk (+16) have moved into the top 10.

In terms of those who finished between No 11 and No 20 in 2026, Maja Chwalinska was at No 150 on 1 January and finds herself 138 places higher at No 12 with her rise coming on the back of her runners-up finish at Roland Garros and her maiden WTA 1000 title at the Wuhan Open.

No 13 Iva Jovic is +22 thanks to a run to the quarter-finals at the Australian Open and the successful defence of her WTA 500 trophy at the Guadalajara Open.

Fellow rising star Alex Eala sits two places behind the American as she climbed 38 places from No 53 with her jump coming on the back of her maiden WTA Tour title at the WTA 500 Washington DC Open while she also finished runner-up at the Hong Kong WTA 250 event.

Sorana Cirstea is up from No 43 to No 16 as she finished her final year as a professional with the Transylvania Open title and a quarter-final appearance at Roland Garros.

*Although the WTA Tour season is over, there are still a few WTA 125K and ITF events taking place, but no one in the top 20 will feature so the above top 20 will remain unchanged, while there could be one or two changes lower down the list.

Kristina Liutova started the 2025 season at No 714, but the 16-year-old surged up the rankings on the back of her maiden title at the Memphis Classic as she became the second youngest player to win a WTA Tour title on debut.

The Russian teenager is currently at No 103, 611 places better off than on 1 January.

Sara Bejlek, Lilli Tagger, Diane Parry, Claire Liu and Hariet Dart also won their maiden titles this year and also earned big jumps.

Czech Bejlek sits at No 33, having started the year at No 92, Parry is one place behind her after surging 90 spots from No 124, Tagger won her maiden title at the age of 18 and she rose from No 159 to No 54, while Liu is +140 from No 207 to No 67 and Dart is +87 from No 172 to No 85.

Dart is currently the British No 3 behind Katie Boulter – who started 2026 at No 106, but is currently No 50 – and Sonay Kartal (No 68 to No 54).

Former Australian Open champion Sofia Kenin’s struggles continued in 2026 as she started at No 28, but has dropped 161 places to no 189.

Emma Raducanu finished the 2025 season as the British No 1 as she was No 29 and she reached No 23 in March, but injury ruined her year as she didn’t play any matches during the second half of the campaign and has slumped 79 places to No 108.

title: Iga Swiatek makes huge schedule change as first event of 2027 season confirmed
article_text:
Iga Swiatek will not line up at the 2027 United Cup as she has opted not to compete at the annual team tournament for the first time since its launch, instead signing up for a regular WTA Tour event.

Since the inaugural United Cup in 2023, Swiatek has been an ever-present member of Team Poland and steered them to back-to-back runners-up titles in 2024 and 2025 before they finally got their hands on the coveted winner’s trophy last year.

But the six-time Grand Slam winner won’t be part of Poland’s title defence in January 2027 as she has decided to swap the team environment for the individual competition of the Tour by entering the Brisbane International.

Swiatek will make her debut at the WTA 500 event that will also feature world No 1 Elena Rybakina – who won the title in 2024 – and four-time Grand Slam winner Naomi Osaka.

Aryna Sabalenka won the tournament the past two years, but organisers are yet to confirm if she will return to seek a third consecutive trophy at the season opener.

For Swiatek, it is certainly a big shift in her calendar following a disappointing 2026 season that saw her fail to win a Grand Slam for the first time since 2021. Her best run at the majors was at the Australian Open where she reached the quarter-finals.

Although she won two titles – the United Cup and the Canadian Open – she finished a disappointing ninth in the WTA Rankings, having started the year at No 2 behind Sabalenka, as she failed to qualify for the season-ending WTA Finals in Indian Wells.

The last time the former world No 1 finished that lowly was back in 2021.

There is no doubt that she and her team, with coach Francisco Roig leading the way, hopes this change will lead to a better 2027 season, especially with several high-quality opponents set to test her in Brisbane ahead of the first Grand Slam of the year.

Before signing up for the United Cup, Swiatek competed at the 2022 Adelaide International and reached the semi-final before losing against then world No 1 Ashleigh Barty. That, though, gave her confidence ahead of the Australian Open as she also reached the last four in Melbourne, but lost against Danielle Collins.

In 2021, she started at the Gippsland Trophy and made it to the quarter-finals, while in 2020 and 2019 she kicked off her season at the Australian Open.

title: ATP Finals 2026: Schedule, results, bracket and groups for year-end championship in Turin
article_text:
Carlos Alcaraz stayed on course for a first ATP Finals title, as he won a thrilling semi-final against Ben Shelton on Saturday.

Alcaraz battled back from a set down to beat the American 3-6, 6-3, 7-6 (1) in Turin.

The year-end championship is one of the showpiece events on the men's tennis tour, and only the top eight players in the calendar year make the cut.

With Jannik Sinner out with an injury and Novak Djokovic failing to qualify, Alcaraz has the chance to win the prestigious title for the first time.

The ATP Finals takes place in two phases: group stage and the knockouts. Eight players are divided into two groups of four, with each player competing against those in their group once.

Top two players from each group will qualify for the semi-final.
