title: Rolex keeps time for Davis Cup through extension
article_text:
World Tennis, the recently rebranded global governing body, has extended its commercial tie-up with luxury Swiss watch brand Rolex.

Through a contract extension unveiled today, Rolex will continue as a sponsor of the Davis Cup men's national teams series; the brand will keep its designation as official timekeeper of that competition.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

Rolex has been in that position since 2007, while its overall involvement in tennis dates back to 1978. GlobalData Sport has valued its most recent tie-up at $1.25 million annually.

It is now, in addition to its Davis Cup involvement, it is a partner of all four Grand Slam tournaments, a sponsor of both the men's ATP and women's WTA tours, and – in addition – the official timekeeper for the Finals of the women's Billie Jean King Cup.

It also has specific agreements in place with current tennis stars Carlos Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner.

This deal has been unveiled in the build-up to the Final 8 finale of the 2026 Davis Cup, which is taking place in Bologna, Italy, between November 24 (tomorrow) and 29.

This month has already seen Yonex, the Japanese racket sports equipment brand, named as the tennis ball partner for this year's Davis Cup Final 8.

The 2026 Davis Cup Final 8 will see eight national teams compete to be crowned world champions. Alongside hosts Italy, seven winning nations from September's second-round qualifiers will participate in the event, including Czechia, Canada, South Korea, Great Britain, Germany, Austria and Spain.

International insurance company Generali Group was recently named as the new presenting partner for the Davis Cup, meanwhile.

World Tennis' commercial portfolio for the tournament also includes the likes of Visa, MG, Corpay, Fred Perry, and Betsson.

Ross Hutchins, chief executive at World Tennis, commented: "The brand is synonymous with success and prestige, and their commitment to our competition is a source of great pride for us. This news is another highlight in a year of significant commercial growth in Davis Cup as we look forward to the Final 8 this week."

World Tennis was unveiled as a rebrand of the International Tennis Federation in late June.

Arnaud Boetsch, Rolex's director of communications and image, added: "Our continued partnership with the Davis Cup by Generali reflects a relationship developed over many years, and we are proud to support the tournament and its values of team spirit, passion and sporting tradition."

The Swiss watchmaker's stable of sporting tie-ups also includes a tie-up with North American golf's top-tier PGA Tour – that deal has also been extended this month.

It also has deals in place with properties including golf's DP World Tour and World Sailing.

title: UEFA awards media rights to club competitions in 10 markets
article_text:
UEFA, European soccer’s governing body, has awarded broadcast rights to its major club competitions in 10 markets across Europe, Oceania, and the Caribbean after announcing its preferred bidders for the 2027-31 cycle.

The markets covered in this process are Australia, the Caribbean, Cyprus, the Dominican Republic, Greece, Iceland, Israel, Malta, New Zealand, and Türkiye.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

Rights have been awarded for the elite UEFA Champions League (UCL), secondary Europa League, and third-tier Conference League for the next four seasons, from 2027-28 through 2030-31.

The process, described as “highly competitive”, included incumbent broadcasters, new market entrants, global digital platforms as well as local pay and free-to-air channels. New partners were secured in five of the 10 markets.

In Australia, all UCL rights have been snapped up by international sports streaming giant DAZN, which includes Foxtel and Kayo Sports.

DAZN has also landed rights to all three club competitions in Israel.

Elsewhere in Europe, rights to all club competitions have been secured by free-to-air (FTA) broadcaster Skai in Greece, pay-TV operator Cyta in Cyprus (with public-service broadcaster CYBC to show UCL Tuesday first pick games on a co-exclusive basis), digital streaming platform Exxen in Turkey, and cable pay-TV broadcaster Melita in Malta, with the semi-finals and finals of each competition to be shown FTA by the government-owned public broadcaster PBS.

CYBC will now provide free coverage of the UCL in Cyprus after previously having rights to the Europa League and Conference League, while Exxen returns as the rightsholder in Turkey, taking over from public-service broadcaster TRT.

In Iceland, streaming service Viaplay will keep UCL rights, while OTT platform Livey has acquired the Europa League and Conference League.

In the Caribbean, CPSL has retained rights to the UCL, Europa League, and Conference League, with ATV having all rights in Suriname co-exclusively. CPSL’s deal also covers the Dominican Republic.

Broadcast partners for the Europa League and Conference League in Australia, and for all three competitions in New Zealand, have been awarded to a preferred bidder but will be announced at a later date.

As well as Viaplay and CPSL, the deals with CYTA, Melita and PBS are also renewals.

UEFA went to market in all 10 territories at the end of September, with a deadline for submissions of November 3.

The tender process was managed by the UC3 commercial arm, a joint venture between UEFA and the European Football Clubs' body, and Relevant Football partners, UEFA’s sales agency for the club competitions through 2033, spanning media, sponsorship, and licensing rights.

Sportcal (GlobalData Sport) understands Relevent’s third and final multi-market tender concluded with an average uplift of around 150% across the 10 markets, which represents the strongest result of the 2027-31 media rights cycle so far for the agency.

Just 12 months after Relevent opened the process with its tender for Europe's top five markets in late 2025, only a small number of markets remain to be finalised.

These are Bosnia and Herzegovina, Croatia, Gibraltar, the Indian Subcontinent, Montenegro, North Macedonia, the Pacific Islands, Serbia, Slovenia and Ukraine.

title: WSL and member clubs agree on central betting sponsor ban
article_text:
English women's soccer's top-tier WSL has an agreement in place with its clubs that it will not take on betting brands as commercial partners at league level.

An announcement was made regarding this decision late last week by the WSL Football body, which governs both the 14-team WSL and the 12-team WSL 2.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

As part of the agreement, neither league can sign deals with betting brands.

However, The Athletic has reported that the move does not stop individual teams from striking deals with betting companies.

Currently, both West Ham United and Birmingham City's women's teams have front-of-shirt deals with betting brands. West Ham have Boyle Sports as their main partner, while Birmingham City have a similar tie-up with Coral.

In terms of the approach to gambling sponsors taken by men's soccer in England, the top-tier Premier League and its 20 clubs have banned front-of-shirt betting sponsors, as of the start of the 2026-27 campaign.

However, clubs are still free to bring in these same brands in other sponsorship categories – such as deals covering training kits and sleeve sponsorships.

In the men's second-tier English Football League, and its three member divisions, meanwhile, no such restrictions apply.

For the WSL, Barclays Bank has title-sponsored the league since 2019-20, with other main partners including Airbnb, British Gas, Tesco, EA FC, and Mercedes-Benz.

The Tesco deal was the last of these agreements to be unveiled, with a multi-year deal between the two parties announced in late September.

Tesco is now serving as the official supermarket partner of the WSL and WSL 2.

The 2026-27 WSL campaign got underway on September 4 and will run through May 23.

WSL Football, owned by its member clubs, was set up in August 2024 and controls the top two leagues. During its first year as a standalone organization – ending in July 2025 – it recorded an operating loss of £8.2 million (at the time, $11.3 million).

title: Copa America close to US return for 2028 edition
article_text:
South American soccer’s CONMEBOL is reportedly close to announcing the United States as the host of the 2028 Copa America continental competition.

The quadrennial tournament, CONMEBOL’s flagship national team competition, will be hosted in the US for the second consecutive time in 2028, and the third time overall.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

The reports come after the US' successful co-hosting of the FIFA World Cup 2026 earlier this year alongside Canada and Mexico, while reports from South America suggest Ecuador is not ready to host the event.

Copa America hosting rights are awarded on a cyclical basis between the CONMEBOL nations and Ecuador. Recent reports state Ecuador remains unprepared to host the event again four years after pulling out the first time.

In 2024, the US stepped in after CONMEBOL agreed to a strategic tie-up with North America’s CONCACAF that saw the US replace the initial host, Ecuador, which had to pull out due to public security issues in the country.

The US also hosted in 2016 a special edition of the tournament outside of the four-year cycle, also part of an agreement between CONMEBOL and CONCACAF to celebrate the centenary of the Copa America.

In all, this means the US has hosted three of the last five editions of the Copa America, perhaps suggesting that CONMEBOL has come to be reliant on the increased financial benefits of staging the tournament in the US.

After all, US hosting means US participation, allowing CONMEBOL to command greater rights fees in the most lucrative sports market in the Americas, and beyond.

The 2024 edition was expanded from 10 to 16 teams, adding six CONCACAF sides to the mix: Canada, Costa Rica, Jamaica, Mexico, Panama, and the US.

Subsequently, rights were snapped up in the US by media giant Fox, which generated multiple record seven-figure viewership tallies during the tournament, despite a US exit.

The 2024 Copa América final between Argentina and Colombia, won by the former, delivered 6.35 million viewers, drawing the largest audience on Spanish-language media giant TelevisaUnivision to that point since the 2014 World Cup final.

Fox’s viewership, which peaked at 7.07 million, increased 211% when compared to the 2021 edition between Brazil and Argentina (1.94 million), and was he tournament’s largest English-language audience on record.

The Copa America tournament overall averaged 1.42 million viewers across the Fox, FS1, and FS2 channels, an increase of more than 350% from 2021’s 309,000, and up 44% from 2016’s 987,000, ranking it as the most-watched edition of the tournament on English-language TV.

Dentsu, the Japanese advertising giant heavily involved in sports marketing, remains the exclusive global consulting and commercial sales agent of the Copa America through the 2028 edition, and will likely be hoping that the event returns to the US, as it would once more be able to attract high-profile US brands to sponsor the event.

The 2024 edition was sponsored by the likes of US beer brand Michelob Ultra, soft drinks giant Coca-Cola, tech firm TCL, Chinese electric car company BYD, and consumer goods conglomerate Unilever.

title: Esso partners NHL in Germany for Dusseldorf international games
article_text:
North America’s elite National Hockey League (NHL) has announced a new partnership with Esso, the prominent retail petrol and diesel brand, covering the German market.

Esso becomes an official partner of the NHL in Germany, gaining marketing rights including virtual slot in-ice advertising and digitally enhanced dashboard placement on NHL regular-season broadcasts in Germany.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

This will include the new free-to-air Monday Night Hockey format, which is shown by the commercial broadcaster RTL, and coverage on pay-TV network Sky (which was recently acquired by RTL).

Esso gains the right to utilize NHL branding and NHL players in co-branded promotional campaigns, and the pair will also collaborate on social media advertising on the NHL’s digital channels.

Marketing rights will extend to the upcoming pair of two regular-season NHL games set to take place in Germany next month, the NHL Global Series Germany, which will see the Ottawa Senators play two games in Dusseldorf against the Chicago Blackhawks, on December 18 and 20.

Esso branding around that game will include digitally enhanced rink-side dasherboards, in-arena signage, a corner in-ice position on the rink, and an “in-arena game presentation feature,” as well as positioning at the Global Series Fan Festival, which will be active from November 30 to December 24 in Schadowstrasse and at the PSD Bank Dome in Düsseldorf (December 18 to 20).

Users of the Esso Extras app may also have the chance to win tickets to the games.

Speaking on the announcement, NHL vice president for global business development Max Paulsen said: "As anticipation builds for the 2026 NHL Global Series Germany in Düsseldorf, our partnership with Esso represents another important milestone in our efforts to deepen fan engagement and grow the NHL across Germany.

“Esso’s marketing support will help us reach fans in new and creative ways in Germany, and we look forward to delivering exceptional fan experiences through our relationship."

Esso's parent company Imperial Oil has been associated with the NHL since 1936, and in 2018, it became the official retail fuel of the NHL in the Canadian market. Now, by expanding its coverage to a priority international territory, it has entrenched itself in the league’s sponsorship platform.

Around one-third of the total number of contracted NHL players are European, of whom seven are German, including Edmonton Oilers forward and five-time all-star Leon Draisaitl, making the DACH region specifically one of the league's targeted growth areas.

The international games in Dusseldorf this season will be presented by Kaufland, through a deal announced earlier this month. Other sponsors include DHL – which agreed a Europe-wide deal with the league in October that also covered a pair of games that took place in Finland later this month, featuring the Carolina Hurricanes and Seattle Kraken.

title: CAF turns profit of over $30m in 2025-26
article_text:
The Confederation of African Football (CAF) governing body has recorded a profit of $31.2 million for the 2025-26 financial year.

This represents a welcome return to profitability for Egypt-based CAF, which managed this through increasing its total revenue to $284 million during the last financial year.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

The governing body unveiled these figures at its 2026 general assembly in Nigeria, over the weekend.

CAF has turned its position around in the last half-decade – five years ago, it had debts of over $100 million.

This past year's figures were boosted by the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) men's national teams tournament in Morocco – over $100 million in revenue arrived through the continent's flagship event.

The soccer body's cash balance position has also improved – as of June this year, that figure came to $118.8 million.

CAF is now able to provide financial support to each of its member federations of $700,000, with this figure having most recently increased in July. Overall, the governing body has the eventual aim of taking this number up to the $1 million mark.

In terms of overall prize money and solidarity funding to African club soccer sides, meanwhile, CAF is this year contributing $48 million. In 2021, that same figure was only $19 million.

Prize money for national teams has also increased significantly over the last half-decade – the winners of the 2025 AFCON, for example, received $10 million, double what the 2021 AFCON winners were allocated.

For the Women's AFCON, the 2026 winners took home $2 million, up from just $200,000 five years ago.

In terms of recent CAF activity, earlier this month, the governing body unveiled a tie-up with sports data provider FeedConstruct.

Armenia-based FeedConstruct has snapped up exclusive match data and betting streaming rights to the full range of top-tier CAF competitions.

CAF is also looking for host nations for the next three editions of AFCON, due to be held in 2028, 2031, and 2033.

That process has a deadline of December 8 for the proper submission of all related documents and government guarantees by interested parties.

CAF, in addition, has a new secretary general, with Nigeria's Samson Adamu having recently been appointed.

title: AlUla, Qatar Tours cancelled, PIF pulls Jayco-AlUla cycling team backing
article_text:
The fallout from the conflict in the Middle East has continued, with elite road cycling becoming the latest sport to be impacted after the 2027 AlUla Tour and Tour of Qatar events were scrapped and AlUla withdrew from its sponsorship coverage of the sport.

The AlUla Tour, formerly known as the Saudi Tour, is the most prominent cancellation. Promoted by Amaury Sport Organisation (ASO), which organizes the Tour de France, the multi-day five-stage race has been an annual staple since 2020, and in 2026 was designated UCI ProSeries class.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

In recent years, prominent names such as British riders Tom Pidcock (2025) and Simon Yates (2024) have won the event, which typically takes place across late January and early February.

It is not yet confirmed whether or not the event will return in 2028, but with the Saudi government’s focus diverting away from sport in the short term, it may be unlikely.

A return for the men’s and women’s Tour of Qatar, which has not been staged since 2016, has also been cancelled, with a new aim of 2028 announced for the race’s restart.

Eight months of conflict between Iran and a US-Israel coalition, as well as increasing tensions in Saudi Arabia with the Houthi rebel group (which has recently claimed credit for multiple attacks on targets in Saudi Arabia), have left confidence in the region from a hosting perspective low, despite the large sums of money that countries in the Middle East can dedicate towards hosting fees.

The AlUla Development Company, the commercial vehicle for the AlUla region, is owned by Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund (PIF), a sovereign wealth fund, which has pared back its sports investments across 2026.

This has affected the peloton, as men’s WorldTour team Jayco-AlUla and associated women's team, Liv-AlUla-Jayco, have been left without sponsorship.

The PIF has pulled its sponsorship of the two teams, which are predominantly backed by Australian businessman Gerry Ryan, founder of caravan manufacturer Jayco, and the eponymous Jayco brand.

Publication Escape Collective claims that Ryan has already secured a crucial new commercial partner, meaning that the team’s budget for 2026 will not be cut too substantially, although a reduction on such short notice is possible.

The team has already lost Grand Tour stage winners Ben O’Connor and Mauro Schmid ahead of the 2027 campaign.

Sponsorship such as this is vital for cycling teams at all levels of the sport, the majority of which are almost entirely sponsor-funded, meaning that losing a title sponsor like AlUla could be crippling to many operations.

Cycling’s heavy reliance on sponsorship revenue, and that spending’s direct correlation with rider contract spending, has created a catch-22 situation where winning races requires top riders, access to top riders requires significant sponsorship revenue, and sponsorship revenue can only be grown by winning races.

This has effectively stratified the WorldTour peloton, with the top six-to-eight teams, backed by high-profile sponsors, billionaire investment, or sovereign wealth financing, performing at a level that the other sides, which rely on less lucrative sponsorship deals and, in many cases, face an annual struggle just to continue operations, cannot.

This dynamic was dissected earlier this year on the Sportcal Podcast, wherein GlobalData Sport lead analyst Conrad Wiacek and head of data Gordon Berry discussed the varying perspectives on cycling sponsorship, where money in cycling comes from, and how teams can improve sponsorship values by maximizing their resources.

title: SEN expands radio rights to A-League in Australia and New Zealand
article_text:
Sports Entertainment Network (SEN), the multi-platform Australian media company, has secured a package of domestic radio rights to the A-League, the men’s top-tier soccer competition, across Australia and New Zealand.

The deal, struck with A-Leagues, the organizer of Australia’s men’s and women’s competitions, will see SEN broadcast at least 18 regular-season A-League Men fixtures, as well as finals matches, during the ongoing 2026-27 season.

Combine business intelligence and editorial excellence to reach engaged professionals across 36 leading media platforms.

SEN’s coverage began on November 20, when Western Sydney Wanderers beat Adelaide, and aired across the SEN and Sport Nation radio networks, as well as the SEN app.

The 2026-27 A-League Men season started on October 16 and features 12 teams competing across 28 match weeks through May 9, 2027. The Final Series then starts on the weekend of June 4 to 6, 2027.

Alongside live matches, the agreement will see A-Leagues content, including player interviews and analysis, integrated across SEN’s programming in Melbourne, Sydney, and Brisbane, as well as Sport Nation in New Zealand.

A-Leagues chief executive Steve Rosich said: “Our focus is on introducing more Australians and New Zealanders to the excitement of live A-Leagues football.

“It’s a great boost for our game to kick off this partnership with the growing SEN network to reach new audiences and create more opportunities for sports fans to experience first-hand what makes live football so special.”

Paramount holds domestic pay-TV and free-to-air rights for the men’s and women’s A-League in a deal running through 2028-29.

Under the deal, all A-League men’s and women’s games are aired on the Paramount+ streaming service, while one men’s game is broadcast live and free on its Network 10 commercial broadcaster every week.

Network 10’s own streaming platform also houses all A-League women’s fixtures.

The new deal follows SEN’s coverage of soccer’s flagship FIFA World Cup 2026 national teams’ tournament earlier this year, the network’s third consecutive World Cup after Qatar 2022 and the Women’s World Cup 2023.

Beyond soccer, SEN holds radio rights to the Australian Rules AFL competition through 2027 and American football’s NFL, covering at least one live game per regular season and the 2026 Melbourne Game, as well as Test and Big Bash cricket matches, netball, horse racing, tennis, and golf.

SEN group content director Sam Thompson said: “Following our extensive coverage of the FIFA World Cup, we’re excited to continue that momentum by showcasing the best of our domestic competition, including some fantastic rivalries and major fixtures.

“The A-League is an important part of the Australian sporting landscape, and this agreement allows us to build on our football offering, complementing programs like Gloves Off with Bozza & Adam Peacock and giving fans more opportunities to engage with the game throughout the season.”

The new deal comes as A-Leagues continues to add to its commercial partnership slate, having brought in Champion Data as the official broadcast graphics provider for the men’s and women’s competitions last month.

title: Women’s World Cup heads to the UK in 2035
article_text:
Sixty-nine years after England lifted the men’s trophy at Wembley, the UK is set to host the World Cup again. FIFA’s Congress meets today, Monday 23rd November, to ratify England, Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales as co-hosts of the 2035 Women’s World Cup.

The four nations are the only bidders, and member associations will vote at a specially arranged virtual meeting while a UK delegation attends Fifa’s Zurich headquarters. Ratification would end a long wait for a World Cup on home soil: England’s bids for the men’s tournament in 2006 and 2018 failed, and a proposed UK and Ireland bid for 2030 was abandoned.

The 2035 tournament will be the second women’s edition to feature 48 teams, with 104 matches played over 39 days. The ‘All Together’ bid proposes 19 venues across the four nations. These range from Wembley, Old Trafford and Everton’s Hill Dickinson Stadium in England to Hampden Park and Easter Road in Scotland, the Principality Stadium and Cardiff City Stadium in Wales, and a redeveloped Windsor Park in Northern Ireland. Birmingham’s Powerhouse Stadium, Wrexham’s Racecourse Ground and a potential new Chelsea ground could take the total to 22 venues across 16 cities.

The bid scored 4.3 out of five in Fifa’s evaluation, published earlier this month. It is not without complications, though. Fifa rated its contractual framework as medium risk, citing qualifications in government guarantees on tax, safety and security. The issue is thought to centre on Fifa’s request for tax-free status for football-related activities. The evaluation concluded that the long lead-in time gives a sound basis for resolving the outstanding issues.

Mark Bullingham, Chief Executive of the Football Association, said, “Hosting Euro 2022 allowed us to change the game in our country, by creating a generation of aspirational role models and growing demand from women and girls to play. Hosting a World Cup would give us the chance to build on that across all four nations.”

For Wales and Northern Ireland in particular, the tournament represents a first. Northern Ireland missed out on Euro 2028 matches after the UK government declined to fund the redevelopment of Casement Park, while Wales has never staged an event of this scale.

Noel Mooney, Chief Executive of the Football Association of Wales, said, “Wales has been a football nation for 150 years and we have never hosted anything on this scale. World Cup football played here, in front of Welsh children, would change what this game looks like in Wales: in the clubs, in the schools, and in the number of girls who grow up seeing a pathway into it.”

Ian Maxwell, Chief Executive of the Scottish Football Association, said, “The impact would go far beyond just the matches themselves. The level of investment into coaching, facilities and player pathways in the years beforehand will shape the future of the game for the generations to come.”

The vote caps a run of major tournaments heading to the UK, with England, Scotland, Wales and the Republic of Ireland co-hosting the men’s Euro 2028. The same Congress is also set to approve the joint bid from the US, Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica for 2031, the first Women’s World Cup to feature 48 teams.

title: Liverpool swap Standard Chartered logo for Play On
article_text:
Liverpool’s men’s and women’s teams have replaced Standard Chartered’s front-of-shirt logo with the Play On message, using one of the most visible sponsorship assets in world sport to tackle girls dropping out of sport.

Liverpool Women wore the Play On shirts against Chelsea on 21st November, followed by the men’s team against Manchester United at Anfield on 22nd November. Before both fixtures, a giant 25m x 23m Play On shirt was displayed on the pitch at St Helens and Anfield.

The limited-edition match shirts are being signed and auctioned, with all proceeds from this year’s campaign going to LFC Foundation to fund programmes that help more girls stay in sport.

Standard Chartered also brought together organisations from across sport, business and civil society at Anfield to discuss how collective action can address the barriers girls face. Guests included representatives from UN Women, the International Working Group on Women and Sport, Liverpool FC and LFC Foundation.

Erica Kerner, Global Head of Brand Partnerships and Sponsorships at Standard Chartered, said, “Sport gives girls so much more than the opportunity to play. It can build confidence, resilience, teamwork and leadership skills that can open doors throughout their lives. Yet girls still drop out of sport at twice the rate of boys by the age of 14. Through Play On, we’re leveraging the power and reach of our partnership with LFC to shine a light on this issue, connecting brands and organisations to create more opportunities for girls to fulfil their potential on and beyond the pitch.”

Kate Theobald, SVP of Global Partnerships at Liverpool FC, said, “Our long-standing partnership with Standard Chartered has always been about more than football, and Play On is a great example of how we can work together to make a meaningful difference. Since launching the initiative in 2023, we’ve continued to build on its impact, using the club’s global reach and the strength of our partnership to raise awareness of the barriers girls face in sport and encourage positive change.“

Theobald continues,“We’re incredibly proud of what we’ve achieved together through Play On over the years, and particularly pleased that this year’s campaign will directly support LFC Foundation and its work to create more opportunities for girls to stay involved in sport. It’s another important step in our shared commitment to making a lasting difference.”

Launched in 2023, Play On is part of the London-headquartered bank’s wider sporting portfolio, which expanded last week when Standard Chartered became a Formula 1 Global Partner from 2027.

title: ITV lands Invictus Games Birmingham 2027 rights
article_text:
ITV will be the exclusive UK broadcaster of the Invictus Games Birmingham 2027, with Birmingham’s own Alison Hammond and Paralympian Ade Adepitan co-hosting the opening and closing ceremonies.

The Games run from 10th to 17th July 2027 and will bring together 550 competitors from 26 nations across 12 adaptive sports, alongside 1,100 family members and supporters. A further 30,000 spectators are expected each day.

ITV’s free-to-air coverage will include both ceremonies, daily highlights programmes and exclusive digital content across ITVX, ITV YouTube and ITV’s social channels. Livewire Pictures will produce the host broadcast, covering all 12 sports and the ceremonies for audiences worldwide.

The deal was confirmed on ITV’s This Morning, where Prince Harry, The Duke of Sussex, appeared alongside former competitors Josh Boggi and Jules Bale. The appearance also marked key milestones in the build-up, including the launch of general sale tickets, volunteer recruitment and the growth of the INSPIRE education programme, which has now engaged nearly 50,000 young learners.

Prince Harry, The Duke of Sussex, Patron of the Invictus Games Foundation, said, “Queen Elizabeth Hospital in Birmingham was the place where so many of our competitors, who were critically wounded in Iraq and Afghanistan, woke up. So the first people they would see were the nurses and doctors in Queen Elizabeth Hospital. For them to come back with me and go back there was a really brilliant moving moment. Hundreds of British soldiers were treated at Queen Elizabeth Hospital. So for them to be going back to the Games in that city means a lot. I don’t think there’s a city in the UK that means so much to them. It’s the right place for it.”

Birmingham was chosen to host because of its long connection to the recovery and rehabilitation of the Armed Forces community. The city is home to Queen Elizabeth Hospital Birmingham and the Royal Centre for Defence Medicine.

Katie Rawcliffe, Director of Entertainment, Reality & Daytime Commissioning at ITV, said, “The Invictus Games is such a beloved event and, we couldn’t be prouder at ITV to be the exclusive UK broadcaster. Our extensive coverage will extend across ITV, ITVX and ITV YouTube for our viewers to enjoy free-to-air, ensuring they do not miss a minute of the action.”

Vicky Gosling, Chair of Invictus Games Birmingham 2027, said, “Having ITV as our exclusive broadcast partner is a major milestone for Birmingham 2027. ITV’s commitment reflects the strength of the Invictus Games, the importance of the stories we have to tell and the appetite among UK audiences to hear them. Together, we can bring the recovery journeys of wounded, injured and sick service personnel and veterans to millions of people, building understanding and support for the community at the heart of our Games.”

This news come after Invictus Games Birmingham 2027 confirmed the continuation of its partnership with Ottobock, which will provide technical support for competitors during the Games in the UK.

title: England's Freeman in contention for All Blacks rematch
article_text:
England wing Tommy Freeman is in contention for Saturday's Nations Championship play-off meeting with New Zealand.

The 25-year-old has been a key part of England's backline this year, starting nine Tests in a row for before being rotated out of the side for their comprehensive win over Japan on 14 November.

He was due to return for the 37-12 win over the All Blacks on Saturday, but a thigh issue forced his withdrawal in the hours before kick-off.

Harlequins' Cadan Murley was called into the side to replace Freeman and impressed in an emphatic England performance.

Head coach Steve Borthwick has bolstered his back-three options, which also include Gloucester's Will Joseph, by calling up Saracens' 20-year-old Noah Caluori.

Caluori, who finished as joint-top try scorer in last year's Prem alongside Freeman, crossed on his England debut against Fiji in July and was a late replacement in the win over Argentina a week later.

He also scored two tries in a England A's win over an Argentine equivalent earlier this month.

Fly-half Fin Smith, who came off 55 minutes into the win over the All Blacks with cramp, is also in a 37-strong squad who have gathered at England's training base to prepare for Saturday's third-place play-off.

England finished a point short of France in the northern hemisphere standings of the new format, missing out on a place in Sunday's Nations Championship final against South Africa.

The result of England and New Zealand's meeting, along with the weekend's other five matches at Twickenham's Allianz Stadium, will contribute to a Ryder Cup-style points race for the inaugural hemisphere shield.

title: South Africa win 'sets us up nicely'
article_text:
After Ireland's win over world champions South Africa on Saturday, Andy Farrell had one eye on the past, and another on what is to come.

It was a result that had left Ireland's head coach brimming with pride, as they ended a run of six straight defeats against either the Springboks, New Zealand or France.

With the World Cup now just 10 months away, it is all part of the bigger picture as Ireland aim to progress past the quarter-finals for the first time, with the ultimate goal of lifting the Webb Ellis Cup.

"Whether we lose by three or win by three, you understand how you apply yourself in a big game like that, and it doesn't get any bigger," Farrell said after the 20-17 win.

"You're always trying to kick on to the next level, and sometimes you don't know what that level is because you've never been there as a group.

"But this group is like that. We're trying to do new things together, and it sets us up nicely to keep kicking on."

Farrell looked back to the opening three matches of the Nations Championship in July, when he handed a number of players minutes at international level against Australia and Japan - such as Nick Timoney, Tom Stewart and Tom Clarkson.

Those players played a key role in downing the Springboks in Dublin as second-half replacements.

"We chose to take players to the Southern Hemisphere who had not had that type of experience.

"It's never going to be smelling of roses in that regard [performances over 80 minutes], so you end up where you're at, but we grew as a group, so therefore it's priceless for us."

Given how the tables were weighted, Ireland would have topped the southern hemisphere table by two points.

But the northern hemisphere's domination of the inaugural competition meant a more condensed table, and a fifth-place play-off against Australia will be their reward.

But Friday will be another tough test against a Wallabies side who were one missed penalty away from beating Ireland in Sydney in July.

Speaking before he knew who Ireland would be playing, and when, Farrell denied that playing for fifth place would be an anti-climax.

"You can only deal with what's in front of you," he said.

"We've got another week of international rugby together. We're in the green shirt, and that's special and it's a privilege, so we'll look forward to that."

Ireland's team selection to face South Africa had a surprise as captain Dan Sheehan, who usually plays at hooker, was named to start at number eight.

It was only his second professional start in the back row, with his first outing coming for Leinster against Munster before the international window.

Farrell's decision was certainly justified as Sheehan more than played his role in a scrum that held its own against the world-leading Springbok pack.

"He's so calm, isn't he? I spoke to him over the last couple of weeks about all sorts of things, about number eight, but he wasn't worried and it doesn't bother him in the slightest," said Farrell.

"It's like, 'why are you asking me that question?'. It's almost like an insult. He's so calm, he's such a gifted rugby player.

"That's his character. He just sees it for what it is and he gets on with it. That calm and influence has a knock-on effect that goes through the team."

Another standout for Ireland was Jamison Gibson-Park, whose experience and guile helped the hosts get over the line as the Boks piled on late pressure.

One clearing kick, from his own try line to the halfway line, was a particular standout in a game filled with classy moments.

Farrell described the 34-year-old's kicking as "immense", and said he is getting better with each passing year.

"He got us out of trouble so many times. You almost expect it from him, but you shouldn't," said Farrell.

"He is growing the whole time. I've never seen him in this good of nick, it just shows the hunger that he's got.

"That's what we've got within our group as well, we've got senior players who are constantly working so hard to continue to get better."

title: Rennie gets backing despite All Black defeats
article_text:
All Blacks head coach Dave Rennie has received the unequivocal backing of his bosses at New Zealand Rugby to lead the team through to next year's World Cup.

Rennie's side have suffered back-to-back defeats in the November leg of the Nations Championship and have lost five times in the calendar year for the first time since 1998.

"We have complete confidence in Rens," NZR chief executive Steve Lancaster said.

"His position is not in question. He will take the team to the World Cup. That is not going to change."

Rennie was appointed in March and started his All Blacks tenure in style, dispatching France and Ireland in the July part of the Nations Championship before a memorable victory over world champions South Africa in the Springboks' spiritual home of Ellis Park.

But New Zealand lost the next three Tests against the Boks to fall 3-1 in the 'Rugby's Greatest Rivalry' [RGR] series, and, although two convincing wins over Australia retained the Bledisloe Cup, the All Blacks have endured a difficult tour of Europe.

A first loss to Wales in 73 years was followed by an English rout in Twickenham, while the All Blacks have also been hit by the tragic death of their long-serving head of security Logan Cadwallader.

The emotional toll of Cadwaller's passing along with the arduous schedule this year are thought to be two mitigating factors behind the dip in form, and New Zealand's administrators will review the impact of the RGR series when planning its return in 2030.

Lancaster added that the union will look to make a call in the middle of next year as to whether Rennie takes charge of the team beyond the 2027 World Cup.

"We will conduct a full campaign and season review following this year, as we always do," he said.

"That will inform how we approach next year, but it will also inform our discussions around what the contract situation looks like beyond next year.

"Our intention is to make all those decisions and have clarity before we go into the World Cup. Nothing has changed from when we appointed Rens earlier this year.

"He is a world-class coach. We went through the most rigorous appointment process that I have been involved in, which included spending time observing him coaching in Japan with his team and in his environment."

title: Olympic silver medallist Krissy Scurfield confirms surprise career move
article_text:
Canadian Olympic silver medallist Krissy Scurfield has confirmed an unexpected next step of her career.

In 2027 the 23-year-old will link up with NRLW’s North Queensland Cowboys for one season.

Scurfield made her debut for Canada Sevens as a teenager and was part of the squad that finished second at the 2024 Olympic Games in Paris, although she did not play in the final after she was hospitalised with a lacerated kidney.

It is expected that Scurfield, who plays wing in the 15-a-side game, will play outside back in rugby league.

“We’re thrilled to welcome Krissy to the Cowboys,” Ricky Henry, Cowboys NRLW head coach, said.

“She’s a highly talented athlete whose success on the international stage speaks for itself.

“Krissy’s desire to test herself in the NRLW highlights her competitive mindset and ambition to keep improving.

“We’re excited to see the positive impact she can have on our squad and the competition.”

During one season with JAECOO Premiership Women’s Rugby club, Loughborough Lightning, Scurfield scored 14 tries in 12 appearances and was included in the league’s 2024/25 Team of the Season.

While with Lightning, the 23-year-old played with current Cowboys full-back Fran Goldthorp, who has represented the Townsville club since 2023.

The Leeds-born back played in all three of England’s Women’s Rugby League World Cup fixtures in October as they exited the tournament at the group stage.

Scurfield is not the first Canadian to have represented an NRLW team, that piece of history is that of Megan Pakulis, and marks an intriguing development in her career.

Scurfield has been named in the Canada Women’s Sevens squad for the opening two legs of the new HSBC SVNS Series season in Dubai and Cape Town.

Canada have been named in Pool B with Fiji, Japan and the Black Ferns Sevens. Last season Canada finished fifth in the SVNS Series and third after three HSBC SVNS World Championship tournaments.

This season a top-four finish will guarantee qualification for the 2028 Olympic Games in Paris.

title: Nations Championship reveal match officials for Finals Weekend
article_text:
Englishman Karl Dickson will lead a multi-national team of officials in the inaugural Nations Championship final between France and South Africa on Sunday.

The former Harlequins scrum-half has refereed two Nations Championship fixtures to date, which both ended in wins for France – 42-26 v Australia in July and 54-17 v Fiji in November.

The 44-year-old refereed in his first Rugby World Cup in 2023 and has five Six Nations Championships behind him in the role, with this weekend’s clash the latest headline fixture in an officiating career that began 12 years ago.

Dickson will be assisted on the day by Andrew Brace (Ireland) and James Doleman (New Zealand), with Andrew Jackson (England) as Television Match Official and Richard Kelly (New Zealand) as the Foul Play Review Official.

Nic Berry (Australia) gets the Finals Weekend underway when he takes charge of the sixth place final between Italy and Fiji on Friday, before Nika Amashukeli (Georgia) referees Ireland v Australia in the third place final.

Luke Pearce then oversees the fifth place final between Wales and Japan on Saturday in his first test at Allianz Stadium, with Angus Gardner (Australia) to then referee England v New Zealand in the second place final.

Pierre Brousset (France) will be in the middle for the fourth place final between Scotland and Argentina in the opening match on Sunday, before Dickson referees a test at Allianz Stadium for the first time as France and South Africa battle it out to be the first to lift the Nations Championship trophy.

World Rugby will be supporting its Social Impact Partner, ChildFund Rugby, with visibility across match officials’ jerseys during the Nations Championship.

title: Dave Rennie delivers blunt verdict on All Blacks' Rugby World Cup hopes
article_text:
All Blacks head coach Dave Rennie remains confident his side has the game plan, coaches, and players to win next year’s Rugby World Cup in Australia, despite two worrying defeats to Northern Hemisphere sides in the Nations Championship.

The 62-year-old head coach has come under pressure in the past two weeks, after his side failed to beat Steve Tandy’s Wales in Cardiff, before stumbling against England last weekend to record back-to-back losses for the second time in 2026.

Both the All Blacks and Springboks have recorded several defeats after the brutal seven-game Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry series earlier in 2026, as the sides feel the effects of four physical Test matches.

But Rennie, who admitted the group had more than enough reasons to produce a bounce-back performance against England, still believes his side has what it takes to lift the Webb Ellis Cup in Sydney next November.

“Yep,” Rennie said about the All Blacks’ Rugby World Cup prospects.

“We’ve used just about 60 players, so we’ve learnt a lot. Really rapt with the effort from these men, and disappointed with yesterday, but an opportunity to finish strong.

“We’ll have a bit of time through Super Rugby to reassess [the plan]. But we know a lot about these men, and I reckon we’ll be able to put together a really strong squad heading into the international window and then the World Cup.”

While the performance will clearly “hurt” the All Blacks for several weeks, Rennie acknowledged his coaching staff have their work cut out for them to get the players to deliver the necessary response this weekend against England.

“Yeah, it still hurts a lot, and so yeah, it doesn’t matter whether you’re an experienced player or a young player, results and performances like last night hurt.

“We’ve seen that in the group, and to be honest, our job is going to be to get them up and get them up quickly because we’ve got a front again in six days, so we’ll learn our lessons.

“But we’ve got to find a positive way of channelling all that energy into a quality performance on Saturday.”

The All Blacks head coach, who took the role in March, said his side’s effort is there, but the performance was far from accurate enough.

“We get a chance to play England again from a redemption point of view.

“But look, I don’t have an issue with the effort. But we got to be a lot more accurate, and there were so many elements of our game that we didn’t get right last night, and you get dealt to from a good side.

“So yeah, look, we’ve got to be better, but I’m confident that we’ll bounce back.

“We‘re going to [have] be a lot better than we were last night. We defended well for big blocks, and had to defend a lot, and in the end, fell off a fair few tackles compared to England.

“We turned over double the amount of ball that they did, and we had half the amount of possession that they had. So all those things add up to a tough night, but we’re not looking for excuses.”

title: Good news for Steve Borthwick as key England duo get all clear
article_text:
Winger Tommy Freeman has been named in England’s 37-man training squad in preparation for Saturday’s rematch with New Zealand despite missing last weekend’s clash.

The Northampton try machine was pulled out of England’s starting line-up and replaced by Cadan Murley on the eve of the record 37-12 win over the All Blacks after picking up a thigh injury in training. But the injury wasn’t deemed serious enough to rule him out of contention for England’s last Test of the year.

However, Saracens flyer Noah Caluori has been brought into an otherwise settled training group, presumably as a precaution.

Fly-half Fin Smith has also been given the green light to train, having suffered from cramp during Saturday’s match.

Uncapped Harlequins back-rower Jack Kenningham could potentially make his Test debut if head coach Steve Borthwick decides to shake things up for a game that seems suited to experimentation.

Borthwick names his team on Wednesday with a sixth successive Test victory the target as England look to confirm their emergence as World Cup contenders next year.

title: Poor ticket sales threaten to blight Nations Championship finals opening night
article_text:
Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

Sluggish ticket sales look set to blight the first night of the Nations Championship finals at Twickenham this weekend.

Friday’s double-header featuring Italy v Fiji and Ireland v Australia appears on course to be played out in front of a crowd of less than half the stadium’s 82,000 capacity.

The tournament’s official ticket website is showing swathes of tickets still available in most sections with the exception of the top tier, which is expected to be closed.

Officials acknowledged earlier this month that sales could be an issue, with fans having to wait until last weekend to discover the finalised schedule for the three-day showpiece.

Tickets for Saturday’s two games – Wales v Japan and England v New Zealand – are much stronger, and they are also better for Sunday, when Scotland play Argentina before South Africa and France contest the final.

Earlier this month, RFU chief executive Bill Sweeney admitted Twickenham was in “unchartered waters” with regard to the ticket sales for the inaugural tournament, which brings together all the major northern and southern hemisphere nations.

Speaking prior to its opening weekend earlier this month, Sweeney added: “This is the first time we’ve done this.

“A lot of fans are waiting to figure out who is playing who and when. You’ve got to go through those pool matches before you know you you’re playing on finals weekend. It’s a bit like a condensed World Cup.”

title: South Africa make seven changes for Nations Championship final against France
article_text:
Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

South Africa have made seven changes and one position swap for the Nations Championship final against France at Twickenham on Sunday, with a potential debut off the bench for loose-forward Emmanuel Tshituka.

Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu moved to full-back for the injured Damian Willemse and is replaced at fly-half by Manie Libbok. Cobus Reinach will start at scrum-half.

The rest of the backline remains the same with Damian de Allende and Jesse Kriel the centres, and Ethan Hooker and Kurt-Lee Arendse on the wing.

The back row of the scrum is also unchanged with captain Siya Kolisi and Pieter-Steph du Toit the flankers alongside number eight Cameron Hanekom.

Salmaan Moerat comes in at lock alongside Lood de Jager, and there is ‌a new front row of hooker Jan-Hendrik ‌Wessels, and props Gerhard Steenekamp and Thomas du Toit.

DR Congo-born Tshituka, whose brother Vincent is a Springbok, could debut off the bench, which has a six-two split between forwards and backs.

"We are disappointed in our last two games because we were not as effective as we should have been in a few areas of the game, and that cost us," suspended coach Rassie Erasmus said.

France beat the Springboks 21-19 in Paris in a pool match this month.

South Africa XV: 1 Gerhard Steenekamp, 2 Jan-Hendrik Wessels, 3 Thomas du Toit; 4 Salmaan Moerat, 5 Lood de Jager; 6 Siya Kolisi (captain), 7 Pieter-Steph du Toit, 8 Cameron Hanekom; 9 Cobus Reinach, 10 Manie Libbok; 11 Ethan Hooker, 12 Damian de Allende, 13 Jesse Kriel, 14 Kurt-Lee Arendse; 15 Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu.

Replacements: 16 Malcolm Marx, 17 Ox Nche, 18 Wilco Louw, 19 Eben Etzebeth, 20 Paul de Villiers, 21 Emmanuel Tshituka; 22 Morne van den Berg, 23 Canan Moodie.

title: Springboks duo make World Rugby men’s player of the year shortlist
article_text:
Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

Springboks duo Malcolm Marx and Ox Nche have been named on the shortlist for World Rugby’s men’s player of the year.

Marx, last year’s winner, could become the third player to claim the prestigious award in back-to-back seasons, while teammate Nche is bidding to become the first prop to win it.

Marx would join Richie McCaw (who won in 2009 and 2010) and Beauden Barrett (in 2016 and 2017) in an elite group of consecutive winners, as well as Dan Carter and Pieter-Steph du Toit as multiple-time victors.

France and Bordeaux Begles winger Louis Bielle-Biarrey, the Six Nations Player ‌of the Championship in 2026, and New Zealand centre Jordie Barrett complete the shortlist.

France players Fabian Brau-Boirie and Aaron Grandidier-Nkanang have been shortlisted for World Rugby's breakthrough player of the year award, alongside South Africa’s Paul de Villiers and Japan flyhalf Ryunosuke Ito.

New Zealand’s Kaipo Olsen-Baker won the women’s player of the year award last month.

The men’s winners will be announced during the Nations Championship Finals at ‌Twickenham this weekend, with France taking on South Africa in the inaugural showpiece, while England face a rematch against New Zealand after a remarkable thrashing of the All Blacks on Saturday.

Ireland take on Australia, who narrowly squeezed past Wales, with Argentina facing Scotland, Wales playing Japan and Italy facing Fiji.

title: Jannik Sinner: Former world No 1 to undergo knee surgery in Finland and doubt for Australian Open in January
article_text:
Former world No 1 Jannik Sinner is set to undergo surgery on his troublesome knee which is likely to see him miss the Australian Open in January, according to Sky in Italy.

The surgery, performed by Lasse Lempainen, one of the world's leading specialists in tendon and muscle injuries, could sideline the Italian for three to four months.

Sinner last played at Wimbledon, where he defeated Alexander Zverev in the final to claim his fifth career Grand Slam title.

The 25-year-old stated earlier this month that he expects to make his official return at the Australian Open following a planned appearance at the Six Kings Slam in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, in late December.

"The goal is to go to Australia; I hope to get there, and perhaps play a few tournaments beforehand," Sinner told media in Milan.

Despite playing only nine tournaments, Sinner compiled an astonishing 44-3 match record (93.6 per cent win rate), where he captured six titles and reclaimed the world No 1 spot during a 30-match winning streak.

He sealed maiden titles in Indian Wells, Monte-Carlo, and Madrid to become only the second man in history [after Novak Djokovic] to win all nine ATP Masters 1000 tournaments.

However, Sinner did not feature in another competitive match after beating Alexander Zverev in four sets to secure his second consecutive Wimbledon title in July, with persistent inflammation in his right knee forcing him to miss the North American hard-court swing, including the US Open.

He shut down his season in October and earlier this month Sinner parted ways with coach Darren Cahill with Magnus Norman poised to replace the Australian.

Due to an extended absence from the tour, Sinner is likely to apply for a protected ranking which would mean he would be able to play in tournaments without having to go through qualifying.

title: Jannik Sinner’s estimated recovery timeline from knee surgery revealed – report
article_text:
With Jannik Sinner reportedly set to undergo surgery on his knee, the world No 2’s lengthy absence from the tour looks likely to extend beyond the start of 2027.

A right knee injury has prevented Sinner from playing since he defeated Alexander Zverev in the Wimbledon final in July.

Sinner has not shared details about the specific nature of his knee injury, but it has been reported that the issue he is dealing with is iliotibial band syndrome (ITBS).

Earlier today, Italian newspaper Il Messaggero reported Sinner was set to travel to Finland for an operation on his right knee on Tuesday.

Graziano Urbani, who wrote the article, claimed Sinner’s surgery will rule him out of the 2027 Australian Open.

“This decision inevitably alters the Italian’s plans and extends his recovery timeline: Sinner will not participate in the Australian Open,” Urbani wrote (translated from Italian).

Want more from Tennis365? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for tennis coverage you can trust.

“The goal of returning to action in Australia — a prospect he had been working toward over the last few weeks — has therefore definitively slipped out of reach.”

Angelo Mangiante, a journalist for Sky Sport Italy, confirmed the news about Sinner’s decision to undergo surgery.

“He will be operated on by surgeon Lasse Lempainen, an orthopaedic specialist of international renown considered one of the world’s leading experts in tendon and muscle injuries,” Mangiante wrote on Twitter/X.

“The surgery will take place in Turku, where Jannik will arrive today. The condition, as is well known, is tendinopathy on the outside of the right knee, known as iliotibial band syndrome.”

On Sinner’s estimated recovery timeline, Mangiante added: “Recovery is estimated to take 3-4 months, so he could return for the clay-court season after the American tournaments. But that is obviously just a possibility.”

Earlier this month, Sinner divulged he was hoping to make his comeback in time to play the 2027 Australian Open.

“The goal is to go to Australia; I hope to get there, and perhaps play a few tournaments beforehand,” said the five-time Grand Slam champion.

Sinner won the first five Masters 1000 tournaments in 2026 before he defended his Wimbledon title.

title: Carlos Alcaraz makes Davis Cup Finals decision as he gives injury update after ATP Finals victory
article_text:
Carlos Alcaraz has confirmed whether he is still planning to play at the 2026 Davis Cup Finals after his maiden triumph at the ATP Finals.

The seven-time major champion prevailed 6-2, 7-6(7) against world No 1 Alexander Zverev in the final at the season-ending championships in Turin.

At the age of 23, Alcaraz has become the youngest player in history to win the ATP Finals and all four Grand Slam tournaments.

Alcaraz secured the title in Turin with a perfect 5-0 record despite suffering a left hamstring injury in his second round robin match against Daniil Medvedev.

After the final, Alcaraz revealed he is planning to lead his country at the Davis Cup Finals in Bologna this week.

“I’m really looking forward to trying to complete the tournaments I have left,” the world No 3 said in his Spanish press conference.

“The Davis Cup is something very important to me. I’ll try to get to Bologna as ready as possible physically. It’s going to be a very, very nice week, and one I’m really looking forward to.”

Want more from Tennis365? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for tennis coverage you can trust.

The Spanish star said he had not considered withdrawing from the ATP Finals due to the hamstring issue.

“Obviously, it is true that the tests came at a time when I was already qualified. That helped me,” Alcaraz said. “The tests came back fine, which meant we could compete.

“Withdrawing or not being on the table was something that had not been considered, but we really didn’t know how we would cope and how the days would go after the test, after the last group match, after the semi-finals.

“The body can react in any way and we had to be ready for everything. That kind of decision, that kind of thought, that uncertainty is what made this week a little more difficult than it should have been.”

The former world No 1 also hailed the importance of his team.

“I had a big part of my team here, a big part of my family, who calmed me down, who gave me the desire, who gave me peace of mind, and that has been a fundamental part of me being here today with the trophy,” he added.

Spain will face Austria in the Davis Cup quarter-finals on Thursday.

title: Alexander Zverev sets unfortunate year-end No 1 record despite winning two Grand Slam titles
article_text:
The 2026 ATP Tour season is officially over, and it is Alexander Zverev who sits at the top of the world rankings after a career-defining year for the German.

Heading into 2026, Zverev was one of the greatest ‘nearly men’ of the sport, falling in three Grand Slam finals despite winning an array of Masters 1000 titles, two ATP Finals, and Olympic gold back in 2021.

However, the 29-year-old’s fortunes at the majors improved dramatically over the past twelve months, with the German battling his way to a first Grand Slam title at the French Open in June, beating Flavio Cobolli in the final.

That was then followed by a second major triumph later in the season, with Zverev defeating Ben Shelton in four sets to lift the US Open title in Septmeber.

Those results helped Zverev debut as the world No 1 earlier this month, and also helped him seal the year-end No 1 ranking ahead of Jannik Sinner and Carlos Alcaraz.

However, despite breaking new ground in 2026, Zverev has now set a rather unfortunate record in the ATP Rankings.

Want more from Tennis365? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for tennis coverage you can trust.

Outside of his victories at Roland Garros and the US Open, Zverev was also the runner-up to Sinner at both Wimbledon and the Madrid Open in 2026. He was also a beaten finalist at the ATP Finals this past week, falling to Alcaraz in the championship match.

Though he tasted success at two Grand Slam tournaments, they proved to be the only titles that the 29-year-old won across the season, and that is now the least amount of titles won in a year by the ATP’s year-end No 1 since the ATP Rankings first launched in 1973.

Prior to Zverev, the record for the least number of titles won by a year-end No 1 was four, jointly held by Novak Djokovic (2018 and 2020), Rafael Nadal (2019), Roger Federer (2009), and Pete Sampras (1998).

The record for the most titles won by a year-end No 1 was set in the very first year of the ATP Rankings, with Ilie Nastase — the first No 1 in ATP history — winning a staggering 16 tour-level titles in 1973.

The two players with the most singles titles won on the ATP Tour in 2026 are world No 2 Sinner and world No 3 Alcaraz, who both won six titles across the year.

Zverev was able to finish the season as the year-end No 1 ahead of both men in part due to his consistency at the Grand Slam tournaments. He banked 2,000 points at both the French Open and US Open, 1,300 points for reaching the Wimbledon final, and 800 points for reaching the semi-final of the Australian Open.

That means Zverev earned 6,100 ranking points from the Grand Slams this year, contributing to his overall total of 10,350 points for the season.

While Zverev banked consistent points across the four majors, Sinner and Alcaraz did not. World No 2 Sinner won Wimbledon and reached the last four of the Australian Open, though lost in round two of the French Open and missed every tournament post-Wimbledon due to injury — including the US Open.

Meanwhile, Alcaraz lifted the Australian Open title in January and was a quarter-finalist at the US Open, though four and a half months out with injury saw him miss both the French Open and Wimbledon, alongside a string of further tournaments.

Ultimately this record is not entirely Zverev’s fault, with the rankings system and injuries to two of his main rivals not exactly in his control.

However, the German will likely have to win more titles in 2027 if he wants to hold on to his world No 1 ranking.

title: Blockbuster Coco Gauff doubles partnership teased by Taylor Townsend ahead of LA 2028 Olympic Games
article_text:
Taylor Townsend has revealed that she and Coco Gauff intend to pair up and go for gold in the women’s doubles event at the Los Angeles 2028 Olympic Games.

It is now only a year and a half until the Summer Olympics head to Los Angeles, in what will be a home games for Townsend, Gauff, and the rest of the potential US tennis squad.

Both Gauff and Townsend represented their country in the Billie Jean King Cup this past weekend, with the USA easing their way to a 4-0 victory over Hungary to progress to next year’s qualifiers.

The USA were 2-0 up after a strong Saturday, with Gauff defeating Dalma Galfi and Ann Li beating Anna Bondar in the opening women’s singles rubbers in Florida.

World No 4 Gauff and Townsend then paired up for the women’s doubles and sealed the decisive victory on Sunday, defeating Galfi and Bondar 6-4, 6-3 before Ashlyn Krueger saw off Adrienn Nagy in a dead rubber.

Victory for Townsend saw her cap off a stunning year on the doubles court, completing the Career Grand Slam alongside Katerina Siniakova thanks to triumphs at the French Open and US Open, as well as claiming victory at the WTA Finals.

With Townsend and Czech Siniakova unable to play together at the Olympics, it now appears that the doubles world No 2 will be pairing up with Gauff for their home games.

Speaking in press after the USA’s victory, Townsend teased that she and Gauff had begun the process of developing their partnership ahead of LA 2028.

She said: “The only thing that was going through my mind, honestly, is like I hope these people are enjoying [this] because this is the partnership for 2028 Olympics, so you know they’re getting a chance to be able to see a sneak peek.

“Hopefully we’ll have some more opportunities to be on the same side of the net with each other because I always really enjoy it.”

A two-time Grand Slam singles champion, Gauff is also a hugely accomplished doubles player. Much like Townsend, she is a former doubles world No 1, and she won the 2024 French Open doubles title alongside Siniakova.

Speaking after her victory alongside Townsend this weekend, she opened up about how playing with her compatriot was an enjoyable experience.

“The few times that we have played, playing with Taylor has been so fun. She has a unique skill of being able to uplift you on court,” added the 21-year-old.

“She is already one of the greats and will definitely go down as one of the greats, so being able to learn from and play with her has been so fun.”

Gauff previously competed at the Paris 2024 Olympic Games, when she memorably got to be the USA flagbearer at the opening ceremony alongside Lebron James.

However, she was unable to claim a medal, falling in the third round of the women’s singles, the second round of the women’s doubles alongside Jessica Pegula, and the quarter-final of the mixed doubles alongside Taylor Fritz.

Townsend has never previously competed at the Olympics, with the 30-year-old potentially in line to make her debut at the prestigious event.

The USA will be eligible to achieve up to 12 quota places for LA 2028, which would include four spots in both the men’s and women’s singles, as well as two pairings in both the men’s and women’s doubles, and one pairing for mixed doubles.

title: Alex Eala’s return to WTA Tour event confirmed as 2027 schedule begins to take shape
article_text:
Alex Eala’s schedule for the 2027 WTA Tour season continues to take shape, with the Filipina confirmed for a return to the Abu Dhabi Open next season.

The Abu Dhabi Open will take place from January 30th to February 6th 2027, and currently looks set to be Eala’s third event of the season.

World No 15 Eala is already confirmed to be starting her season at the Auckland Open in early January, where she will look to better this year’s run to the semi-final, before competing at the Australian Open — the opening Grand Slam tournament of 2027.

The WTA 500 event in Abu Dhabi will take place directly after the Australian Open, with Eala reaching the quarter-final of the tournament on her second event appearance this past February.

The Filipina defeated Zeynep Sonmez and Aliaksandra Sasnovich to reach the last eight before losing to second seed Ekaterina Alexandrova, the eventual runner-up.

Want more from Tennis365? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for tennis coverage you can trust.

Eala had previously received a wildcard into the tournament while still a teenager back in 2024, losing to Magda Linette in the opening round.

With the tournament sharing a sponsor with the Washington Open, the tournament Eala memorably won this summer, all eyes will be on whether she can achieve a similar level of success.

In a statement, Eala said: “Returning to Abu Dhabi for my third Mubadala Abu Dhabi Open is something I’m really looking forward to, especially as they celebrate the tournament’s fifth anniversary.

“The energy from the Filipino community and the fans across the UAE makes competing here that much more special. I’ve continued to grow and develop myself as a player, and I’m excited to bring that experience back to Abu Dhabi this year on my favourite surface on tour. It’s always a privilege to compete alongside such a talented field and in front of such energetic crowds.

“The crowds that came and watched me last year were electric and it was an event I loved participating in. After the triumph at the Mubadala DC Open this summer, hopefully I can bring the same luck with me in the UAE capital.”

So far, she is the only player confirmed for the Abu Dhabi Open field, though the tournament traditionally attracts high-profile players. Aryna Sabalenka, Elena Rybakina, and Belinda Bencic have all won the title since the event was first launched in 2021.

Sara Bejlek won the title in 2026, beating Alexandrova in the final.

The Abu Dhabi Open will likely be the first of three events for Eala in the Middle East Swing, with the first two WTA 1000 events of the year also held in February.

Following the Abu Dhabi Open, the first WTA 1000 event of the year will be the Qatar Ladies Open in Doha, which will itself then be followed by the second WTA 1000 event of the season at the Dubai Tennis Championships.

Eala will be targeting a strong campaign after a career-best year, cracking the top 20 for the first time and ending the season at a new high of 15th in the WTA Rankings.

title: Denmark claim only European title as Korea and Chinese Taipei dominate Scottish Open
article_text:
Europe had several finalists at the Scottish Open, but Kristoffer Kolding/Mette Werge were the only Europeans to leave with a title as Korea and Chinese Taipei claimed the remaining four.

Kolding/Werge (3) secured the mixed doubles title in an all-Danish final against compatriots Jesper Toft/Amalie Cecilie Kudsk, winning 21-19 13-21 25-23.

Germany also had two pairs in the finals. Stine Küspert/Isabel Lohau finished runners-up in women's doubles, while Daniel Hess/Simon Krax reached the men's doubles final. Both pairs were beaten by Korean opposition, with Seung Hee Lee/Park Min Ji winning 21-17 21-16 and Jin Sung Ik/Lee Hyeong Woo taking the title 14-21 22-20 21-7.

Croatia's Aria Dinata also reached the men's singles final, but Chinese Taipei's Ting Yen-Chen proved too strong, winning 21-9 21-14.

Korea collected three titles in total, with Kim Min Ji also winning the women's singles final against compatriot Park Ga Eun 20-22 22-20 21-19.

The Scottish Open therefore ended with three titles for Korea, one for Chinese Taipei and one for Denmark, the sole European winner of the tournament.

title: Anders Antonsen claims Hong Kong Open title without playing final
article_text:
Denmark's Anders Antonsen secured his third BWF World Tour title of 2026 on Sunday, but not quite in the way he had hoped. The Dane was crowned Hong Kong Open champion after his final opponent, Kunlavut Vitidsarn, was forced to withdraw due to injury.

The highly anticipated men's singles final between Antonsen and Thailand's Kunlavut Vitidsarn never took place, as the Thai star withdrew with a back injury before the scheduled match.

It was an unusual ending to an otherwise impressive week for Antonsen, who had battled his way through several challenging matches to reach the final.

Speaking to Danish broadcaster TV 2 Sport, Antonsen expressed his disappointment at missing out on the opportunity to face Vitidsarn.

"It's frustrating. It's very anticlimactic. I had been looking forward to today's match so much. I was really excited and thought it would be a great experience, and, as so many times before, a thrilling match against Kunlavut Vitidsarn. This wasn't the way I had hoped to win," Antonsen told TV 2 Sport.

The Dane survived a thrilling quarterfinal against China's Zhu Xuan Chen, winning 21-18, 14-21, 24-22, before delivering a convincing 21-13, 21-13 victory over India's Lakshya Sen in the semifinals.

Although the title came without a final being played, the result adds another trophy to Antonsen's collection ahead of the season-ending BWF World Tour Finals in December, where he will be joint by follow europeans Christo Popov and world champion Alex Lanier.

While the men's singles final was never played, the remaining four finals produced their champions on Sunday.

In women's singles, China's Wang Zhi Yi successfully defended her title, defeating Thailand's Pornpawee Chochuwong 21-16, 21-11.

Malaysia celebrated two titles, with Man Wei Chong/Tee Kai Wun winning the men's doubles against Indonesia's Leo Rolly Carnando/Daniel Marthin 21-19, 21-18.

Their compatriots Pearly Tan/Thinaah Muralitharan also claimed the women's doubles title, defeating Japan's Sumire Nakade/Miyu Takahashi 22-20, 21-16.

Finally, China's Feng Yan Zhe/Huang Dong Ping secured the mixed doubles title after a three-game victory over compatriots Jiang Zhen Bang/Wei Ya Xin, winning 17-21, 21-9, 21-15.

title: RSM Classic Full Prize Money Payout 2026
article_text:
The final PGA Tour event of the season, the RSM Classic, is drawing to a close at Sea Island, Georgia.

Because of its status as the last of the FedExCup Fall events, there is more at stake this week than in many other tournaments.

Finnish player Sami Valimaki is defending the title he won a year ago.

Meanwhile, many other players have another priority, namely securing their full PGA Tour card for the 2027 season.

For those not otherwise exempt, the tournament offers the final opportunity for players to secure their places in the top 100 of the FedExCup standings, with several notable names on the bubble at the start of the week.

As a result, it could be argued that the prize money is less important to some players than the potentially career-defining perks at stake.

However. there are still ample opportunities for those who made the cut to boost their bank balances by a substantial margin, with $400,000 more than what was on offer a year ago.

Back then, Valimaki picked up a check for $1.2 million from an overall payout of $7 million.

This year, $7.4 million is on the table, with the winner set to claim prize money of $1.332 million.

If a player finishes solo second, he will earn $806,600, while everyone in the top 19 is in line for a six-figure payout.

After a washout on Saturday, the tournament is due to finish on Monday. At the 54-hole stage, Rasmus Hojgaard and Michael Thorbjornsen co-led at 13-under.
