title: Peter Finch's DP World Tour Invite Is Not 'Pathetic'
article_text:
News of Peter Finch's sponsor's invitation into the upcoming AfrAsia Bank Mauritius Open unsurprisingly caused plenty of discussion on social media, and it's perhaps an instant example of how the decision has already been a success.

Golf Monthly's news story has had over 145,000 views on X in just a few days with over 70 replies and quote-tweets, including from the man himself who admitted there had been "quite the range of comments."

The platform formerly known as 'Twitter' is not always regarded as the friendliest of places and, while there was plenty of support for the YouTube giant, there was inevitably some 'hate' dished out following the news of his DP World Tour debut.

The man with over 850,000 subscribers' invite "deprives a hard working pro and his family the chance to earn a living," one user wrote, while there were some harsher calls of "pathetic", "joke" and an "embarrassment."

The news comes amid the European circuit agreeing sponsor invite deals with nine ex-LIV Golfers, so the subject of DP World Tour invites and making life harder for the DPWT rank-and-file is a current topic of significant debate.

A news story on defending champion Jayden Schaper or two-time Masters champion Bubba Watson committing to the event would not have received anywhere near the views, which I think illustrates the struggle certain tournament officials are facing.

The golfing calendar is incredibly packed and it's tough for events like the Mauritius Open to stand out when there's another three or four on in the same week and then another three or four more the next week. That's not to even mention YouTube Golf, Netflix, other sports, streaming and the rest of the internet that tour events are having to compete with.

Subscribe to the Golf Monthly newsletter to stay up to date with all the latest tour news, equipment news, reviews, head-to-heads and buyer’s guides from our team of experienced experts.

The Mauritius Open features one of the most naturally beautiful settings of the season but it has a low purse and a fairly weak field, so Finch's addition has obviously been made to increase eyeballs on what would usually be a fairly missable week.

We've seen YouTubers added to fields before on various global and we'll almost certainly see it again. Luke Kwon, Mac Boucher and 'Taco Golf' received Asian Tour invites, while Brad Dalke made the cut at this year's BMW International Open on the DP World Tour, the same tournament which invited the Bryan Bros last year.

PGA Tour winner, Wesley, was also joined in the field by his brother, George, at the PGA Tour's Bermuda Championship in 2024. The pair also played in last year's International Series Philippines event on the Asian Tour.

So YouTubers being invited is nothing new, and the only thing new here is the man in question. Peter Finch will be making his debut on the DP World Tour and I for one am very much looking forward to tuning in.

Would I have been watching the opening round of the Mauritius Open without his participation? I can't say for sure that I would, and that will be the same for many.

Thursday and Friday tour golf is intriguing but not exactly the most gripping, and having Finch there for at least the first two days will inevitably increase viewership. It will also lead to plenty of social media coverage before the event, too.

A user replied to our post that Finch will likely shoot 78-78 and miss the cut while another stated he "isn't anywhere near good enough." I would like to challenge those as the Englishman undoubtedly has some serious game and has shown plenty of signs in recent years that he can hang with the pros.

Just two months ago, Finch finished T6th in a Tartan Tour event, which is an OWGR-sanctioned circuit.

The PGA Professional ended just six strokes off the lead at the Fairmont St Andrews Classic, where a certain Michael Stewart missed the cut. Stewart then finished T4th at the Alfred Dunhill Links Championship on the DP World Tour just a month later.

Finch reached Final Qualifying for the Open Championship, after winning his regional event, last year. Also in 2025, he made the cut at the Asian Development Tour's Egyptian Open, and he has had plenty of high level experience from competing in the Q at Myrtle Beach in recent years.

Making the cut might look unlikely, but it's certainly not a foregone conclusion that he will just turn up and go home early. His invite undoubtedly adds intrigue to an event that is crying out for some extra attention, and I will be one of many cheering him on to make the weekend.

And finally, Finch is hardly taking the spot of a pro who has earned their way into the field.

The Mauritius Open is not the best-supported event of the season by any means, with almost all of the tour's top players skipping it. Last year, 11 sponsor's invitations were handed out and Finch will be one of these in 2026.

Sponsor's invites are undoubtedly controversial, but when there are so many up for grabs it seems harsh to be critical when one is given to someone who will genuinely adds to the TV and digital numbers.

What do you make of Finch's sponsor's invite? Let us know your view in the comments section. And will he make the cut? Find out on golfmonthly.com next month.

title: Emma Raducanu Joins Uniqlo’s Commitment to Keep U.K. Families Warm This Winter
article_text:
LONDON — U.S. Open champion Emma Raducanu joined Uniqlo’s charitable effort to support families facing hardship in the U.K.

The Uniqlo global brand ambassador visited Little Village in Camden, where she met families, staff and volunteers, just as the retailer marked its donation of 16,800 Heattech items to 29 baby banks this year.

The visit, held around World Children’s Day on Nov. 20, was part of the retailer’s Heart of LifeWear initiative and its ongoing partnership with Save the Children.

During her visit the brand said Raducanu spoke with a mother and her 4-year-old daughter about the support they had received from the baby bank. She also helped volunteers pack personalized bundles, which included Heattech clothing donated by Uniqlo alongside hygiene products, baby equipment, toys and books.

“Today has been a chance to see how the program can make a genuine difference to families, and how everyday clothing like Heattech can bring warmth, comfort and support when it is needed most,” Raducanu said.

The U.K. donation forms part of a broader effort across Europe. The fashion label under Fast Retailing has vowed to donate more than 100,000 Heattech items to charities for the third consecutive winter.

Save the Children has partnered with Uniqlo globally for more than four years. In Europe, the partnership has expanded over the past three years through fundraising, product donations and local initiatives.

The charity is a founding member of the Baby Bank Alliance, a network of more than 270 baby banks in the U.K. that provide families with essentials free of charge. In 2025, baby banks supported 210,000 families and 400,000 children.

As reported, Uniqlo named Raducanu its latest global brand ambassador earlier this year. The British tennis player joins a roster that includes Roger Federer, Kei Nishikori, Adam Scott and Ayumu Hirano. Raducanu is the roster’s only woman and its fifth tennis player.

The appointment is intended to extend beyond the court. Uniqlo has developed an initial tennis dress for Raducanu, but she will also wear and represent the brand off court, reflecting the brand’s LifeWear positioning around clothing for different parts of everyday life.

Clare Waight Keller, Uniqlo’s creative director, said the company had long wanted a woman athlete on its ambassador team. She described Raducanu as an exciting choice for connecting with younger customers and aspiring athletes.

“The way Emma conducts herself, and her confidence, but addressing struggles too — I think a lot of young people do struggle — and so the nice balance for us is that it feels very authentic and very real, and that’s what we love so much,” Waight Keller added.

title: LIV Golf could make shock return as former player reveals intriguing takeover rumour
article_text:
Former LIV Golf player Travis Smyth has claimed the defunct breakaway tour could yet return in the future.

The circuit filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in the United States in September, and officially collapsed earlier this month after a proposed $300m restructuring deal with a London-based credit firm fell through.

BC Partners Credit had demanded that a minimum number of marquee players sign new contracts by late October to finalise the rescue package, before walking away when several star names opted to leave the tour.

Smyth, 31, played in the inaugural LIV event at Centurion Club in 2022 and made eight further appearances as a reserve - including four starts this season - despite never holding a full-time team contract.

While the Australian did not win an individual title on the circuit, he was part of victorious teams alongside Bryson DeChambeau's Crushers GC in Korea and the all-Australian Ripper GC side in the UK this summer.

Speaking to Fox Sports Australia ahead of this week's Australian PGA Championship at The Lakes in Sydney, Smyth suggested BC Partners head Ted Goldthorpe has not completely abandoned hopes of a revival.

"I still wish it was around," he said. "I loved it. I believed in it. I thought it was great fun as a player.

"Travelling to those countries, it meant that I could be in Sydney, Australia a little bit more. I love that sort of idea. I kind of envisioned that a little bit. But it's gone now. I don't know for what reasons.

"I guess ultimately the bigger players, not enough of them signed up for whatever reason. But hope it comes back.

"Actually I heard a rumour that the leading investor dude, Ted [Goldthorpe], from BC Partners, is still trying to buy it, so it might come back in the future."

Reflecting on his time competing on the circuit, Smyth added: "My experience was amazing, obviously.

"I was playing at the time [on the] Asian Tour, a tour that only feeds into LIV. The only pathway forward. So that's what I was always striving for.

"I'm super grateful that I got to play. On Bryson's team with a win, on Ripper's team with a team win, had a top 10 myself in one of those starts, so it was an amazing experience."

The New South Wales native was also quizzed on LIV's lavish spending. It's understood the Saudi PIF ploughed more than $5bn into the venture.

"I don't even know if the Saudis cared how much they would spend," Smyth said.

"I don't really know if that model being sustainable was even like a concern.

"But from all reports, the way it was going to be next year, was that it was structured to be a sustainable product, and it would have made it work.

"I don't think we'll ever see a golf tour the way that it was before with the Saudis just going all out.

"Because it felt like there was just so much wasted money, so much, just everything going on at those tournaments."

Following the demise of LIV Golf, Smyth has secured playing privileges on the DP World Tour and plans to contest roughly 26 tournaments over the next 12 months.

"Now DP [World Tour] and the Asian Tour have sort of got back together and so over the next 12 months, I'll focus on DP and I'll get to play the co-sanction events in Asia, so I'll get my starts up there," he said.

"I feel like it's all just sort of mixing in perfectly.

"I'll pretty much play every event that I can possibly get into on the DP schedule.

"I'm going to go to Mauritius after Aussie Open.

"Then if I don't get into certain events and there happens to be an Asian Tour event or a Japan Tour event, I might go play.

"But I think my category is going to get a lot of starts in DP and I'm gearing up to play, I don't know, 26 events for the year."

title: Talor Gooch is now facing a very harsh reality as LIV Golf folds
article_text:
It was five years ago this week that Talor Gooch secured his first win on the PGA Tour, as he won The RSM Classic by three shots.

Less than two years later, Gooch was declaring himself one of the best players in the world after a superb season on LIV Golf in which he won three times.

As the 2026 season concludes, however, the 35-year-old finds himself facing an incredibly long road back to the PGA Tour.

And crucially, there are few signs to suggest that he is ready for the challenge.

Gooch is one of the most successful players in LIV Golf history. His four victories helped him earn more than $72 million in prize money.

Nevertheless, he became a figure of ridicule for many of the league’s biggest critics.

There was no shortage of comments made by those associated with LIV Golf that did the league no favours whatsoever during its existence.

But one of the most infamous claims came from Gooch following a LIV event at Pumpkin Ridge in 2022 in which he suggested that the atmosphere was not too dissimilar to what you would see at a Ryder Cup or Presidents Cup.

Of course, it did not help Gooch had played in neither event.

Who do you think will be golf's breakout star in 2027?

The PGA Tour and DP World Tour both look incredibly strong next year!

Meanwhile, in 2023, Gooch claimed that he was one of the best players in the world after clinching the individual title for the season on LIV. In fairness, he had won three times that year, so that comment was a little more understandable.

His status did not help earn him an invite for The Masters the following year. Nevertheless, he went on to hit the headlines for suggesting that there would be an asterisk against Rory McIlroy‘s name if he completed the Career Grand Slam that year at Augusta National due to the fact that some of the best players on LIV were missing from the event.

It should be noted that Gooch has played in six majors since LIV Golf’s first ever event in 2022. He has missed the cut three times and never finished higher than 34th.

He took on a leadership role with LIV at the start of 2026 following Brooks Koepka‘s departure from the league. And his captaincy led to Smash being rebranded as OKGC during the season.

Of course, LIV Golf is now no more. But while many are waiting to see what the future holds for the likes of Bryson DeChambeau, Jon Rahm, Dustin Johnson, and Cam Smith, there appears to be virtually no chatter about what is next for Gooch.

He won four times in total and is third on LIV’s all-time money list. He was apparently one of the best players in the world for a spell.

And yet, you would have been forgiven for not even noticing that he was missing from the list of players who have struck a deal with the DP World Tour for the 2027 season.

Perhaps he will still receive some invites to DP World Tour events next season. But it is seemingly going to be extremely difficult for Gooch to regain his PGA Tour card for 2028 as things stand.

There was undoubtedly a time when Gooch was one of LIV’s biggest success stories. However, the silence concerning what comes next for him may say everything about his current status in the game.

title: Rick Shiels hits back after brutal dig from LIV Golf executive
article_text:
Rick Shiels has laughed off some brutal criticism aimed towards him during LIV Golf’s bankruptcy court proceedings after the league’s collapse.

The YouTube star, who boasts over three million subscribers and participated in this year’s $4million Internet Invitational, is one of the creditors owed money following LIV’s demise.

Shiels signed a strategic partnership with LIV at the start of 2025, promoting the league’s events as an official ambassador by filming videos with players at tournament venues.

But when the Saudi Public Investment Fund withdrew its funding from LIV at the end of this season, several of the league’s highest paid employees had not been paid the totality of their original contracts.

And it emerged in court documents that England-based Shiels was owed $1.4 million on his multi-year-deal. When asked why Shiels was owed that sum, LIV’s Chief Restructuring Officer David Orlofsky offered a cutting response.

“As I understand it, Rick Shiels is some sort of golf influencer, but I have never heard of him,” Orlofsky said. “So I couldn’t tell you much about him, but apparently his job was to write stuff and publicize stuff about the events.

“And because he has supposedly a following, people were supposed to – there’s supposed to be some value he added there. I couldn’t pick him out of a lineup.”

Responding to this quote later on Instagram, Shiels wrote, “Unbelievable” alongside a laughing face emoji. “David who?” he added.

In an exclusive interview with TG last year, Shiels explained his reasons for joining LIV, two years after conversations initially started with the breakaway league. He said that the opportunity to travel the world, bolster his team and have access to players like Jon Rahm and Brooks Koepka ultimately became irresistible.

But Shiels is not the only one who is now owed money after the LIV taps were turned off. While players were the biggest creditors, several small UK businesses have taken a hit after being left unpaid from the doomed $5 billion project.

According to invoices seen by the BBC, Global Infusion Group, a catering company in Buckinghamshire, near London, is owed roughly $420,000. BD365 Clean, a Suffolk-based cleaning agency, is owed just shy of $100,000. The company’s owner Krissi Foskett described the unpaid bills as “sickening”.

“How can they sleep at night,” Foskett told the BBC, “knowing they are potentially putting companies out of business?”

Meanwhile, Goodysphere, a family-run business that provides a sensory bus designed to help autistic children that might find events overwhelming, is still owed around $4,000.

title: LIV Golf Secures $2.2 Million From UK Travel Firm as $700,000 Dispute Continues
article_text:
LIV Golf's bankruptcy estate is set to receive approximately $2.2 million from Corporate Travel Management (United Kingdom) Limited following an agreement reached between both parties in the league's ongoing Chapter 11 proceedings.

A consent order filed in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the District of New Jersey requires the travel services company to transfer the money to LIV Golf's debtors within seven days of the order's entry. The agreement resolves part of a dispute over funds held by the company.

However, approximately $700,000 will remain with Corporate Travel Management while the parties continue to resolve their respective claims. The development was highlighted by David Rumsey, who shared details of the court document on X.

LIV Golf Set to Receive $2.2 Million From Corporate Travel Management

The court order concerns a motion filed by LIV Golf's debtors against Corporate Travel Management (UK) Limited, also known as CTM. The motion sought to enforce the automatic stay, compel the return of debtor funds and impose sanctions against the travel company.

Both parties reached an agreement to resolve the motion without an admission of liability or a court decision on the merits of their respective positions.

Under the terms of the consent order, CTM must transfer approximately $2.2 million to LIV Golf's debtors. The payment must follow written wire instructions provided by the debtors' legal representatives.

The order also states that the transfer will be in full and final satisfaction of all rights and claims between the parties concerning those particular funds. CTM will not be entitled to recover any portion of the transferred money for any reason.

The parties can also agree in writing for some or all of the money to be sent in pounds sterling to a UK account designated by LIV Golf's debtors. The actual amounts transferred in the relevant currencies will determine the payment, rather than the approximate US dollar figure.

However, the order does not mean the entire dispute between LIV Golf and CTM has been settled. The agreement only addresses the funds covered by the $2.2 million transfer.

While CTM has agreed to return approximately $2.2 million, the company is permitted to retain the remaining funds, estimated to be worth around $700,000.

The court order allows CTM to hold the money while the parties' respective rights are determined through the claims-allowance process in LIV Golf's Chapter 11 cases, another appropriate legal proceeding or a further written agreement.

However, CTM cannot transfer, use or otherwise dispose of the retained funds without an order from the court or an agreement with LIV Golf's debtors. Any agreement to release the money must also satisfy the consent requirements involving the debtor-in-possession lender.

Importantly, the court has not decided whether LIV Golf or CTM is entitled to the remaining $700,000. The order also does not allow CTM to use the money to satisfy any claim it may have against the debtors without further court approval or a written agreement.

The latest agreement therefore gives LIV Golf a route to recover approximately $2.2 million while leaving another significant portion of the disputed funds unresolved.

The seven-day transfer requirement will be the next important step, while the remaining $700,000 will continue to depend on the outcome of the parties' claims or a further agreement.

title: Syed Modi: Depth of Home Talent in Focus
article_text:
The next generation of India’s women’s singles shuttlers take centrestage with the Syed Modi India International 2026 beginning Tuesday in Lucknow.

While Indian icon Pusarla V Sindhu won’t be in action, several of those seeking to follow in her footsteps will be geared up for what promises to be an intense week. India have nine women’s singles players in the top 50; apart from Pusarla, the others are in action in Lucknow.

Among those evoking interest will be world No.47 Rakshitha Sree Santhosh Ramraj, who was relatively unknown until a week ago. That changed in the space of two days at last week’s LI-NING Hong Kong Open 2026 when she first took down Mia Blichfeldt, followed by the even bigger upset of Chen Yu Fei. Ramraj is in the top quarter, and will expect to run into top seed Riko Gunji in the second round.

Among other Indian prospects are second seed and world No.21 Tanvi Sharma, winner of the YONEX Taipei Open; No.23 Unnati Hooda, winner of the Polish Open; VICTOR Korea Masters winner Ashmita Chaliha, and Thailand Masters winner Devika Sihag.

Then there are other prospects like Isharani Baruah, Anmol Kharb, Malvika Bansod and Shriyanshi Valishetty, among others, who have had some memorable performances this season.

Tanvi Patri, who fell in a dramatic final at the Youth Olympics recently, will play the qualifying draw.

In men’s singles, second seed Lee Zii Jia will draw the most attention, particularly after he made the semifinals of the CLASH OF CLANS Arctic Open 2026.

Teh Jia Heng heads the draw; for home fans, No.3 seed HS Prannoy and eighth seed Tarun Mannepalli will shoulder the hopes of home fans.

title: India at 2026 BWF World Tour with Nine Titles as Lakshya Sen, Sindhu Lead Resurgence
article_text:
India has secured nine BWF World Tour titles across Super 750, Super 500 and Super 300 tournaments in 2026, placing 11th in the global standings.

Lakshya Sen, PV Sindhu and the doubles combination of Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty have led India's campaign, which reflects a significant improvement in the country's international badminton performances.

India's badminton campaign in 2026 has witnessed a notable resurgence, with players across singles and men's doubles contributing to a nine-title haul on the BWF World Tour. While the country currently occupies 11th position in the overall national standings, its performances at the Super 750 and Super 500 levels underline the growing competitiveness of Indian badminton.

According to the latest title standings through November 22, India has won three Super 750, three Super 500 and three Super 300 titles. However, the absence of a Super 1000 championship and titles at the Super 100 level has prevented India from making a stronger impact on the overall rankings.

China leads the standings with 57 titles, followed by South Korea with 17 and Chinese Taipei with 13. India's nine-title tally places it behind France, which has eight titles but a superior distribution of victories at the higher tournament levels.

Two of India's biggest singles stars, Lakshya Sen and PV Sindhu, have played central roles in the country's 2026 campaign. Sen has won two Super 500 titles, capturing the Hylo Open and Japan Masters during November. His consecutive victories towards the end of the season have been particularly important, helping him secure qualification for the prestigious BWF World Tour Finals in Hangzhou, scheduled from December 9 to 13.

The Indian also came close to a major Super 1000 breakthrough at the All England Open, reaching the men's singles final before losing to Chinese Taipei's Lin Chun-yi 15-21, 20-22.

That defeat highlighted the narrow margins separating Sen from the biggest titles on the international circuit. Nevertheless, his November performances have demonstrated his ability to compete consistently against the world's leading shuttlers. Sindhu has also enjoyed an encouraging season, winning the Japan Open (Super 750) and Hylo Open (Super 500). Her return to the winner's podium at two different tournament levels has been an important development for Indian women's badminton.

Together, Sen and Sindhu have contributed four of India's nine titles, demonstrating the importance of experienced international campaigners in the country's overall performance.

India's men's doubles combination of Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty has delivered two Super 750 titles in 2026. The pair won the Singapore Open and China Masters, reinforcing their position among the world's leading men's doubles combinations.

Their victories have been particularly valuable because India has struggled to produce comparable results in other doubles disciplines this season. Despite the success of Satwik and Chirag, India has not secured a single World Tour title in women's doubles or mixed doubles across the completed tournaments.

This remains an important area for improvement, especially considering the strength of countries such as China, South Korea, Malaysia and Indonesia in the doubles categories.

India's nine championships have been distributed across three tournament levels and three playing categories.

One of the encouraging aspects of India's campaign has been the emergence of younger women's singles players.

Devika Sihag won the Thailand Masters, and Tanvi Sharma captured the Taipei Open, while Ashmita Chaliha claimed the Korea Masters title. These victories demonstrate that India's women's singles depth extends beyond established names such as Sindhu. The emergence of younger champions is particularly important as the country builds towards the Los Angeles 2028 Olympic cycle.

The national standings use a tier-based ranking methodology rather than simply ordering countries by their total number of trophies. Super 1000 titles carry the highest priority, followed by Super 750, Super 500, Super 300 and Super 100 championships.

This explains why Canada occupies ninth position with just two titles, ahead of France and India, despite both countries having higher overall trophy counts. France is ranked 10th with eight titles, including four Super 750 championships. India follows in 11th position with nine titles but only three Super 750 victories.

China's dominance is driven by its extraordinary depth, particularly in women's doubles and mixed doubles. South Korea, meanwhile, has relied heavily on An Se-young and its successful men's doubles combinations.

For India, the absence of a Super 1000 title remains the biggest gap. Sen's All England final appearance and Satwik-Chirag's Super 750 success show that the country is capable of challenging at the highest level, but converting those performances into the biggest titles remains the next objective.

India still has opportunities to improve its overall title tally before the 2026 season concludes. The Syed Modi International, scheduled in Lucknow from November 24 to 29, will be followed by the Guwahati Masters from December 1 to 6 and the Odisha Masters from December 8 to 13.

These tournaments provide opportunities for Indian players to add to their championship count, particularly in the Super 300 and Super 100 categories. However, under the existing tier-based ranking methodology, additional Super 300 and Super 100 victories cannot bridge India's deficit to France, which has four Super 750 titles compared to India's three.

The BWF World Tour Finals in Hangzhou will therefore be particularly significant for the final standings, with Lakshya Sen representing India's challenge. India's nine-title campaign is already a considerable improvement on its position entering the closing stages of the previous season. With five of its nine victories coming in women's singles and two each in men's singles and men's doubles, the results also reveal the areas where the country has developed the most.

title: Meta inks 49ers sponsorship, will give away AI glasses
article_text:
The 49ers have signed Silicon Valley neighbor Meta to a sponsorship described by parties as a “landmark multiyear partnership,” which will emphasize the company’s high-end version of is A.I. glasses.

The newly created category for Meta is “official moment maker” of the 49ers. At launch, the signature activation will be a giveaway of Oakley Meta HSTN glasses to more than 4,700 49ers suite holders and club season ticket holders to celebrate the 80th anniversary of the franchise. Oakley, an NFL sponsor, typically sells the product at for $399 or more.

Also, Meta’s Whatsapp messenger app will become the “official instant messenger provider” of the 49ers, intended to support the team’s global marketing efforts in the U.K., UAE and Mexico in the NFL’s global markets program.

In a prepared statement, 49ers COO Brent Schoeb said “Innovation and technology are part of our franchise’s DNA,” making the connection logical. We ... look forward to seeing the content they create with Meta’s AI glasses.“ Financial terms were not disclosed.

Also, Meta will be the presenting sponsor of the 49ers’ military “Salute to Service” campaign, with a dedicated focus on blind and low-vision veterans. Meta will receive digital signage at Levi’s Stadium in the deal.

Meta has signed 49ers FB Kyle Juszczyk as a brand ambassador to support the sponsorship.

Meta’s current sports sponsorship portfolio includes the UFC and Arsenal F.C. The team negotiated the deal with Meta directly.

title: Why MLB could be the first major league to move its championship to streaming
article_text:
It’s not a question of if, but when the first major American professional sports league puts its championship exclusively on a streaming service. Based on timing and the value of that championship, Major League Baseball is in the perfect position to make that decision, but only if it chooses.

Streaming services have quickly become major players in the American sports media rights space. Prime Video now has rights to the NFL, NBA, and NASCAR. Peacock is saturated with MLB, NBA, Premier League, and basketball and football from the Big Ten. Netflix has rights to MLB and NFL, and will exclusively air the 2027 Women’s FIFA World Cup in the United States and Canada (and could soon secure rights to the 2030 men’s World Cup).

But none of those rights include championship games, except Netflix and the Women’s World Cup. The NFL, MLB, and NBA have gone as far as to put playoff games on streamers (the entirety of the 2027 NBA Eastern Conference Final will air on Prime Video), but the Big Four leagues have not gone all the way yet.

There is good reason to believe, however, that could soon change. Both the NHL and MLB will see their media rights expire after the 2028 season (if there is a lockout, the MLB contracts could go through 2029). Streamers have already shown interest in both leagues. NHL games air on ESPN Unlimited and Hulu, while MLB games stream across Netflix, Peacock, and Apple TV.

With the NFL and NBA locked into relatively longer contracts, based on timing alone, the league to make the streaming jump first for its championship could be the NHL or MLB.

The NHL’s public comments have already tipped their hand; not necessarily that they are about to deal the Stanley Cup Final to a streamer, but that they are looking for a significant media rights increase, 50% to 100% more, according to CNBC. The NHL currently makes around $650 million annually from its U.S. media contracts.

While MLB has not indicated so publicly, the league will likely look for an increase in a similar range. That has been the norm in media rights recently. The NBA’s latest contracts saw an increase more in the range of 150%.

One of the reasons the NBA was able to get such an increase is that the league was willing to put key inventory on streaming. Games on Peacock and Prime are key components of the NBA’s agreement. As previously mentioned, both services air playoff games, and Prime goes as far as the conference finals.

The other key reason the NBA got its increase was competition. ESPN, Prime, NBC, and TNT were four media companies competing for three packages. Having more bidders than packages drove up the price for the NBA. If either league truly wants to maximize its next national deal, it needs to incentivize competition for its key media rights packages. Allowing streamers to bid on their championship inventory could be that incentive.

MLB has already carved out a streaming package of key rights for Netflix, featuring Opening Night, the Home Run Derby, and a special-event game. The league has shown a willingness to put important inventory on streaming already, which could signal a willingness to shop the World Series.

But why MLB instead of the NHL? MLB has more to gain because the World Series is more popular than the Stanley Cup Final. This year’s World Series averaged 11.83 million viewers on Fox; the Stanley Cup Final averaged less than half that, 5.27 million viewers on ABC (which was the most-watched since 2019).

MLB has also historically been far more reliant on revenue from the collapsing local TV business than the NHL, NFL, and NBA. A 2023 Sportico report found that local media, including radio, accounts for 23% of MLB team revenue. With revenue from the regional sports network business drying up, MLB will have more incentive to maximize its national media rights revenue.

There are some clear risks for MLB if it goes down this path, however. By going to streaming, MLB would make its games less accessible and likely hurt its viewership, at least in the near term. The reach of broadcast television is still unmatched for live sports viewership, though streamers have closed the gap in recent years for major events like Netflix’s Christmas Day games or Prime Video’s Thursday Night Football.

There’s also the PR nightmare moving the World Series to streaming would create. Whichever league moves its championship to a streamer first is going to have to put up with some very angry fans and some terrible press coverage. Polling shows that Americans are extremely unhappy with sports fragmentation, and that was with no league championships on streaming.

Not to mention, the federal government has taken interest in slowing the shift of live sports from broadcast to streaming. MLB, like other pro sports leagues, enjoys a federal antitrust exemption that could be put in jeopardy should the league make an aggressive move towards streaming.

So, there is no guarantee that either the NHL or MLB will move their championships to a streamer, even on a partial basis. The NHL may be wary because of its decision to split the Stanley Cup Final between over-the-air television (ABC) and cable (TNT) has not paid off from a viewership standpoint.

But with national media rights becoming even more important, and the World Series still holding incredible value, the league will at least consider selling it to a streamer, if only to test the market.

title: F1 sponsors focus on contract terms as average deals hit $8.1M
article_text:
F1 sponsors focus on contract terms as average deals hit $8.1M

Ampere Analysis forecasts that Formula 1 sponsorship spend will top $3 billion in 2026. The average F1 deal costs nearly four times the average NBA or NFL deal. Qualcomm CMO Don McGuire says the old advertising-value-equivalency math has been upended. He says brands should structure deals around their end goals rather than promises of exposure.

This story was produced through MarketScale. See how Sports & Entertainment teams put it to work with Events & Onsite Capture.

Ampere Analysis forecasts that F1 sponsorship spend will pass $3 billion in 2026, up 15% on last season and 66% since 2022. Business Insider's Lara O'Reilly reported those figures along with a harder question from the marketing chiefs writing the checks: with this many logos on the grid, what does any one of them actually buy?

The people closest to these deals keep pointing to the contract. That suggests the rights a brand negotiates could matter more than the exposure it gets.

The scale is both the problem and the pitch. F1 now has more than 400 sponsorship partners, an average of 34 per team, and the average deal costs nearly four times the average NBA or NFL deal. A buyer paying that premium shares the car, the kit and the paddock with dozens of other brands.

Business Insider cited a 2024 academic paper finding that sponsors were more likely to renew when their team performed well, and that a larger sponsor roster was linked to a higher chance that individual brands would leave. Tim Crow, a longtime sports-marketing consultant, said F1's huge global audience includes fewer passionate fans than football or NASCAR, so brands have to work harder to stand out.

The audience still explains why brands keep paying. F1 says its global fan base reached 827 million in 2025, up 12% on the prior season, and that 43% of fans are under 35 and 42% are women. Few properties offer that mix on a calendar that runs most of the year and crosses continents.

Qualcomm CMO Don McGuire told Business Insider he sees some brands overpaying for F1 rights, which makes the market messier for everyone else. His second point matters more to anyone building a measurement plan. The old advertising-value-equivalency math has been upended, he said.

Other big sports buyers are taking a closer look too. McDonald's recently said it would end a 32-year FIFA World Cup partnership, and Heineken said last year it would end its 30-year UEFA Champions League sponsorship in 2027. Neither is an F1 deal. Both show that long-running sponsorships now face the same review as any other large line item.

McGuire's advice is to structure the deal around the brand's end goals rather than promises of exposure, and Qualcomm's own renewal shows how that works. When Qualcomm renewed with the Mercedes-AMG PETRONAS F1 Team earlier this year, McGuire pushed for a separate agreement with driver Kimi Antonelli. McGuire says F1 is delivering strong return for the company.

Ben Cronin, editor of SportBusiness Sponsorship, reported that the addition of Brazilian driver Rafael Câmara to Haas F1's driver lineup has unlocked a sponsorship deal with Bradesco, one of Brazil's largest banks. A driver's nationality and profile can open a market for the team and the sponsor at once. That makes the driver lineup a fair topic in any negotiation, not something to wait and see about.

In B2B deals the equivalent is hospitality. Misha Sher, founder of the talent-management and brand-marketing firm One of Not Many, explained the logic to Business Insider using Oracle's partnership with Red Bull. Oracle doesn't need 100 million viewers, he said. It needs 25 decision-makers to understand how it uses technology under extreme pressure.

For a B2B sponsor, the return on an average $8.1 million F1 deal could depend on who sits in the hospitality suite.

The categories growing fastest are the ones whose products can do a visible job for a team. Ampere reports that F1 sponsorship revenue from software companies has grown 65% since 2022 and 42% since 2025. Revenue from AI-native companies is up nearly 450% since last season. Sher said brands that show how their technology helps on track get the most traction, and he pointed to Oracle with Red Bull and to Google building its Pixel phones and Gemini into McLaren's work with drivers Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri.

SponsorUnited, via Motorsport.com; Ampere Analysis, via Business Insider

Motorsport.com, citing SponsorUnited, puts 2025 team sponsorship at $2.54 billion, up 22% on the previous year.

Three teams have signed wellness partners this year, Alex Harrington of Motorsport.com reported. The products are aimed as much at mechanics and engineers as at drivers, and Eight Sleep designs its beds for long-haul travel and time-zone changes. Because a wellness brand sells something fans can buy for themselves, the bigger prize could sit outside the garage, in fan activations that turn a team deal into consumer sales.

The model doesn't fit every buyer. For brands outside technology and automotive-adjacent industries, Crow said the numbers can be hard to make work. Lego and LVMH are his examples of brands that got through anyway. Lego built drivable cars for the 2025 Miami Grand Prix and the 2026 British Grand Prix. LVMH makes custom Louis Vuitton trophy trunks and supplies the Moët & Chandon the winners spray on the podium. Both made objects that became part of the race weekend.

New Zealand Rugby Union confirms Rennie as national team coach through 2027 World Cup — BBC Sport
article_text:
New Zealand Rugby Union has confirmed that Dave Rennie will remain head coach of the All Blacks through the 2027 World Cup. BBC Sport reports.

Union chief executive Steve Lancaster said that the organization has full confidence in Rennie and that his position is not in question. The union plans to decide in the middle of next year whether the coach will continue working with the national team after the 2027 World Cup.

New Zealand suffered two consecutive defeats in the November part of the Nations Championship. Overall, the All Blacks lost five times during the calendar year — for the first time since 1998.

Rennie took charge of the team in March. In the July Nations Championship matches, the New Zealanders beat France and Ireland, and also defeated the reigning world champions, South Africa, at Ellis Park.

More current news is available on the UA.News Telegram channel Telegram.

After the victory over South Africa, New Zealand lost to their opponents three times in the Rugby's Greatest Rivalry series and lost it 1-3. Two convincing victories over Australia allowed the All Blacks to retain the Bledisloe Cup.

At the same time, the European tour proved difficult: the team lost to Wales for the first time in 73 years and then suffered a crushing defeat to England at Twickenham by a record margin.

The team also experienced the death of long-serving security chief Logan Cadwallader. The BBC notes that the emotional impact of this loss and the demanding schedule of the year are considered factors that partly explain the decline in form. New Zealand rugby administrators will also review the impact of the Rugby's Greatest Rivalry series as they plan its possible return in 2030.

title: Rassie Erasmus recalls controversial Springboks star as two players depart
article_text:
The Springboks have made several changes to their squad ahead of the inaugural Nations Championship final against France this weekend.

Rassie Erasmus' side will be looking to put a difficult couple of weeks behind them after suffering consecutive defeats to France and Ireland.

However, despite those setbacks, South Africa still finished top of the southern hemisphere standings after the All Blacks also lost their final two matches against Wales and England.

There have been further setbacks for the world champions, with Erasmus handed a suspension following his criticism of the officiating in the defeat to France.

Meanwhile, Jasper Wiese has also been banned for an illegal clearout at the breakdown.

South Africa will now face France for a second time in a matter of weeks, with the Six Nations champions standing between them and the Nations Championship title.

The final will take place in London on Sunday.

Ahead of the showdown, Erasmus has been forced into a couple of changes to his squad, with two forwards ruled out through injury.

Springbok forwards Ruan Nortje and Ntuthuko Mchunu will return to South Africa after picking up injuries that make them unavailable for selection this weekend.

In response, Erasmus has called up experienced hooker Bongi Mbonambi, who is expected to join the squad in the UK on Tuesday.

The 82-cap international is a two-time Rugby World Cup winner and brings plenty of experience to the group, both on and off the field.

However, his inclusion is unlikely to go unnoticed given his recent controversies.

The hooker had been excluded from training and the Sharks' early URC matches while awaiting the outcome of the investigation. He subsequently departed the Durban-based club with immediate effect to rejoin the Stormers.

He also has a controversial history involving England.

During the 2023 Rugby World Cup semi-final between England and South Africa in Paris, flanker Tom Curry accused Mbonambi of directing a racial slur at him.

World Rugby launched an investigation but ultimately cleared the Springbok hooker, ruling that there was insufficient evidence to substantiate the allegation.

title: World Rugby Awards 2026 men’s nominees announced
article_text:
The nominees in the men’s categories have been unveiled for the World Rugby Awards 2026, recognising the players and moments that have defined the sport over the past calendar year.

With the women’s categories already presented at the end of the WXV Global Series in October, this year’s men’s shortlist spans three headline categories: International Rugby Players Association Try of the Year, World Rugby Breakthrough Player of the Year, and Player of the Year in partnership with Visa.

Each nominee for Breakthrough and Player of the Year has been voted by the World Rugby Awards panel, comprised of former legends of the game, Marcelo Bosch, Jacques Burger, Fiona Coghlan, Victor Matfield, Drew Mitchell, Ugo Monye, Kieran Read, Blaine Scully, and Dimitri Yachvili, ensuring that the highest accolades in the sport are a peer recognition reflective of both excellence on the field and inspiration off it.

The Men’s 15s Try of the Year nominees have been selected by members of the International Rugby Players Association, which represents the interests of professional rugby players worldwide. Fans will once again have the final say, voting for their favourite try on World Rugby’s website to decide the winner. Voting closes on Wednesday, 25 November at 17:00 GMT.

The recipients of the World Rugby Awards 2026 men’s categories as well as the Coach of the Year and Rugby for All Awards will be revealed across World Rugby’s digital platforms during the Nations Championship Finals Weekend (27-29 November), ensuring fans everywhere can share in the excitement of the end of the international window. In addition, the highly anticipated World Rugby Men’s 15s Dream Team of the Year will be unveiled on Monday, 30 November, showcasing the standout performers from across the rugby world.

Recognising the most spectacular tries scored on the international stage in 2026, celebrating the skill, creativity and teamwork behind the game’s standout moments. Nominees are:

The five nominees for the International Rugby Players Association Men’s 15s Try of the Year showcase some of the most spectacular attacking rugby of 2026. France captain Antoine Dupont was on the end of a breathtaking attack launched from inside his own 22 against Scotland in the Men's Six Nations, while New Zealand’s Peter Lakai finished a slick Bledisloe Cup move against Australia sparked by Jordie Barrett’s aerial take and Damian McKenzie’s break. England back-row Henry Pollock showed remarkable pace to burst through the Fiji defence and race clear in the Nations Championship, while Pita-Gus Sowakula finished an ambitious, flowing Fiji counter-attack from inside their own half against Wales. Completing the shortlist, Portugal’s Raffaele Storti finished a superb end-to-end team move against Tonga, with Tomás Appleton, Manuel Cardoso Pinto and Samuel Marques combining to send the wing over in the World Rugby Nations Cup.

Recognising emerging talents who have celebrated their first 15s international cap and made a significant impact on the international stage in 2026. Nominees are

The four nominees for World Rugby Men’s 15s Breakthrough Player of the Year have each made an immediate impact on the international stage in 2026. France centre Fabien Brau-Boirie marked his test debut with a try against Wales in the Men's Six Nations before starting against Italy and all three of France’s July Nations Championship matches, impressing with his ability to make metres through contact and offload in tight spaces. South Africa flanker Paul de Villiers seized his opportunity after being handed a test debut against England, going on to make eight appearances to date for the Springboks and scoring two tries while catching the eye with his work-rate and strength at the breakdown. France wing Aaron Grandidier-Nkanang has successfully made the transition from Olympic gold medallist in sevens to the test arena, scoring twice on debut against Australia and four tries in his first four internationals. Completing the shortlist is Japan fly-half Ryunosuke Itō who was thrust into test rugby before playing a professional match and has quickly established himself with composed performances against Italy, Ireland and France, before scoring his first international try against Australia.

Celebrating the individual who has consistently delivered world‑class performances and inspired fans across the globe during the 2026 international season. Nominees are:

The four nominees for World Rugby Men’s 15s Player of the Year in partnership with Visa reflect outstanding performances across the international game in 2026. New Zealand centre Jordie Barrett has combined his trademark physicality with outstanding distribution, contributing five try assists in ten test starts and helping the All Blacks retain the Bledisloe Cup. France wing Louis Bielle-Biarrey has continued his remarkable try-scoring form, crossing nine times in the Men's Six Nations and 11 times in eight tests to date, while again being named Men's Six Nations Player of the Championship. South Africa prop Ox Nché, shortlisted for a second successive year, has remained a cornerstone of the Springbok pack, featuring throughout their Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry series victory over New Zealand and scoring his first test try against Australia in Perth. Reigning World Rugby Men’s 15s Player of the Year Malcolm Marx completes the shortlist after another influential season at the heart of the world champions’ forward pack, scoring six tries in 10 tests while remaining a formidable presence at scrum, breakdown and with ball in hand.

title: Nations Championship: 40,000 empty seats on Friday?
article_text:
The first night of the Nations Championship finals could be played in front of some 40,000 empty seats, according to the Guardian. More than half the tickets were still available on Monday for Friday 27 November at Twickenham’s 82,000-capacity Allianz Stadium, and the upper tier is reportedly set to be closed.

That evening, Fiji v Italy opens the programme at 5.40pm (French time), followed by Ireland v Australia, the fifth-place play-off, possibly without Dan Sheehan. Sales are said to be better for the weekend, at 70% of capacity: the organisers hope to fill the stadium on Saturday, for England v All Blacks and Wales v Japan, and on Sunday, the day of France v South Africa, which follows Scotland v Argentina.

Supporters had to wait until the final round of the group stage, on Saturday, to find out which match their team would play, and on which day. Tickets start at £60 on the Friday (£20 for juniors), £100 on the Saturday and £125 on the Sunday (£50 for juniors). A ticket exchange has been opened for supporters who want to follow their team, so the number of empty seats on Friday could rise further still.

The organisers, Six Nations and Sanzaar, declined to comment on sales. Do the maths: 40,000 empty seats out of 82,000 is almost one seat in two. Television audiences are healthier: in England, ITV claims an average of 3 million viewers for its matches, and more than 4 million for Wales’ victory over the All Blacks.

title: Six Nations relegation decision confirmed for 2030 as Georgia push for promotion
article_text:
The Six Nations countries could face relegation from rugby's new Nations Championship from 2030, but their places in the annual Six Nations tournament will remain untouched.

That is the key distinction as rugby's leading unions continue discussions over promotion and relegation.

England, Ireland, Scotland, Wales, France and Italy are all guaranteed their places in the Six Nations Championship, regardless of their results.

However, those same countries could eventually face relegation from the Nations Championship, the new global competition featuring the world's leading international sides.

And that could open the door for Georgia.

Under the existing agreement, promotion and relegation between the Nations Championship and the second-tier Nations Cup are scheduled to begin in 2030.

According to The Guardian, the Six Nations' official position remains that promotion and relegation should be introduced.

However, the precise system has yet to be finalised.

Some of rugby's leading unions are reportedly concerned about the financial consequences of dropping into the second tier.

Wales and Italy are among the countries mentioned in discussions about possible safeguards.

For example, Wales could theoretically finish bottom of the Nations Championship and lose their place in that competition under the proposed system.

They would still compete against England, Ireland, Scotland, France and Italy in the Six Nations every year.

The same would apply to any of the other five countries.

It means relegation could have serious financial and sporting consequences without changing the make-up of Europe's historic annual tournament.

Georgia have spent years campaigning for greater opportunities against rugby's established nations.

Their historic 13-12 victory over Wales in Cardiff in 2022 demonstrated their ability to compete against Six Nations opposition.

However, that result did not give them a pathway into the Six Nations Championship.

The Nations Cup could eventually offer something different.

Under the proposed promotion and relegation arrangements, Georgia could earn a place in the elite Nations Championship through their performances.

They would not, however, replace Wales or Italy in the Six Nations.

World Rugby has established a review group, chaired by chairman Brett Robinson, to examine how promotion and relegation could operate.

RFU chief executive Bill Sweeney has confirmed that the principle remains part of the plans, although several details still need to be resolved.

Financial protection for relegated unions is understood to be one of the biggest issues.

For Georgia, the opportunity is significant.

After years of knocking on the door, they could finally have a route into rugby's top international competition.

But for now, the Six Nations itself remains a closed shop.

title: Springboks refuse to speak English in press conference after World Rugby ban
article_text:
South Africa assistant coach Mzwandile Stick conducted media duties in the isiXhosa language on Monday.

The Springboks are preparing for their Nations Championship final against France at Allianz Stadium Twickenham on Sunday and took the unconventional step of naming their team for the clash early.

And in another unusual turn of events, Stick spoke in the isiXhosa language at the team announcement via an interpreter - a journalist - to communicate with the assembled press pack in London.

It comes a week after head coach Rassie Erasmus was a handed a six-match suspension for comments made in a press conference after their defeat to France in Paris.

Erasmus, 54, questioned whether match officials were involved in "match-fixing" and pointed out numerous decisions he felt were incorrect. You can read more about that here.

The sport's governing body World Rugby acted swiftly and handed the double World Cup winner a ban - which the Springboks have requested a personal hearing for.

There had been suggestions that because English is not Erasmus' first language that his words did not come across as intended. The Springboks appear to have taken the step to allow Stick to speak in isiXhosa to avoid any further misunderstandings.

Stick, who speaks perfect English, has previously answered questions in isiXhosa from South African journalists.

According to the Irish Independent, IsiXhosa is the second most spoken home language in ‌South Africa after isiZulu.

SuperSport journalist Kuhle Sonkosi stepped in to translate Stick's comments about team selection.

“(Stick) used to coach me as an under-21 player and I had been begging him for an opportunity. I never got to play (for the Springboks), ‌so this is my chance to be selected as a translator,” Sonkosi said.

South Africa take on Les Bleus in London on Sunday, with Erasmus once again hosting a watch-along live stream for supporters while banned from attending matches.

title: All six Nations Championship final referees confirmed as controversial official appointed
article_text:
English referee Karl Dickson has been appointed to take charge of Sunday's Nations Championship final between France and South Africa.

It is an appointment that could bring plenty of scrutiny, given the controversy surrounding the Springboks and match officials during their last meeting with France.

Less than two weeks ago, France defeated South Africa in Paris, with Springboks head coach Rassie Erasmus subsequently handed a six-match ban for his post-match comments about the officiating.

Jasper Wiese also received a red card during the match and was given a four-game suspension.

Erasmus was forced to watch the Springboks' next game from his hotel room, where he streamed a live watchalong, as he served the first part of his suspension.

With the two sides now preparing to meet again, this time with silverware on the line, Dickson could find himself under considerable pressure.

The Englishman has already found himself at the centre of controversy involving South Africa this year, following his performance in the fourth Test of the Rugby's Greatest Rivalry tour against New Zealand.

Rome, Italy - 23.02.2025: Referee Karl Dickson seen in action during the Guinness Six Nations 2025 match between Italy and France at Olympic Stadium. PUBLICATIONxNOTxINxITA Copyright: xMarcoxIacobucci/IPAxSportx/xipa-agency.netx/xx IPA_54494215 IPA_A

Dickson came under fire from the All Blacks camp after the Springboks' 43-28 victory in Baltimore, which secured a 3-1 series triumph for South Africa.

Several decisions attracted criticism, particularly an incident involving Cam Roigard, who was penalised for offside after being challenged without the ball.

New Zealand assistant coach Neil Barnes also questioned two early scrum penalties against Codie Taylor for failing to maintain his brake foot.

Barnes argued that both teams had committed similar offences and suggested South Africa were getting “the rub of the green” on tight decisions.

However, he was also quick to acknowledge that the Springboks deserved their victory.

Despite the criticism, Dickson remains widely regarded as one of the leading referees in world rugby.

A former professional scrum-half, he brings an understanding of the game that helps him manage the breakdown, maintain the flow of matches and communicate calmly under pressure.

His appointment to such a high-profile fixture is another show of faith in his ability to officiate at the highest level.

Dickson will be assisted by Andrew Brace and James Doleman for the France versus South Africa final, with Andrew Jackson appointed as television match official (TMO) and Richard Kelly as foul play review officer (FPRO).

Elsewhere, Angus Gardner will referee England's clash with New Zealand, while Pierre Brousset takes charge of Scotland against Argentina.

Luke Pearce will officiate Wales versus Japan, Nika Amashukeli has been appointed for Ireland against Australia, and Nic Berry will referee Italy against Fiji.
