title: England squad to face New Zealand: Steve Borthwick names 37 players
article_text:
Steve Borthwick has named a 37-man England squad ahead of Saturday's Nations Championship Finals Weekend clash with New Zealand at Allianz Stadium, Twickenham.

England return to action on Saturday, 28 November, with kick-off scheduled for 4.40pm and live coverage on ITV1.

The squad has assembled at Pennyhill Park as preparations begin for another meeting with the All Blacks.

Saracens youngster Noah Caluori is included in the 37-man group, having missed the previous training squad.

There are also places for Fin Smith, Ollie Chessum, George Furbank and Seb Atkinson, giving Borthwick plenty of options ahead of his final selection.

Henry Pollock retains his place among the forwards, while George Ford, Marcus Smith and Fin Smith provide competition at fly-half.

England will be hoping to build on their recent 37-12 victory over New Zealand when the sides meet again at Twickenham.

Tickets remain available for Finals Weekend, with each day's ticket providing access to two international matches.

title: Jannik Sinner to reportedly undergo knee surgery, will miss second straight Grand Slam
article_text:
Former World No. 1 Jannik Sinner is set to undergo surgery this week for the right knee injury that ended his 2026 season, Sky Sport Italy reported Monday.

The recovery is expected to take three-to-four months, which will keep the five-time major champion out of the Australian Open. It will be Sinner's second consecutive Grand Slam absence. He withdrew from the US Open with the same injury.

That prevented Sinner from advancing to the US Open final for the third consecutive year. He won the tournament in 2024, defeating American Taylor Fritz. Last year, he finished as runner-up, losing to rival Carlos Alcaraz.

Sinner also withdrew from the Cincinnati Open in August due to his knee injury. With that event taking place so close to the US Open, his availability to play in Queens was put in doubt.

However, Sinner not playing in Cincinnati was viewed as a precautionary measure that would allow him an opportunity to recover and train for the US Open. But Sinner's knee turned out to need more treatment than originally anticipated.

Sinner, 25, won his second consecutive Wimbledon title approximately a month earlier, defeating Alexander Zverev in the final. But he didn't play in an event since that July 12 match.

The surgery will cap off a difficult year for Sinner. Though he did win Wimbledon, Sinner lost to Novak Djokovic in the Australian Open semifinals and was upset by Juan Manuel Cerundolo in the second round of the French Open while struggling with dehydration and cramping.

In a video posted to social media, Sinner told fans that he needed to think about his long-term career when he decided to end his 2026 season in October. At the time, he said he and his doctors had mapped out a course of treatment. Apparently, Sinner's right knee didn't respond to that regiment. Or surgery was always the eventual outcome.

"I will do everything possible to get back to 100 percent," Sinner said in the video. "I will thank you already in advance for your support and hope to see you very, very soon on court again. Ciao, Ciao."

At the Davis Cup Finals this week in Bologna, Italy, Italian team captain Filippo Volandri told reporters that he sent a message of support to Sinner.

"We wish him the best of luck because he's important not only for the Davis Cup, but for Italy and for everyone," Volandri said, via Sky Sport Italy. "Regardless of whether he's not here physically, he's here because he writes to us in our chat. We wish him the best of luck and are waiting for him with open arms."

title: French pair target Grand Slam glory after ATP Finals crown in Turin
article_text:
French tennis players Théo Arribagé and Albano Olivetti were on Monday setting their sights on playing in their country's Davis Cup team and trophies at the four Grand Slam tournaments next year after capturing the doubles title at the 2026 men's end-of-season championships.

Arribagé and Olivetti beat the fourth seeds Marcelo Arevalo and Mate Pavic 3-6, 7-6, 10-6 in Turin on Sunday night to claim their most prestigious prize since teaming up in October 2025.

"The main objectives for next season will be the French [Davis Cup] team and winning Grand Slams," Arribagé said.

"Following on from what we have done this year, we want to perform better but without setting ourselves limits," he added.

Arribagé, 26, and Olivetti, 34, went into the eight-team doubles event in Italy as the sixth seeds on the back of crowns in Auckland, Dallas, Montpellier, Halle, Mallorca and Basel as well as finals in Munich, Tokyo and Lyon.

On 15 November, they lost to Arevalo and Pavic in straight sets in the opening match of the round robin stage.

Two days later, they bounced back with a 6-4, 7-6 victory over the eighth seeds Orlando Luz and Rafael Matos. On 19 November, they upset the top seeds Henry Patten and Harri Heliovaara to advance to the semi-finals.

There, they squandered three match points and then saved three match points on their way to a 7-6, 6-7, 12-10 win over the seventh seeds Kevin Krawietz et Tim Pütz.

"After we won in Auckland I started to feel that we could really be a very solid pair," added Arribagé. "And I felt that we could achieve some great things if we worked hard.

"We're the pair that has won the most tournaments this year but we were missing that big title. With this trophy, there is no better way to end the season."

Arribagé and Olivetti are the third all-French pair after Fabrice Santoro and Michaël Llodra and Nicolas Mahut and Pierre-Hugues Herbert to win the doubles title at the end of season championships since it was set up in 1970.

In the singles event, Carlos Alcaraz capped his return from a five-month injury lay-off with a third consecutive title and a first ATP Finals trophy.

The Spaniard overwhelmed the top seed Alexander Zverev 6-2, 7-6 on Sunday night to join André Agassi, Roger Federer and Novak Djokovic as the only men to win at the four Grand Slam venues in Melbourne, Paris, London and New York as well as the end-of-year championships.

"This one is special," Alcaraz said. "This one means the world to me, to my team, to my family. They know how hard I've been chasing this moment and how hard I've been working to lift this trophy."

Alcaraz dispatched seventh seed Frances Tiafoe, fourth seed Daniil Medvedev and fifth seed Flavio Cobolli with dropping a set during the round robin stage.

He dropped the opening set to third seed Ben Shelton before recovering to win 3-6, 6-3, 7-6 in the semi-finals on Saturday.

Zverev, who won the end-of-season championhips in 2018 and 2021, was munificent in defeat.

"You're an absolute legend of our sport and you are only 23-years-old," said the 29-year-old German during the trophy presentation ceremony. "So if you retire tomorrow, it's okay. You can relax!"

title: Alcaraz gains ground on Sinner following Turin title, Mover of Week
article_text:
World No. 3 Carlos Alcaraz finished the 2026 ATP Tour season on a 14-match winning streak, claiming consecutive titles in Vienna, Paris and at the coveted Nitto ATP Finals, where he sealed his first triumph at the year-end event.

The Spaniard’s late-season surge has helped him close the gap on World No. 2 and rival Jannik Sinner.

For the final time this year, ATPTour.com looks at the movers of the week in the PIF ATP Rankings, as of Monday 23 November.

Alcaraz completed a perfect campaign in Turin on Sunday, finishing 5-0 for the week and defeating World No. 1 Alexander Zverev in the championship match.

Having begun the Nitto ATP Finals trailing World No. 2 Sinner by 1,850 PIF ATP Ranking points, Alcaraz is now only 350 points behind the Italian. The 30-time tour-level titlist Alcaraz holds 7,600 PIF ATP Rankings points.

Zverev claimed ATP Year-End No. 1 presented by PIF honours, receiving that trophy in Turin. After a runner-up finish at the Nitto ATP Finals, the German holds 10,350 PIF ATP Ranking points. He is 2,400 points ahead of World No. 2 Sinner.

Having reached the last four in Turin, Shelton consolidated his position at World No. 4. Competing at the Nitto ATP Finals for the second consecutive year, Shelton improved upon last year's 0-3 showing with a semi-final run. Shelton's only losses in Turin this year were to Zverev and Alcaraz. The US Open finalist earned 400 points last week.

Fils, 22, made his Nitto ATP Finals debut and became the first Frenchman to earn a match win at the event since Jo-Wilfried Tsonga in 2011. Fils moved up one place in the PIF ATP Rankings and is now at a career-high No. 6.

Following his 10th career ATP Challenger title, Seyboth Wild is back inside the Top 100. The 26-year-old Brazilian was crowned champion at the Montevideo Challenger on Sunday. He was one of seven Challenger champions last week, alongside Toby Samuel, Francesco Passaro, Yosuke Watanuki, Dylan Dietrich, Sebastian Gorzny and Oliver Tarvet.

title: Badminton: Rexy wants Pearly-Thinaah to carry mental growth into World Tour Finals
article_text:
PETALING JAYA: Skill wins you points, but keeping your emotions in check wins you titles.

And that is the positive change that national doubles coaching director Rexy Mainaky saw in national women’s doubles aces Pearly Tan-M. Thinaah as they reclaimed the Hong Kong Open crown on Sunday (Nov 22).

"They have learnt to focus on how to handled thing when they were not going well on court," said Rexy.

"They have learnt to stay motivated and help each other through those difficult moments."

The world No. 4 pair had to hold their nerve in the final at the Kai Tak Arena, saving a game point in the opener before beating Japan’s Sumire Nakade-Miyu Takahashi in straight games.

It was the closest they came to dropping a game all week as they reclaimed the crown they first won in 2024.

Pearly-Thinaah have had their share of setbacks and comebacks over the years.

They won the 2022 French Open less than two months after Pearly injured her hamstring.

A back injury sidelined Pearly again in April this year, but the pair have since won the Denmark and Hong Kong Opens.

These victories took their tally to three titles this year, following their Indonesia Masters win in January.

And Rexy hoped they would continue to show improvement when they get ready for the season-ending World Tour Finals in Hangzhou from Dec 9-13.

Pearly-Thinaah will aim to better last year’s run to the semi-finals, their best showing at the tournament.

"They have plenty of experience in these situations," said Rexy.

"My advice is to stay focused and learn from the way they played to win the Denmark and Hong Kong Opens," said Rexy.

Pearly acknowledged that they have learnt to stay composed when things went against them during a heart-to-heart after their first round exit at the Japan Masters.

Staying calm also helped Pearly vary her attack in Hong Kong, bringing out the trick shots she learnt as a junior from her father and first coach, Tan Seng Hoe.

"My father taught me those skills when I was young," said Pearly.

"I can use them effectively when I remain calm, but sometimes, when I become too eager to win, I tend to forget about them."

title: How Lakshya Sen turned a faltering season into a World Tour Finals comeback
article_text:
Written off after a string of early defeats, Lakshya Sen won 13 straight matches in November, picked up two Super 500 titles and booked his first World Tour Finals berth in five years.

Lakshya Sen lost the opening game of the Kumamoto Masters Japan final 13-21 to Koki Watanabe, a home favourite who had already beaten him twice this year.

Sixty-four minutes later, he had turned it around, winning 13-21, 21-18, 21-14 to become the first Indian to lift the title since the tournament was introduced in 2023. It was his second Super 500 crown in a fortnight.

A month earlier, such a run would have seemed improbable.

Lakshya had entered the final stretch of the season on the back of first-round exits at the China Masters and Denmark Open, a second-round exit at the Asian Games and an upset defeat at the home World Championships.

The question then was not whether he could win titles, but whether he could string together wins.

The year had promised much more. At the All England Open in March, Lakshya beat top seed and defending champion Shi Yu Qi 23-21, 19-21, 21-18 in the first round, ending a five-match losing streak against the Chinese shuttler.

He then survived a four-match-point deficit against Ng Ka Long Angus to win 21-19, 21-23, 21-10, beat Li Shi Feng 21-13, 21-16 in the quarter-finals and defeated Canada's Victor Lai to reach his second All England final.

Lin Chun-Yi beat him 15-21, 20-22 in the title match, extending his losing streak against the Taiwanese shuttler to five.

By late May, Lakshya had returned to the world top 10 for the first time in more than 440 days.

Lakshya injured his elbow in the opening game of India's Thomas Cup quarter-final against Chou Tien-chen, although he went on to win 18-21, 22-20, 21-17 as India secured bronze.

Defeats to Watanabe followed at the Singapore Open and Japan Open.

At the World Championships in New Delhi in August, he won the opening game 21-19 against world No. 92 Garret Tan, an 18-year-old American, before losing in three games.

Victor Lai, whom he had beaten in the All England semi-finals, knocked him out of the China Masters in straight games. At the Asian Games, Lakshya led Loh Kean Yew 5-1 in the opening game before losing 12-21, 21-15, 14-21 in the second round.

Chou then beat him 18-21, 21-13, 15-21 in the opening round of the Denmark Open.

Lakshya arrived at the Hylo Open in Saarbrucken as the seventh seed.

He dropped the opening game against Finland's Kalle Koljonen in the quarter-finals before rallying to win 14-21, 21-17, 21-13. He then beat world No. 14 Toma Junior Popov 21-17, 21-13 in the semi-finals.

In the final, he faced fourth seed and defending champion Jonatan Christie, who held a 4-3 lead in their head-to-head record. Lakshya won 21-17, 21-10 in 39 minutes to level the record and claim his first title since the Australian Open in November 2025.

It was his second Hylo Open title, following his 2019 triumph, and came on the same day PV Sindhu won the women's singles. "Approach remains the same," Lakshya said afterwards, crediting his family, coaches and support team.

Seeded eighth in Kumamoto, Lakshya recovered from 12-16 down in the opening game against Chi Yu Jen to win his first-round match before beating China's Dong Tianyao to reach the quarter-finals.

There, he defeated Yushi Tanaka, his opponent in last year's Australian Open final, 21-16, 21-15.

The semi-final against Indonesia's world No. 10 Alwi Farhan went the distance. Lakshya took the opening game 21-12 but lost the second 15-21 after Farhan opened up an 11-4 lead at the interval. He then closed out the decider 21-11 in 70 minutes.

A year earlier, his Kumamoto campaign had ended in the semi-finals against Kenta Nishimoto.

The final against Watanabe carried added significance in the race for the World Tour Finals.

Lakshya was 10th in the Race to Finals before the tournament. The title, worth 9,200 points, lifted him to sixth and brought him within touching distance of qualification for Hangzhou.

The Hong Kong Open was the final tournament in the qualifying window.

Lakshya needed a semi-final finish to secure his place, but the equation eased on the opening day when Kidambi Srikanth beat Watanabe in the first round.

Lakshya entered the week with 74,180 points, compared to Watanabe's 73,620.

After beating home player Lee Cheuk Yiu in the opening round, he defeated Denmark's Rasmus Gemke 21-11, 21-18 and then eighth seed Loh 21-17, 10-21, 21-13 in the quarter-finals, avenging his Asian Games defeat.

It was his 13th consecutive win across three tournaments.

The streak ended in the semi-finals against third seed Anders Antonsen, who beat him 13-21, 13-21.

Antonsen went on to win the title by walkover after Kunlavut Vitidsarn withdrew from the final with a back injury.

The clearest difference has been Lakshya's ability to navigate close matches.

Through the middle of the year, he lost deciding games to Tan, Loh and Chou. In November, he came from a game down against Koljonen and Watanabe, while also winning three-game matches against Farhan and Loh.

His long-time mentor Vimal Kumar credited the coaching team's planning after Kumamoto, writing on X that the win over Watanabe brought back "memories of the brilliance he displayed in 2021-22".

That period saw Lakshya reach a career-high world No. 6 in November 2022. He currently sits at No. 11.

title: Marco Penge claims maiden PGA Tour win: Englishman triumphs from four-way playoff at RSM Classic
article_text:
English golfer Marco Penge claimed a stunning maiden win on the PGA Tour as he emerged victorious from a four-way playoff at the season-ending RSM Classic.

Penge, a three-time winner on the DP World Tour, had gone into the tournament at risk of losing his PGA Tour card for next year after a rookie season disrupted by a viral illness placed him outside of the top 100.

With a top-four finish required to retain his spot, the 28-year-old found form at the best possible time at the Sea Island Golf Club this week, and a final-round 65 earned him a spot alongside Haotong Li of China and Americans Michael Thorbjornsen and Max Greyserman in a playoff decider - all four locked at 16 under.

Penge's five-under 65 on the Seaside Course included six birdies, including one at the last, and a single bogey, while he birdied 18 again to clinch victory in the playoff after nailing his approach to 10 feet.

"I always seem to play my best golf when my back's up against the wall," Penge said following his stunning win.

"I've been through this before on the DP World Tour, keeping my card in the last event and dealing with adversity and coming back from health issues, all that stuff.

"So I knew I could do it, I just wasn't sure I ever had the game this week to be able to do it and thankfully I did."

Rasmus Hojgaard, who had held a share of the lead - on 13 under with Thorbjornsen - heading into the weather-delayed final round on Monday, ultimately finish tied fifth.

The Ryder Cup star posted a disappointing final round of 69 to end two shots off the pace on 14 under, level with Jackson Koivun.

Fellow Americans Harris English, Nick Dunlap and five-time major winner Brooks Koepka finished tied-seventh, ninth and tied-10th, respectively.

Denmark's Rasmus Neergaard-Petersen also finished in the top 10.

title: History was within Nelly Korda’s grasp. 5 rounds kept her from grabbing it
article_text:
When the ink is dry on the obituary for Nelly Korda’s 2026 season, the top line will be about her blistering start, her mindset shift after a winless 2025 and her two major victories, including a dramatic U.S. Women’s Open win at Riviera.

Korda was fantastic to start the season. She set the golf world on fire and embraced her role as the main character in growing the sport. She achieved a lifelong dream by becoming a U.S. Women’s Open champion, won her second Chevron Championship and put herself one point away from reaching the LPGA Hall of Fame.

It was a historic season for Korda. But it was one that ended on Sunday with a third-place finish at the CME Group Tour Championship and Korda still being one point shy of etching her name into LPGA immortality. Despite fighting a two-way miss this week at Tiburon Golf Club, Korda put herself in position to win on Sunday and open history’s gates. She has said that she only focuses on the next shot. That she is driven by a love of competition and not the big-picture rewards that come her way when she plays “Nelly Golf.” But Korda admitted on Saturday in Naples that she has at times battled with blocking out the noise. She hears it and knows what’s at stake. At times, she has let that impact her game. But she knows what will bring her to her ultimate goal is her ability to keep what lies on the horizon from affecting how she does business.

“I would say that like obviously I’ve struggled with it, too,” Korda said on Saturday. “I understand everyone wants a story, but for me, I just love the game. Sometimes I struggle with it where I like listen to the outside, and I put a little bit more pressure on myself, but I feel like I’ve learned. I’ve had the same team through the majority of my career, pretty much my entire career, where they know how to pull me out of, you know — pull my head out of my ass, pretty much.

“I’m so grateful for them because we’re all human beings, right? We all kind of make mistakes. We all want to be perfect but we’re not. So tomorrow I’m just going to go [out] and have fun.”

title: What's new on the 2027 Race to Dubai?
article_text:
There will be a feel of all new but also familiar as we head through the Race to Dubai in 2027.

There are three events on the schedule that did not feature in 2026 as the historic national opens of Singapore, Portugal and Hong Kong return, all bringing returning venues with them.

Of the six venues that are new for 2027, we will be visiting two for the very first time, while as always, we will welcome a host of new stars to golf's global Tour.

Here, we take a look at a few of the events, venues and players to keep an eye out for in 2027.

While the three events added may not be new, far from it in some cases, they make a very welcome return across the Asian Swing, European Swing and Back 9.

Straight after the year's first Major Championship at the Masters Tournament we head to Sentosa Golf Club for the Deutsche Bank Singapore Open.

While the DP World Tour has been a regular visitor to Singapore since the early 90s and was there as recently as 2025, the Singapore Open has not been part of the schedule since 2012, when Matteo Manassero lifted the trophy.

Ian Poulter, three-time champion Adam Scott and Gonzalo Fernandez-Castaño also won the event on the DP World Tour, joining a roll of honour that includes Major champions Sergio Garcia and Shaun Micheel.

The European Swing then brings the return of the Open de Portugal | Cascais Lisboa for the first time since Garrick Higgo lifted the trophy in 2020.

The event was on the schedule every season barring two from 1973 to 2010 and had a list of winners including Sam Torrance, Colin Montgomerie, Miguel Ángel Jiménez, Thomas Bjørn and notably Pablo Martin as an amateur in 2007.

It returned in 2017 when Matt Wallace took the title and has since been a regular feature on the HotelPlanner Tour.

Our third returnee is one of the most storied events in golf as we head back east for the Hong Kong Open.

One of Asia’s most historic tournaments, it returns to the DP World Tour’s schedule for the first time since the 2019 season.

Established in 1959, the event was co-sanctioned by the DP World Tour and Asian Tour 18 times in total after first featuring on the DP World Tour’s schedule in 2002 and was last won as a DP World Tour event by Aaron Rai.

He is the fifth Major winner to lift the trophy in the DP World Tour era along with José María Olazábal, Pádraig Harrington, Rory McIlroy and Justin Rose and they join the likes of four-time winner Jiménez, Montgomerie and Poulter on the roll of honour.

Our return to Singapore also sees us back at Sentosa Golf Club, home of the four previous DP World Tour editions of the Singapore Open.

Designed by Ron Fream and opened in 1982, The Serapong Course sits on Sentosa Island and having undergone renovations, will present a different test to our last visit 14 years ago.

The Estrella Damm Catalunya Championship then brings a brand new venue as Empordà Golf hosts the second edition of the Spanish event.

A three-time venue on the HotelPlanner Tour across 2021 and 2022, Empordà's Dunes Course designed by Robert von Hagge has been evolving since its inception in 1989 and will provide a links-style test just back from the coast.

A returning venue is Oitavos Dunes Links Golf which will host the Open de Portugal on the DP World Tour for the fifth time the following week.

Opened in 2001, the Arthur Hills designed layout plays along the Atlantic coast and its links style produced wins for Paul Broadhurst in 2005, Pablo Martin in 2007, Grégory Bourdy in 2008 and Michael Hoey in 2009.

The next week we have our second entirely new venue of the season as PGA Frisco plays host to the year's second Major, the US PGA Championship.

Only opened in 2023 and designed by the renowned Gil Hanse, the rugged Fields Ranch East layout is set to host a number of PGA of America Championships over the coming years, with the body having its headquarters onsite.

From a brand new venue to a returning classic as Kennemer Golf and Country Club hosts the KLM Open for the first time since 2015.

In its current location since 1927, Kennemer's 18 holes used for the KLM Open are made up of holes from three separate nine-hole courses with some designed by Harry Colt and others by Frank Pennink.

Its 22 editions so far, 12 on the DP World Tour, have seen Seve Ballesteros claim his maiden victory and wins for the likes of Bobby Locke, Flory Van Docke, José María Olazábal, Darren Clarke and home hero Joost Luiten.

Towards the end of the Back 9 we then head east again to Hong Kong Golf Club and one of the most prestigious venues in Asian golf.

The event has been staged at the club ever since its inaugural edition in 1959 and is now played over a composite of the New and Eden courses.

The club can trace its history back to 1889 and has been in Fanling since 1911 when the Old Course opened, with the New (1931) and Eden (1969) following after.

The pathways to the DP World Tour always provide us with a plethora of new talent and 2027 will be no different as HotelPlanner Tour graduates, Qualifying School graduates and players from our partner tours around the world get their first taste of full-time membership.

title: DP World Tour hands out another shock invite
article_text:
YouTube golf star Peter Finch has been offered a surprise chance to make his DP World Tour debut next month.

Finch, who boasts over 850,000 subscribers, has announced he has accepted a sponsor’s invite into the AfrAsia Bank Mauritius Open.

The England-based content creator is currently undergoing a challenge to break into the top 1,000 in the Official World Golf Rankings, but has never before been handed an opportunity of this magnitude.

“I’m thrilled to share that I will be teeing it up at the AfrAsia Bank Mauritius Open on the DP World Tour,” Finch wrote on Instagram.

“I cannot wait to get out to Mauritius and compete against some of the best players in the world!”

Last year, Finch made the cut and tied for 50th at the Egyptian Open, an Asian Development Tour event, which boosted his ranking.

He has also made Final Qualifying for The Open, as well as finishing T6 at the Fairmont St Andrews Classic on the Tartan Pro Tour earlier this year. But this is a level above, with the $1.5 million event headlined by two-time Masters champion Bubba Watson.

Multiple DP World Tour winners Casey Jarvis, Branden Grace, Thriston Lawrence and Dean Burmester are also set to tee it up in Mauritius.

Finch added: “I remember watching this tournament over the years and just thinking what an amazing spectacle and an amazing privilege it would be to play at these courses and that’s what we’re going to be doing.”

Finch confirmed he will be filming content at the 72-hole stroke play event, which begins on December 10.

title: Standard Chartered puts Play On centre stage to help more girls stay in sport
article_text:
- Liverpool FC Men and Women replaced Standard Chartereds front-of-shirt logo with Play On, putting the issue of girls dropping out of sport in front of millions of fans.

- All proceeds from this years Perfect Match campaign will go to LFC Foundation to support programmes helping girls stay in sport.

- Standard Chartered convened organisations across the sporting ecosystem in Anfield, including UN Women, LFC and LFC Foundation, to help drive greater collective action on this issue.

Standard Chartered and Liverpool Football Club (LFC) have once again put Play On centre stage, using one of the most visible sponsorship assets in world sport to focus attention on helping more girls stay in sport.

The Play On message replaced Standard Chartereds usual branding on the front of the players shirts, with the LFCs Womens team wearing the Play On logo against Chelsea WFC on 21 November, followed by the Mens team against Manchester United FC at Anfield on 22 November.

Ahead of both fixtures, a giant 25m x 23m Play On shirt was displayed on the pitch at St Helens and Anfield Stadiums, reinforcing the campaigns call to help girls stay in sport.

The limited-edition match shirts are now being signed and auctioned, with proceeds from this years campaign going to LFC Foundation, supporting programmes designed to break down barriers and help more girls participate in sport.

Standard Chartered also convened organisations and individuals working across sport, business and civil society at Anfield to discuss how greater collective action can help address the barriers girls face. Guests included representatives from UN Women, the International Working Group on Women and Sport, LFC and LFC Foundation.

This builds on Standard Chartereds longer-term ambition for Play On, connecting organisations with different capabilities, from funding and programme delivery to policy expertise, communications reach and access to communities, to explore how they can work together more effectively to keep girls in sport.

Erica Kerner, Global Head of Brand Partnerships and Sponsorships, Standard Chartered, said: Sport gives girls so much more than the opportunity to play. It can build confidence, resilience, teamwork and leadership skills that can open doors throughout their lives. Yet girls still drop out of sport at twice the rate of boys by the age of 14. Through Play On, were leveraging the power and reach of our partnership with LFC to shine a light on this issue, connecting brands and organisations to create more opportunities for girls to fulfil their potential on and beyond the pitch.

Kate Theobald, SVP of Global Partnerships at Liverpool FC, said: Our long-standing partnership with Standard Chartered has always been about more than football, and Play On is a great example of how we can work together to make a meaningful difference. Since launching the initiative in 2023, weve continued to build on its impact, using the clubs global reach and the strength of our partnership to raise awareness of the barriers girls face in sport and encourage positive change.

Were incredibly proud of what weve achieved together through Play On over the years, and particularly pleased that this years campaign will directly support LFC Foundation and its work to create more opportunities for girls to stay involved in sport. Its another important step in our shared commitment to making a lasting difference.

Play On was launched by Standard Chartered and LFC in 2023 to help more girls stay in sport and benefit from the skills, confidence and opportunities it can create throughout their lives.

The joint Standard Chartered and LFC Play On initiative aims to help girls stay in sport as it builds confidence, resilience, teamwork and leadership  skills that can lead to opportunities in education, employment and wider life.

Play On was launched in 2023 to support the Banks Lifting Participation Stand and ambitions. To-date, it has mainly been campaign-based, aiming to raise awareness of the following:

- Twice as many girls than boys drop out of sports by age 14.

- 94 per cent of women in C-suite roles played sport as girls.

- 74 per cent of executive women believe a background in sport can help accelerate a womans career.

Tactically, we teamed up with LFC Academy and Foundation coaches to deliver our bespoke Play On Train the Trainer programme through our community partners in Kenya and South Africa: 69 local coaches were upskilled through the training, who went on to train more than 10,500 girls over the following year.

We are a leading international banking group, with a presence in 55 of the worlds most dynamic markets. Our purpose is to drive commerce and prosperity through our unique diversity, and our heritage and values are expressed in our brand promise, here for good.

Standard Chartered PLC is listed on the London and Hong Kong stock exchanges.

title: Amex Stadium will host 2035 Women's World Cup matches
article_text:
Brighton's Amex Stadium could host matches at the 2035 Women's World Cup, after a successful bid from England, Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales.

The ground was among 19 venues listed as possible host stadiums at a FIFA meeting yesterday after football’s governing body gave its approval to the plans.

The 104-match tournament will be the first time a football World Cup has been held in the UK since 1966.

Brighton and Hove City Council previously expressed a desire to become one of the host cities for the tournament in late 2025, highlighting potential benefits including tourism and global media exposure.

The Amex, which can seat more than 32,000 supporters, previously played host to several matches at the 2022 Women's Euros, including two involving England.

Among the other English venues for the 2035 tournament are Wembley, Villa Park, Bristol's Ashton Gate and Newcastle's St James' Park.
